title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試録序
上御極於今十有一年為丙子凡
四舉鄉試矣
廟堂登崇之典材賢長育之機愈
盛以新而江西頻年兵盜項始
告靖然詩書禮樂之習視昔罔
渝挾策求試之士揚衡雲集益
有以見
===
國家道化之深土地風俗之厚固
有撓之而不濁者時監察御史
李〔潤〕被
命按治寔當監臨之任盖前此臺臣
嘗以是任之重宜付諸其人無
惟常資是襲遂請于
punctuated:
江西鄉試録序

上御極於今十有一年，為丙子，凡四舉鄉試矣。廟堂登崇之典，材賢長育之機，愈盛以新。而江西頻年兵盜項始告靖，然詩書禮樂之習，視昔罔渝。挾策求試之士，揚衡雲集，益有以見國家道化之深、土地風俗之厚，固有撓之而不濁者。

時監察御史李〔潤〕被命按治，寔當監臨之任。盖前此臺臣嘗以是任之重，宜付諸其人，無惟常資是襲，遂請于
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

It is now eleven years since His Majesty ascended the throne. This is the bingzi year [1516], and the Provincial Examination has been held four times. The court’s institutions for advancing and honoring worthy men, and its means of nurturing talent and virtue, have grown ever more flourishing and renewed. Jiangxi, however, has suffered warfare and banditry for successive years, and has only just been reported pacified [?]. Nevertheless, its traditions of poetry, documents, rites, and music remain unchanged from former times. Scholars carrying their books and seeking examination gather like clouds, “raising the crossbeam” [?]. This further demonstrates the depth of the dynasty’s moral influence and the strength of the region’s customs: here indeed is something that, though disturbed, does not become turbid.

At that time, Investigating Censor Li Run 李潤 received orders to conduct an inspection and duly assumed the duties of Supervising Official. Previously, a censor had observed that, given the importance of this responsibility, it should be entrusted to a suitable person, rather than assigned merely according to customary qualifications. He therefore submitted a petition to …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
上著為規行之自〔潤〕始云既至以試
院舊多𤰞浥命葺治之堂宇門
垣初就軒整士入試者舊不盈
二千頗病於狹乃與提學僉事
田〔汝耔〕議少增至二千五百有
奇而得以盡士之蘊藩司久燬
近者重建亦甫落成鹿鳴賓筵
===
于時燕集諸皆一新之會也時
又鎮守太監許〔滿〕巡撫右副都
御史孫〔燧〕既素先文教而尤加
意試事郎中吳〔山〕員外郎蔣〔愷〕
主事鄭〔玉〕黃〔希英〕方〔揩〕行人詹
〔昇〕劉〔璣〕皆以公事至及試而提
調則左布政使張〔嵿〕右參政陳
punctuated: 上，著為規，行之自〔潤〕始云。既至，以試院舊多𤰞浥，命葺治之，堂宇門垣初就軒整。士入試者舊不盈二千，頗病於狹，乃與提學僉事田〔汝耔〕議，少增至二千五百有奇，而得以盡士之蘊。藩司久燬，近者重建，亦甫落成，鹿鳴賓筵于時燕集，諸皆一新之會也。時又鎮守太監許〔滿〕、巡撫右副都御史孫〔燧〕既素先文教，而尤加意試事。郎中吳〔山〕、員外郎蔣〔愷〕、主事鄭〔玉〕、黃〔希英〕、方〔揩〕、行人詹〔昇〕、劉〔璣〕皆以公事至。及試而提調，則左布政使張〔嵿〕、右參政陳
translation_en:
…to the Emperor, and this was established as a regulation, its implementation beginning with Li Run. Upon arriving, he found that much of the examination compound had long been low-lying and damp, and ordered repairs. The halls, gates, and walls had just been made lofty and orderly. Previously, fewer than two thousand candidates had been admitted to sit the examination, and this restricted number was considered a considerable drawback. He therefore consulted with Tian Ruzi, the Education Intendant and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, and increased the number somewhat, to over two thousand five hundred, allowing the candidates full opportunity to display their abilities. The Provincial Administration Commission’s premises had long lain destroyed; recently rebuilt, they too had just been completed. The Deer’s Call banquet for the honored guests was held there at this time: it was an occasion on which everything had been renewed.

At this time, the Regional Defender, Grand Eunuch Xu Man, and the Grand Coordinator, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Sui, who had always given priority to literary education, devoted particular attention to the examination. Bureau Director Wu Shan, Vice Director Jiang Kai, Secretaries Zheng Yu, Huang Xiying, and Fang Kai [?], and Messengers Zhan Sheng and Liu Ji had all arrived on official business. When the examination took place, the Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zhang Ding and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Chen…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
洪謨監試則按察使張〔淵〕僉事
王〔疇〕若右布政使王〔啓〕左右叅
政方〔璘〕程〔杲〕副使馮〔纘〕許〔庭光〕
楊〔璋〕左右叅議羅〔中〕楊〔學禮〕僉
事李〔嘉言〕王〔崇仁〕師〔夔〕署都指
揮僉事郭〔宇〕許〔清〕皆協贊而防
範于外考試官則學正〔樺〕孫〔芝〕
同考試官則教諭丁〔裕〕季〔春〕楊
===
〔武〕方〔珩〕樊〔華〕蔡〔時〕張〔瀚〕費〔讓〕黎
〔貫〕訓導蘇〔子受〕皆膺聘時至自
鎻院至揭曉為日二十有一取
士之中式者九十有五蓋自監
臨以下及于百執事皆取必於
大公至愼罔敢易也事竣錄其
punctuated:
洪謨，監試則按察使張〔淵〕、僉事王〔疇〕。若右布政使王〔啓〕、左右叅政方〔璘〕、程〔杲〕、副使馮〔纘〕、許〔庭光〕、楊〔璋〕、左右叅議羅〔中〕、楊〔學禮〕、僉事李〔嘉言〕、王〔崇仁〕、師〔夔〕、署都指揮僉事郭〔宇〕、許〔清〕，皆協贊而防範于外。考試官則學正〔樺〕、孫〔芝〕，同考試官則教諭丁〔裕〕、季〔春〕、楊〔武〕、方〔珩〕、樊〔華〕、蔡〔時〕、張〔瀚〕、費〔讓〕、黎〔貫〕、訓導蘇〔子受〕，皆膺聘時至。
自鎻院至揭曉，為日二十有一，取士之中式者九十有五。蓋自監臨以下，及于百執事，皆取必於大公至愼，罔敢易也。事竣，錄其
translation_en:
… Hongmo. Overseeing the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Yuan and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Chou. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Wang Qi; Left and Right Administration Vice Commissioners Fang Lin and Cheng Gao; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Feng Zuan, Xu Tingguang, and Yang Zhang; Left and Right Administration Assistant Commissioners Luo Zhong and Yang Xueli; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Li Jiayan, Wang Chongren, and Shi Kui; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Guo Yu and Xu Qing all assisted and maintained safeguards outside the examination compound. The Examiners were the instructors Hua [surname missing?] and Sun Zhi. The Associate Examiners were Instructors Ding Yu, Ji Chun, Yang Wu, Fang Heng, Fan Hua, Cai Shi, Zhang Han, Fei Rang, and Li Guan, and Assistant Instructor Su Zishou. All accepted their invitations and arrived on time.
From the sealing of the examination compound to the announcement of the results, twenty-one days elapsed. Ninety-five candidates passed. From the Supervising Official down to all those carrying out duties, everyone insisted upon the utmost impartiality and care; none dared treat the matter lightly. When the work was completed, we recorded their …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
姓氏及文之可式者以獻于
上〔燁〕謹首言曰士之始進有履端於
始之義君子重焉
國家用天下士圖惟治理豫養以
學校而后以科目進之崇階膴
秩惟才與德是與待士之禮既
優且渥矣今諸士子行即試南
===
宮臚
大對以服官序喜遭遇之及時而
展布之有地其亦思所以自立
以報稱于
上者哉吾嘗慨夫世之士飭於始而
終或違妍於外而內或爽矜持
於時之暇裕而或不能不移於
punctuated:
姓氏及文之可式者，以獻于上。〔燁〕謹首言曰：士之始進，有履端於始之義，君子重焉。
國家用天下士，圖惟治理，豫養以學校，而后以科目進之。崇階膴秩，惟才與德是與。待士之禮，既優且渥矣。今諸士子行即試南宮，臚大對，以服官序，喜遭遇之及時，而展布之有地，其亦思所以自立，以報稱于上者哉！吾嘗慨夫世之士，飭於始而終或違，妍於外而內或爽，矜持於時之暇裕，而或不能不移於
translation_en:
…their names and those writings that could serve as models, to present to His Majesty. Ye 〔燁〕 respectfully offers these opening words: When scholars first enter official life, their beginning carries the significance of setting the course correctly at the outset; the gentleman attaches great importance to this.
The state employs scholars from throughout the realm with good government as its aim. It nurtures them beforehand in schools and then advances them through the examinations. Lofty ranks and generous emoluments are granted solely on the basis of ability and virtue. The courtesy with which it treats scholars is both gracious and bountiful. Now these candidates will soon sit the Metropolitan Examination at the Ministry of Rites and be presented for the great response at the Palace Examination [?], thereafter taking their places in official service. Rejoicing that their opportunity has come at the proper time and that they have a sphere in which to exercise their abilities, should they not also consider how to establish themselves so as to repay His Majesty’s favor worthily? I have often lamented that scholars of this world are scrupulous at the beginning but may depart from their principles in the end; that they are admirable outwardly but may be otherwise within; and that they maintain their composure in times of leisure and ease, yet may be unable to remain steadfast when…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
事變之少殷若是者非見之未
瑩則守之有遺力焉耳用士之
意豈其然歟傳曰臣共而不二
禮之善物也夫惟不二然後恒
且實而安焉恒則始終罔有間
也實則外內罔背而馳也安則
合常變而一之也貫始終之謂
===
毅齊外內之謂純合常變之謂
貞毅可以立功矣純可以立言
矣貞可以立德矣士而至是也
士之職分盡而為臣之能事畢
矣
國家正大光明之業輔翊之於無
疆而報禮至矣科目藉以光重
punctuated: 事變之少殷。若是者，非見之未瑩，則守之有遺力焉耳。用士之意，豈其然歟？傳曰：「臣共而不二，禮之善物也。」夫惟不二，然後恒且實而安焉。恒則始終罔有間也，實則外內罔背而馳也，安則合常變而一之也。貫始終之謂毅，齊外內之謂純，合常變之謂貞。毅可以立功矣，純可以立言矣，貞可以立德矣。士而至是也，士之職分盡，而為臣之能事畢矣。國家正大光明之業，輔翊之於無疆，而報禮至矣。科目藉以光重
translation_en: …when affairs become somewhat more pressing. Those who behave thus either lack clarity of understanding or fail to exert their full strength in holding fast to their principles. Could this be the intention behind employing scholars? The Commentary says: “For a minister to be reverent and undivided in loyalty is an excellent embodiment of ritual propriety.” Only with undivided loyalty can one become constant, sincere, and settled in these qualities. Constancy means that no break occurs between beginning and end; sincerity means that outward conduct and inner disposition never run in opposite directions; being settled means unifying one’s conduct in ordinary and changing circumstances. Consistency from beginning to end is called resolve; harmony between the outward and inward is called purity; unity in ordinary and changing circumstances is called steadfastness. Resolve enables one to establish achievements; purity enables one to leave enduring words; steadfastness enables one to establish virtue. When a scholar reaches this point, he has fulfilled his proper duties as a scholar and accomplished all that service as a minister requires. He assists the state’s upright and illustrious undertaking without limit, and his repayment of its gracious treatment reaches its fullest measure. The examination system thereby gains lustre and prestige…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而燁輩掄校之明可少居矣此
固諸士子所素講者然禮始冠
也賓有辭焉出而見諸鄉大夫
先生有辭焉祝而望之也諸士
子始進與其事適相類燁輩一
日之勞雖未敢自謂為知己然
祝望之私用是以斯言先入之
===
倘遂以為主焉則豈直不負知
己而已哉
山西平陽府絳州儒學學正顔
燁謹序
punctuated:
而燁輩掄校之明可少居矣。此固諸士子所素講者，然禮始冠也，賓有辭焉；出而見諸鄉大夫先生，有辭焉，祝而望之也。諸士子始進，與其事適相類。燁輩一日之勞，雖未敢自謂為知己，然祝望之私，用是以斯言先入之。倘遂以為主焉，則豈直不負知己而已哉！
山西平陽府絳州儒學學正顔燁謹序。
translation_en:
…and we, Ye and his colleagues, may claim some small credit for discernment in selecting and evaluating them. These are, of course, matters that you scholars have long discussed. Yet when a young man first undergoes the capping ceremony, the guest delivers an address; when he goes out to visit the local dignitaries and elders, they too have words for him, expressing blessings and hopes. Your first advancement, scholars, is closely analogous to that occasion. Although our brief labor does not embolden us to call ourselves those who truly recognize your worth, our personal hopes and good wishes prompt us to place these words before you at the outset. If you then take them as your guiding principle, will you merely have lived up to the expectations of those who recognize your worth?
Respectfully prefaced by Yan Ye, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
正德十一年江西鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史李　潤〔子雨濟州衛籍山西蒲州人辛未進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使張　嵿〔時峻浙江蕭山縣人丁未進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司右參政陳洪謨〔宗禹湖廣武陵縣人丙辰進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司按察使張　瀾〔道夫河南洛陽縣人壬戌進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司僉事王　疇〔叙之湖廣崇陽縣人戊辰進士〕
===
考試官
山西平陽府絳州儒學學正顏　燁〔文華浙江上虞縣人丁卯貢士〕
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正孫　芝〔子秀直隸當塗縣人丁卯貢士〕
同考試官
湖廣常德府武陵縣儒學教諭丁　裕〔叔容福建莆田縣人甲子貢士〕
河南汝寧府汝陽縣儒學教諭季　泰〔定夫直隸無錫縣人甲子貢士〕
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭楊　武〔靖夫直隸嘉定縣人甲子貢士〕
廣東韶州府曲江縣儒學教諭方　珩〔純禮福建莆田縣人辛酉貢士〕
陝西西安府鄠縣儒學教諭樊　華〔中實四川長壽縣人丁卯貢士〕
punctuated:
正德十一年江西鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按江西監察御史李　潤〔子雨，濟州衛籍，山西蒲州人，辛未進士〕。

提調官：
江西等處承宣布政使司左布政使張　嵿〔時峻，浙江蕭山縣人，丁未進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司右參政陳洪謨〔宗禹，湖廣武陵縣人，丙辰進士〕。

監試官：
江西等處提刑按察司按察使張　瀾〔道夫，河南洛陽縣人，壬戌進士〕。
江西等處提刑按察司僉事王　疇〔叙之，湖廣崇陽縣人，戊辰進士〕。

考試官：
山西平陽府絳州儒學學正顏　燁〔文華，浙江上虞縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正孫　芝〔子秀，直隸當塗縣人，丁卯貢士〕。

同考試官：
湖廣常德府武陵縣儒學教諭丁　裕〔叔容，福建莆田縣人，甲子貢士〕。
河南汝寧府汝陽縣儒學教諭季　泰〔定夫，直隸無錫縣人，甲子貢士〕。
浙江紹興府蕭山縣儒學教諭楊　武〔靖夫，直隸嘉定縣人，甲子貢士〕。
廣東韶州府曲江縣儒學教諭方　珩〔純禮，福建莆田縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
陝西西安府鄠縣儒學教諭樊　華〔中實，四川長壽縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
translation_en:
Jiangxi Provincial Examination, eleventh year of Zhengde (1516).

Supervising Official:
Li Run, Regional Inspector of Jiangxi serving as an Investigating Censor. His courtesy name was Ziyu; he was registered with the Jizhou Guard and was a native of Puzhou, Shanxi. He was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the xinwei year.

Proctors:
Zhang Ding, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Shijun; he was a native of Xiaoshan County, Zhejiang, and a metropolitan graduate of the dingwei year.
Chen Hongmo, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration Commission. His courtesy name was Zongyu; he was a native of Wuling County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the bingchen year.

Examination Overseers:
Zhang Lan, Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Daofu; he was a native of Luoyang County, Henan, and a metropolitan graduate of the renxu year.
Wang Chou, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiangxi Provincial Surveillance Commission. His courtesy name was Xuzhi; he was a native of Chongyang County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuchen year.

Examiners:
Yan Ye, Instructor at the Confucian school of Jiangzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. His courtesy name was Wenhua; he was a native of Shangyu County, Zhejiang, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingmao year.
Sun Zhi, Instructor at the Confucian school of Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. His courtesy name was Zixiu; he was a native of Dangtu County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingmao year.

Associate Examiners:
Ding Yu, Instructor at the Confucian school of Wuling County, Changde Prefecture, Huguang. His courtesy name was Shurong; he was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year.
Ji Tai, Instructor at the Confucian school of Ruyang County, Runing Prefecture, Henan. His courtesy name was Dingfu; he was a native of Wuxi County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year.
Yang Wu, Instructor at the Confucian school of Xiaoshan County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. His courtesy name was Jingfu; he was a native of Jiading County, Zhili, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year.
Fang Heng, Instructor at the Confucian school of Qujiang County, Shaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong. His courtesy name was Chunli; he was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the xinyou year.
Fan Hua, Instructor at the Confucian school of Hu County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. His courtesy name was Zhongshi; he was a native of Changshou County, Sichuan, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the dingmao year.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
浙江處州府松陽縣儒學教諭蔡時〔中道四川巴縣人　庚午貢士〕
直隸常州府靖江縣儒學教諭張瀚〔孔量福建候官縣人　辛酉貢士〕

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知止而后有定定而后能靜靜而后能安
安而后能慮慮而后能得
士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
矣
無爲其所不爲無欲其所不欲如此而已
易
顯比之吉位正中也
===
君子以申命行事
以言乎邇則靜而正
其道甚大百物不廢懼以終始其要旡咎
書
愼厥身修思永
先王肇修人紀從諫弗咈先民時若居上
克明爲下克忠與人不求備檢身若不
及以至于有萬邦玆惟艱哉敷求哲人
俾輔于爾後嗣
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
知止而后有定，定而后能靜，靜而后能安，安而后能慮，慮而后能得。
士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠矣。
無爲其所不爲，無欲其所不欲，如此而已。

易
顯比之吉，位正中也。
君子以申命行事。
以言乎邇，則靜而正。
其道甚大，百物不廢，懼以終始，其要旡咎。

書
愼厥身修，思永。
先王肇修人紀，從諫弗咈，先民時若。居上克明，爲下克忠，與人不求備，檢身若不及，以至于有萬邦。玆惟艱哉！敷求哲人，俾輔于爾後嗣。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
Knowing where to rest, one can become settled; being settled, one can become tranquil; being tranquil, one can become at ease; being at ease, one can deliberate; through deliberation, one can attain the goal.
A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute: his burden is heavy and his road is long.
Do not do what you would not do; do not desire what you would not desire. That is all.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
The good fortune of manifest union comes from occupying a correct and central position.
The gentleman accordingly reiterates his commands and carries out his affairs.
Speaking of what is near, it is still and correct.
Its Way is exceedingly great, leaving none of the myriad things out. With apprehensive care from beginning to end, its essential aim is freedom from blame.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
Be mindful of your own cultivation, and think for the long term.
The former king first established the ordering of human relationships. He followed remonstrance without resisting it and took the ancients as his models. In a superior position he could be discerning; in a subordinate position he could be loyal. In dealing with others he did not demand perfection; in examining himself he acted as though he had not done enough. Thus he came to possess the myriad states. How difficult this was! Seek widely for wise men, so that they may assist your descendants.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
水曰潤下火曰炎上木曰曲直金曰從革
土爰稼穡
政貴有恒辭尚體要
詩
龍盾之合鋈以觼軜
彼爾維何維常之華彼路斯何君子之車
戎車既駕四牡業業豈敢定居一月三
捷駕彼四牡四牡騤騤君子所依小人
所腓四牡翼翼象弭魚服豈不日戒玁
狁孔棘
===
顒顒卬卬如圭如璋令聞令望
宣哲維人文武維后燕及皇天克昌厥後
春秋
衛師入郕〔隱公五年〕齊師宋師曹師城邢
〔僖公元年〕
晉人宋人衛人曹人伐鄭〔宣公十年〕
宋師伐陳衛人救陳〔宣公十二年〕
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵〔隱公元年〕
punctuated:
水曰潤下，火曰炎上，木曰曲直，金曰從革，土爰稼穡。
政貴有恒，辭尚體要。

詩
龍盾之合，鋈以觼軜。
彼爾維何？維常之華。彼路斯何？君子之車。戎車既駕，四牡業業。豈敢定居？一月三捷。駕彼四牡，四牡騤騤。君子所依，小人所腓。四牡翼翼，象弭魚服。豈不日戒？玁狁孔棘。
顒顒卬卬，如圭如璋。令聞令望。
宣哲維人，文武維后。燕及皇天，克昌厥後。

春秋
衛師入郕。〔隱公五年〕齊師、宋師、曹師城邢。〔僖公元年〕
晉人、宋人、衛人、曹人伐鄭。〔宣公十年〕
宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔宣公十二年〕
天王使宰咺來歸惠公仲子之賵。〔隱公元年〕
translation_en:
Water moistens and descends; fire burns and ascends; wood bends and straightens; metal yields and changes form; earth permits sowing and reaping.
In government, constancy is prized; in speech, substance and essentials are esteemed.

Odes
The dragon-emblazoned shields are paired; white-metal-plated buckled rings secure the inner reins.
What is that luxuriant growth? The blossoms of the cherry tree. What great carriage is that? The commander's chariot. The war chariot is harnessed, its four stallions mighty. How dare we remain at rest? In one month, three victories. We harness those four stallions, the four stallions strong and vigorous. The commander rides upon the chariot; the common soldiers take cover behind it. The four stallions move in order; there are ivory bow tips and fish-skin quivers. How could we fail to keep watch daily? The Xianyun menace is most urgent.
Solemn and lofty, like a jade gui tablet, like a jade zhang tablet: fine in reputation, fine in bearing.
Discerning and wise are his men; accomplished in civil and military affairs is their lord. His peace reaches august Heaven, and he can bring prosperity to his descendants.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The army of Wei entered Cheng. 〔Fifth year of Duke Yin.〕 The armies of Qi, Song, and Cao built walls around Xing. 〔First year of Duke Xi.〕
Men of Jin, Song, Wei, and Cao attacked Zheng. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
The army of Song attacked Chen; men of Wei came to Chen's aid. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕
The Heavenly King sent the Steward Xuan to come and present funeral gifts for Duke Hui and Zhongzi. 〔First year of Duke Yin.〕

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕公會王人齊侯
宋公衛侯許男曹伯陳世子欵盟于洮
〔僖公八年〕公會宰周公齊侯宋子衛侯鄭
伯許男曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕會王人晉
人宋人齊人陳人蔡人秦人盟于翟泉
〔僖公二十九年〕公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯
小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕尹氏立王子
朝〔昭公二十三年〕
===
禮記
凡官民材必先論之論辨然後使之任事
然後爵之位定然後祿之
居子與臣之節所以尊君親親也
清廟之瑟朱絃而疏越壹倡而三歎有遺
音者矣
君子也者人之成名也百姓歸之名謂之
君子之子是使其親爲君子也是爲成
其親之名也已
punctuated:
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕。公會王人、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、許男、曹伯、陳世子欵盟于洮〔僖公八年〕。公會宰周公、齊侯、宋子、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯于葵丘〔僖公九年〕。會王人、晉人、宋人、齊人、陳人、蔡人、秦人盟于翟泉〔僖公二十九年〕。公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。尹氏立王子朝〔昭公二十三年〕。

禮記

凡官民材，必先論之，論辨然後使之，任事然後爵之，位定然後祿之。

居子與臣之節，所以尊君親親也。

清廟之瑟，朱絃而疏越，壹倡而三歎，有遺音者矣。

君子也者，人之成名也。百姓歸之名，謂之君子之子，是使其親爲君子也，是爲成其親之名也已。
translation_en:
The royal officer Zitu came to the aid of Wei. 〔Sixth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 The Duke of Lu met with a royal officer, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, and Kuan, heir apparent of Chen, to conclude a covenant at Tao. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke of Lu met with the chief minister, the Duke of Zhou, the Marquis of Qi, the heir of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao at Kuiqiu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Xi.〕 A meeting was held with a royal officer and representatives of Jin, Song, Qi, Chen, Cai, and Qin to conclude a covenant at Diquan. 〔Twenty-ninth year of Duke Xi.〕 The Duke of Lu met with Viscount Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The Yin clan set up the king’s son Zhao as king. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhao.〕

Record of Rites (Liji)

Whenever talented men from among the people are appointed to office, they must first be assessed. Only after assessment has distinguished their abilities are they employed; only after they have undertaken duties are they granted rank; and only after their positions have been settled are they granted stipends.

Observing the bounds proper to a son and a minister is the means of honoring one’s ruler and cherishing one’s parents.

The zither accompanying the hymn “Pure Temple” has vermilion strings and widely spaced sound holes. One voice leads and three respond: there is sound that lingers beyond the notes.

“Gentleman” is a designation that completes a person’s good name. When the people accord someone this designation, calling him the son of a gentleman, this makes his parent a gentleman: it thus completes his parent’s good name.

translation_en:
Second Session

Discourse
“When the ruler’s resolve is settled, orderly government throughout the realm is achieved.”

Edicts, proclamations, and memorials 〔One topic within this category [?]〕
Compose an edict in the voice of Emperor Wen of Han proposing relief grants and loans during the mild weather of spring. 〔Second year of his reign〕

Legal Judgments 〔Five items〕

Third Session

Considered separately, each serves the other; in substance, however, they lead to the same end. For the Three Dynasties and earlier, the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
所稱莫可尚已我
太祖高皇帝挺生南服起定中原雖方草昧之
時其創造規模有承平暇裕之時所不
能到者觀其首立三局分統庶務視天
下既定之後固有詳畧之不同然簡而
有體畧而不遺千條萬目兼司並轄經
綸之妙非
聖智孰能與於此其後復命儒臣定擬三禮及
自作
===
大誥三篇與夫洪武禮制
大明律等書次第頒示臣民瞻聽翕然一新
列聖相承宣明申布重熙累洽與古帝王之治
異世同符猗歟盛矣不知漢唐宋之君
間亦有能彷彿者乎
皇上嗣大歷服精勤化理雖行已同倫而違越
之禁尤嚴刑已當罪而
欽恤之典累下於是可仰窺
皇上之心即
punctuated:
所稱，莫可尚已。我太祖高皇帝挺生南服，起定中原。雖方草昧之時，其創造規模，有承平暇裕之時所不能到者。觀其首立三局，分統庶務，視天下既定之後，固有詳畧之不同，然簡而有體，畧而不遺，千條萬目，兼司並轄。經綸之妙，非聖智孰能與於此？其後復命儒臣定擬三禮，及自作《大誥》三篇，與夫《洪武禮制》、《大明律》等書，次第頒示臣民，瞻聽翕然一新。列聖相承，宣明申布，重熙累洽，與古帝王之治異世同符。猗歟，盛矣！不知漢唐宋之君，間亦有能彷彿者乎？
皇上嗣大歷服，精勤化理。雖行已同倫，而違越之禁尤嚴；刑已當罪，而欽恤之典累下。於是可仰窺皇上之心即
translation_en:
…what the Odes and Documents praise could not be surpassed. Our Emperor Taizu Gao arose preeminent in the southern regions and took up arms to pacify the Central Plain. Even in that unsettled founding period, the scope and design of his institutions reached heights unattainable even with the leisure and ample resources of settled peace. Consider how he first established three bureaus, dividing responsibility for the many affairs of government among them. Compared with the arrangements after the realm had been pacified, these admittedly differed in their degree of elaboration. Yet they were simple while possessing proper structure, concise while omitting nothing: the thousand provisions and myriad particulars all fell within their joint administration and oversight. Who without sagely wisdom could have attained such mastery in ordering affairs? Subsequently, he again commanded Confucian officials to draw up definitive provisions for the three rites, and personally composed the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements. These, together with such works as the Ritual Regulations of the Hongwu Reign and the Great Ming Code, were successively promulgated to officials and commoners, renewing at once all that they saw and heard. The successive sage emperors clarified and repeatedly proclaimed these provisions, bringing prosperity upon prosperity and peace upon peace. Their government matched that of the ancient emperors and kings, though in a different age. Ah, how splendid! We wonder whether, among the rulers of the Han, Tang, and Song, there were any who even approached this achievement.
His Majesty has succeeded to the great imperial mandate and applies himself diligently to moral transformation and good government. Although conduct already conforms to common ethical norms, the prohibitions against transgression are especially strict; although punishments already fit the crimes, edicts enjoining reverent care and compassion in administering punishment have repeatedly been issued. From this we may reverently discern that His Majesty’s heart is precisely…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖與
列聖之心也但民志尚未能悉定而偕以敗禮
民行尚未能悉正而縱以犯法豈奉行
者之失職歟抑承平之久威易於恩渥
之餘也茲欲體
聖祖創造之意舉
列聖繼守之盛以祗順
皇上圖治之心必有道矣諸士子經濟之志藴
藉有素其發抒而盡言之以告我盖不
===
特占子之用世而已
問國家設官分職凡以爲民也故親民之
職莫如守令而戢暴以安民則惟將帥
焉是皆不可不慎重者也古者論當官
之法其事有三行師之法其德有五夷
考其人若令富邑而力行清潔守河北
而躬履節儉歷遷三郡謙恭每形於色
爲宰數年教化大洽於民皆所謂循吏
者也不知於三者之事果能盡焉否乎
punctuated:
聖祖與列聖之心也。但民志尚未能悉定，而偕以敗禮；民行尚未能悉正，而縱以犯法。豈奉行者之失職歟？抑承平之久，威易於恩渥之餘也？茲欲體聖祖創造之意，舉列聖繼守之盛，以祗順皇上圖治之心，必有道矣。諸士子經濟之志，藴藉有素，其發抒而盡言之，以告我，盖不特占子之用世而已。

問：國家設官分職，凡以爲民也。故親民之職莫如守令，而戢暴以安民，則惟將帥焉。是皆不可不慎重者也。古者論當官之法，其事有三；行師之法，其德有五。夷考其人，若令富邑而力行清潔，守河北而躬履節儉，歷遷三郡、謙恭每形於色，爲宰數年、教化大洽於民，皆所謂循吏者也。不知於三者之事，果能盡焉否乎？
translation_en:
…the heart of the Sagely Founder and the successive sage emperors. Yet the people’s dispositions have not all been settled, and they join together in violating ritual propriety; their conduct has not all been rectified, and they give themselves free rein to break the law. Is this because those charged with implementing these measures have failed in their duties? Or, after so long a period of peace, has awe of authority weakened amid abundant imperial favor [?]? There must be a way to embody the Sagely Founder’s intentions in establishing the dynasty and to carry forward the splendid achievements of the successive sage emperors in preserving it, thereby reverently fulfilling His Majesty’s desire for good government. You examination candidates have long cultivated aspirations to order the realm and benefit the people. Express them fully and tell us all that you have to say, for our purpose is not merely to judge your fitness for public service.

Question: The state establishes offices and assigns duties entirely for the sake of the people. Thus, among offices in close contact with the people, none compares with those of prefect and district magistrate; while suppressing violence to bring peace to the people falls to military commanders. These are all responsibilities that must be treated with the utmost care. The ancients, in discussing the principles of holding office, identified three essential tasks; in discussing the principles of commanding an army, they identified five virtues. Examining the men concerned, we find one who served as magistrate of a wealthy district and diligently maintained his integrity; one who governed Hebei and personally practiced frugality; one who successively governed three commanderies and whose humility and respectfulness were always evident in his demeanor; and one who served as magistrate for several years and whose moral instruction thoroughly permeated the populace. All were what are called exemplary officials. But were they indeed able to fulfill all three of those tasks?

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
或别有其人歟若養兵用間以復齊七
十餘城移陣渡水以却秦八十萬衆師
行有紀佐漢祚以中興使命交通感吳
人之翕服皆所謂良將者也不知於五
者之德亦能舉焉否乎抑别有其人歟
方今
聖明勵精爲治嚴守令之選廣將帥之求非不
慎且重也然而惠澤未溥於閭閻而貪
饕之風猶存威望未嚴於敵愾而糜費
之弊滋甚若此者其故何歟兹欲爲守
令者三事是脩爲將帥者五德是舉將
以追配於古人而成乂安於
===
今日是必有道矣諸生行有斯民之責其詳
著于篇以觀所藴焉
問君子之論人不過因言考行因名責實
期不失其真而已然慱觀往籍爲論不
一豈去取軒輊各以其意初無一定之
鑒歟如自納於刑贖懼君以兵之罪耳
punctuated:
或别有其人歟？若養兵用間，以復齊七十餘城；移陣渡水，以却秦八十萬衆；師行有紀，佐漢祚以中興；使命交通，感吳人之翕服，皆所謂良將者也。不知於五者之德，亦能舉焉否乎？抑别有其人歟？方今聖明勵精爲治，嚴守令之選，廣將帥之求，非不慎且重也。然而惠澤未溥於閭閻，而貪饕之風猶存；威望未嚴於敵愾，而糜費之弊滋甚。若此者，其故何歟？兹欲爲守令者三事是脩，爲將帥者五德是舉，將以追配於古人，而成乂安於今日，是必有道矣。諸生行有斯民之責，其詳著于篇，以觀所藴焉。

問：君子之論人，不過因言考行，因名責實，期不失其真而已。然慱觀往籍，爲論不一，豈去取軒輊各以其意，初無一定之鑒歟？如自納於刑贖，懼君以兵之罪耳。
translation_en:
…Or were there others? Those who maintained troops and employed spies to recover more than seventy cities of Qi; who had the opposing battle line moved back and crossed the river to repel Qin’s host of eight hundred thousand; whose armies marched with discipline and who assisted in restoring the Han dynasty; and who exchanged envoys and won the wholehearted submission of the people of Wu—all are called fine generals. Yet did they fully possess the five virtues? Or were there others?

Today, our sagacious sovereign devotes his energies to good government, rigorously selecting prefects and magistrates and searching widely for generals. These matters certainly receive careful and serious attention. Yet beneficence has not reached all the common people, and the habit of rapacity persists; military prestige has not sufficiently overawed the enemy [?], while the abuses of wasteful expenditure grow ever worse. Why is this so? If we now wish prefects and magistrates to cultivate the three duties, and generals to exemplify the five virtues, so that they may match the men of antiquity and bring order and peace to the present day, there must surely be a way. You candidates will soon bear responsibility for these people. Set out your views fully in your essays, so that we may see what you have within you.

Question: When a gentleman judges others, he merely examines their conduct in light of their words and demands that their actual deeds match their reputations, seeking only to ascertain the truth about them. Yet a broad survey of earlier writings reveals divergent judgments. Could it be that acceptance and rejection, praise and disparagement, each follow the critic’s own inclinations, with no fixed standard of discernment at all? For example, submitting oneself to punishment and redemption of the penalty merely concerned the offense of frightening one’s ruler with armed force.…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
顧謂其愛君何歟施敬於鹽盂刑于寡
妻之常耳遂謂其有德何歟舉賢而忘
仇嫌何以謂之善爲相而無私積何以
謂之忠受彤弓之賦乃成知禮之名辭
大舘之授乃致近德之許感國士之遇
而報以國士取之若是巳然擊衣之請
似未免涉於迂竭股肱之力而加以忠
貞與之若宜巳然斯言之玷似未免失
於始豈其就事論事不暇及其全節或
===
微意所指未可淺之爲議歟宋儒論人
皆聖賢家法無容訾巳至真西山論歷
代輔臣則槩以四事律之其亦有所放
歟抑惟獨得之見也設以西山之論加
之若數人者其失得又當何如諸士子
考究精深詳叙而折衷之宜無難者幸
毋讓
問學者尚友前脩必誦其詩讀其書而又
論其世也江西諸士子生長之地請即
punctuated:
顧謂其愛君，何歟？施敬於鹽盂，刑于寡妻之常耳，遂謂其有德，何歟？舉賢而忘仇嫌，何以謂之善？爲相而無私積，何以謂之忠？受彤弓之賦，乃成知禮之名；辭大舘之授，乃致近德之許。感國士之遇，而報以國士，取之若是巳，然擊衣之請，似未免涉於迂；竭股肱之力，而加以忠貞，與之若宜巳，然斯言之玷，似未免失於始。豈其就事論事，不暇及其全節？或微意所指，未可淺之爲議歟？宋儒論人，皆聖賢家法，無容訾巳。至真西山論歷代輔臣，則槩以四事律之，其亦有所放歟？抑惟獨得之見也？設以西山之論加之若數人者，其失得又當何如？諸士子考究精深，詳叙而折衷之，宜無難者，幸毋讓。

問：學者尚友前脩，必誦其詩，讀其書，而又論其世也。江西，諸士子生長之地，請即
translation_en:
…Yet he is said to have loved his ruler: why? Showing respect over a salt bowl was merely the ordinary practice of setting an example for one’s wife; why, then, was he declared virtuous? Why was recommending a worthy man while forgetting personal enmity called goodness? Why was serving as chief minister without accumulating private wealth called loyalty? Receiving a recitation of “The Vermilion Bow” earned one man a reputation for understanding ritual; declining the offer of a grand lodging earned another the commendation that he approached virtue. One man, moved by being treated as a distinguished man of the realm, repaid that treatment as such a man should. Such approval of him seems right; yet his request to strike the robe seems perhaps unduly misguided. Another exerted himself fully as his ruler’s trusted assistant and was praised for loyalty and constancy. Such commendation seems fitting; yet the blemish in his words seems to reveal a fault at the outset. Were these judgments made case by case, without time to consider the entirety of each man’s conduct? Or was there a subtle intention behind them that cannot be discussed superficially? The Song Confucians judged people according to the established methods of the sages and worthies, leaving no room for censure. But when Zhen Xishan discussed the assisting ministers of successive dynasties, he judged them uniformly by four criteria. Did he too have a precedent to follow, or was this an insight uniquely his own? If Xishan’s judgments were applied to these several men, how should their faults and merits be assessed? You candidates should investigate deeply and precisely, set out the details, and arrive at a balanced judgment. This should present no difficulty; please do not hold back.

Question: When scholars seek friendship with worthy predecessors across the ages, they must recite their poems, read their writings, and also examine the times in which they lived. Jiangxi is the land where you candidates were born and raised. Please take as your subject…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
其詩文名家者論之託隱廬阜晉之徵
士也而以古詩鳴其後有爲江西詩派
者果能窺五柳之戶牖歟書山石之辭
詩亦高矣何乃不得與二賢班耶崛起
廬陵宋之名臣也而以古文鳴其時有
爲江西山斗者果能入六一之閫奥歟
記袁州之學文亦古矣何乃不得與二
公並耶我
朝文教聿興崇尚理學科舉條式罷去詩賦
===
詩雖不言可矣而以文取士則猶昔也
不知今之文之與古文同乎異乎如遊宦
理學者濂溪始倡於溢浦不由師傳默
契道體其高不可及考亭再倡於白鹿
主敬明理集其大成其說爲甚長至於
教學者亦曰作詩須從陶韋門庭來其
於爾鄉之前輩固亦推尊之矣意者理
學可通於古詩歟又曰文章至歐蘇始
是暢其於爾鄉之先賢固亦表章之矣
punctuated: 其詩文名家者論之。託隱廬阜，晉之徵士也，而以古詩鳴。其後有爲江西詩派者，果能窺五柳之戶牖歟？書山石之辭，詩亦高矣，何乃不得與二賢班耶？崛起廬陵，宋之名臣也，而以古文鳴。其時有爲江西山斗者，果能入六一之閫奥歟？記袁州之學，文亦古矣，何乃不得與二公並耶？我朝文教聿興，崇尚理學，科舉條式罷去詩賦。詩雖不言可矣，而以文取士則猶昔也。不知今之文之與古文同乎，異乎？如遊宦理學者，濂溪始倡於溢浦，不由師傳，默契道體，其高不可及。考亭再倡於白鹿，主敬明理，集其大成，其說爲甚長。至於教學者，亦曰：「作詩須從陶韋門庭來。」其於爾鄉之前輩，固亦推尊之矣。意者理學可通於古詩歟？又曰：「文章至歐蘇始是暢。」其於爾鄉之先賢，固亦表章之矣。
translation_en:
…discuss those renowned for their poetry and prose. He who sought seclusion on Mount Lu was a scholar summoned to office under the Jin, and won renown through ancient-style poetry. Could those who subsequently formed the Jiangxi school of poetry truly glimpse through the doors and windows of Wuliu, the Master of the Five Willows [Tao Qian]? The author of Mountain Rocks also attained great heights in poetry; why, then, could he not rank alongside the two worthies? He who rose to prominence from Luling was an eminent minister of the Song, and won renown through ancient-style prose. Could those of his time who became Jiangxi’s Mount Tai and Northern Dipper—its literary authorities—truly enter the inner chambers of Liuyi [Ouyang Xiu]? The author of the account of the school in Yuanzhou also wrote prose in the ancient manner; why, then, could he not stand alongside the two gentlemen?

Under our dynasty, literary education has flourished, and the learning of principle has been held in high esteem. The examination regulations abolished poetry and rhapsody. Although we may leave poetry aside, selecting men through prose remains the practice, just as in former times. Is the prose of today the same as ancient-style prose, or different?

As for scholars of principle who served away from their native places [?], Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi] first advocated this learning at Yipu [?]. Without receiving instruction from a teacher, he tacitly apprehended the substance of the Way; his lofty attainment was beyond reach. Kaoting [Zhu Xi] advocated it anew at Bailu, the White Deer Grotto Academy. Taking reverent attentiveness as his foundation and elucidating principle, he brought this learning to its great synthesis; his teachings have much to commend them. Yet when instructing students, he also said: “To compose poetry, one must come through the gateway of Tao and Wei.” Thus he certainly also esteemed the predecessors of your native region. Might the learning of principle, then, connect with ancient-style poetry? He also said: “Only with Ou and Su did prose attain fluency.” Thus he certainly also honored the earlier worthies of your native region.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
意者理學可兼乎古文歟凡若此者先
儒具有成說在諸士子究心於景仰之
餘久矣願相與論之以觀尚友之學
問國衛於兵民資於食皆政務之最要者
也我
朝奄有華夏承平百五十餘年制兵足食之
方皆極其備夫何頃者獨石永寧等處
烽火小警輒勞
聖慮命將出師是果各邊將士平日之所練者
===
有不足於用歟昔人有守鴈門而匈奴
不敢近屯九郡而單于輒引去善騎射
者卻契丹於代州躬勞苦者拒西戎於
隴右固皆善於備邊者矣不知亦可用
於今否乎近者直隸河南等處穀麥告
災至厪
宸衷遣官分賑是果各郡倉廩平日之所儲者
有不足於用歟昔人有守益州按田稅
計口以備荒知襄邑籍賈舟販穀以備
punctuated:
意者理學可兼乎古文歟？凡若此者，先儒具有成說在，諸士子究心於景仰之餘久矣。願相與論之，以觀尚友之學。

問：國衛於兵，民資於食，皆政務之最要者也。我朝奄有華夏，承平百五十餘年，制兵足食之方，皆極其備。夫何頃者獨石、永寧等處烽火小警，輒勞聖慮，命將出師？是果各邊將士平日之所練者，有不足於用歟？昔人有守鴈門而匈奴不敢近，屯九郡而單于輒引去；善騎射者卻契丹於代州，躬勞苦者拒西戎於隴右，固皆善於備邊者矣。不知亦可用於今否乎？近者直隸、河南等處穀麥告災，至厪宸衷，遣官分賑。是果各郡倉廩平日之所儲者，有不足於用歟？昔人有守益州，按田稅、計口以備荒；知襄邑，籍賈舟、販穀以備
translation_en:
…Might the Learning of the Way also encompass ancient-style prose? On all such matters, earlier Confucian scholars have left established explanations. You candidates have long devoted careful thought to them while revering those scholars. I invite you to discuss these matters, so that I may assess your learning in taking the worthy men of the past as friends.

Question: The state is defended by soldiers, and the people depend upon food. Both are among the most essential concerns of government. Our dynasty has held sway over all China and enjoyed peace for more than a hundred and fifty years. Its arrangements for managing the armed forces and ensuring sufficient food have been brought to the fullest state of preparedness. Why, then, did minor alarms at the beacon towers in Dushi, Yongning, and other places recently trouble His Majesty and lead him to appoint generals and dispatch troops? Can it truly be that the training ordinarily undertaken by officers and soldiers along the frontiers is inadequate when put to use? In former times, one man defended Yanmen so effectively that the Xiongnu dared not approach; another stationed troops in nine commanderies, whereupon the chanyu withdrew. A man skilled in mounted archery repulsed the Khitan at Daizhou; another, who personally endured toil and hardship, held off the western Rong in Longyou. These were certainly all men adept at frontier defense. Could their methods also be employed today?

Recently, grain and wheat crops in Zhili, Henan, and other places were reported stricken by disaster. This so concerned His Majesty that he dispatched officials to distribute relief. Can it truly be that the reserves ordinarily held in the granaries of the various prefectures are insufficient when needed? In former times, one man governing Yizhou assessed taxes on the fields and counted the population to prepare for famine; another, serving as magistrate of Xiangyi, registered merchant boats and traded in grain in preparation for…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
糶或散公廪而活青州五十萬人或弛
鹽禁而活京東八萬餘口固皆長於捄
荒者矣不知亦可行於今否乎諸生以
濟時行道爲志其於制兵足食之要必
籌之熟矣其敷陳之毋隱
punctuated: 糶，或散公廪而活青州五十萬人，或弛鹽禁而活京東八萬餘口，固皆長於捄荒者矣。不知亦可行於今否乎？諸生以濟時行道爲志，其於制兵足食之要，必籌之熟矣。其敷陳之，毋隱。
translation_en: …for sale as grain relief. Some distributed grain from public granaries and saved five hundred thousand people in Qingzhou; others relaxed the salt prohibitions and saved more than eighty thousand people in Jingdong. They were certainly all adept at relieving famine. Might their measures also be put into practice today? You candidates aspire to meet the needs of the times and put the Way into practice; you must surely have deliberated thoroughly on the essentials of managing troops and ensuring sufficient food. Set forth your views fully, withholding nothing.

text:

四書
知止而后有定定而后能靜靜而后能安
安而后能慮慮而后能得
郭鵬
同考試官教諭張　批〔至善爲明德新民之標的自是明白塲中作者於知止處多泛言之殊失經旨且撫〕
〔拾腐語可厭此篇氣充而理暢講貫之精筆力之健蕪〕
〔而有之佳士也〕
===

同考試官教諭楊　批〔題本明白作者類能成文求其縝密精到者此篇爲冠〕
考試官學正孫　批〔體認親切而辭足以發之宜〕

理以極其至爲善學以止其所爲終也然非先

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“When one knows where to rest, one has a settled purpose; with a settled purpose, one can be tranquil; with tranquility, one can be at ease; at ease, one can deliberate; through deliberation, one can attain the goal.”

Guo Peng

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “That the highest good is the goal of illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people is clear in itself. Candidates in the examination hall mostly discuss ‘knowing where to rest’ in vague terms, quite missing the meaning of the classic. Moreover, they cobble together stale phrases [?], which is tiresome. This essay is full of vigor and lucid in its reasoning. It possesses both [?] precision born of thorough study and strength of expression. This is an excellent scholar.”

Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “Ordinary examination essays cannot match this. Its author has evidently devoted effort to the Way taught in the Great Learning.”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “The topic itself is clear, and most candidates can compose an essay on it. But if one seeks close reasoning and precise insight, this essay ranks first.”

Examiner Sun, Director of Studies, comments: “His understanding is intimate and immediate, and his language adequately expresses it. Fitting.”

Examiner Yan, Director of Studies, comments: “Its reasoning and writing are distinctive in themselves and worthy of serving as a model. It is recorded here as a model for the many scholars.”

In discussing resting in the highest good, the Great Learning teaches that one must first understand it clearly in the mind, and thereby have the means to attain it. For principle is good when brought to its utmost perfection, and learning reaches its completion when one rests in the proper place. Yet unless one first…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
明諸心何以能定靜安慮而得其所止哉聖經
一章示人止至善之由如此意謂明德新民固
有至善之當止矣然止之豈無所自邪蓋必庶
物明於貫通之後而其本然一定之則有以見
之真衆善覺於昭晰之餘而其當然不易之極
有以擇之審德不惟明而已知明之有當止之
地而全體極天下之至精民不惟新而已知新
之有當止之所而大用極天下之至妙知止如
此然后志趣專而不疑於所往趨向正而不昧
===
於所從斯能定矣能定如此然后意無將迎而
中自有主心無出入而動必以天斯能靜矣靜
則與理相涵不擇地而後泰以道爲體隨所處
而皆宜不於是而能安乎安則物來而權度精
切不爽毫髮矣事至而見幾明決不俟終日矣
非因之而能慮乎能慮則造詣既深有左右逢
原之機踐履益熟有體用一源之妙明德所當
止者得而止焉事理本然之則無蔽於始無缺
於終矣新民所當止者得而止焉義理當然之
punctuated: 明諸心，何以能定、靜、安、慮而得其所止哉？聖經一章示人止至善之由如此。意謂明德新民，固有至善之當止矣，然止之豈無所自邪？蓋必庶物明於貫通之後，而其本然一定之則有以見之真；衆善覺於昭晰之餘，而其當然不易之極有以擇之審。德不惟明而已，知明之有當止之地，而全體極天下之至精；民不惟新而已，知新之有當止之所，而大用極天下之至妙。知止如此，然后志趣專而不疑於所往，趨向正而不昧於所從，斯能定矣。能定如此，然后意無將迎而中自有主，心無出入而動必以天，斯能靜矣。靜則與理相涵，不擇地而後泰；以道爲體，隨所處而皆宜，不於是而能安乎？安則物來而權度精切，不爽毫髮矣；事至而見幾明決，不俟終日矣，非因之而能慮乎？能慮則造詣既深，有左右逢原之機；踐履益熟，有體用一源之妙。明德所當止者，得而止焉，事理本然之則無蔽於始，無缺於終矣；新民所當止者，得而止焉，義理當然之
translation_en:
…make it clear in the mind, how could one achieve settled purpose, stillness, peace, and deliberation, and attain the proper resting place? The single chapter of the sage’s canonical text thus shows people the way to rest in the highest good. Its meaning is that manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people certainly have a highest good in which one should rest. Yet could resting there have no starting point? Only after achieving comprehensive understanding do the myriad things become clear, enabling one truly to perceive their inherent, fixed standards; only after attaining lucid discernment does one apprehend the many forms of goodness, enabling one carefully to distinguish their proper, unchanging ultimate standards. It is not enough merely to manifest virtue: one must know the point at which its manifestation should rest, so that its substance in its entirety reaches the utmost refinement in the world. It is not enough merely to renew the people: one must know the point at which their renewal should rest, so that its great operation reaches the utmost subtlety in the world. Knowing where to rest in this way, one’s aspirations become single-minded, without doubt about where to go; one’s direction becomes correct, without confusion about what to follow. Thus one can attain settled purpose.

With purpose thus settled, one’s thoughts neither pursue what has passed nor anticipate what is to come, and one naturally has a master within. The mind neither goes out nor comes in, and its activity necessarily accords with Heaven. Thus one can attain stillness. In stillness, one abides in mutual permeation with principle, without needing to choose a particular place before being at ease. Taking the Way as one’s substance, one is appropriately disposed wherever one finds oneself. Does this not enable one to attain peace? At peace, when things come before one, one’s weighing and measuring are exact, without the slightest error; when affairs arise, one discerns their incipient tendencies clearly and decisively, without waiting until the day’s end. Does this not, in turn, enable one to deliberate? Able to deliberate, one’s attainment is now profound, and one can encounter the source on every side; one’s practice grows increasingly accomplished, and one realizes the subtle unity of substance and function in a single source. One attains and rests in the point where manifesting luminous virtue should rest: the inherent standards of affairs and their principles are neither obscured at the beginning nor deficient at the end. One attains and rests in the point where renewing the people should rest: the proper…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
極非苟知之亦允蹈之矣吁自知止而后及於
能得如此序之不可亂而功之不可缺迺互見
之矣為大人之學者可不知所從事哉抑考書
之所謂安汝止欽厥止即止至善之謂也易之
所謂知至至之知終終之即知止能得之謂也
蓋三代而上道明德一故聖賢告君皆不外此
其為教可知已三代而下治衰教弛故聖賢發
明不一而足其憂世可知已學者味書之言則
益知至善之當止味易之言則益知止至善之
功矣
===
士不可以不弘毅任重而道遠
張勛
同考試官教諭費 批 弘毅可以見士之所養此作
論說極是而於任重道遠處尤善體貼觀此足以占
子之所養矣
同考試官教諭丁 批 論語義要莊重渾厚場中
作者不腐則鑿讀之殊為可厭雅徤切實無如此
篇宜錄之以式來學
punctuated:
極，非苟知之，亦允蹈之矣。吁！自知止而后及於能得，如此，序之不可亂，而功之不可缺，迺互見之矣。為大人之學者，可不知所從事哉？抑考《書》之所謂「安汝止」、「欽厥止」，即止至善之謂也；《易》之所謂「知至至之，知終終之」，即知止能得之謂也。蓋三代而上，道明德一，故聖賢告君皆不外此，其為教可知已；三代而下，治衰教弛，故聖賢發明不一而足，其憂世可知已。學者味《書》之言，則益知至善之當止；味《易》之言，則益知止至善之功矣。

士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠。
張勛

同考試官教諭費批：弘毅可以見士之所養。此作論說極是，而於任重道遠處尤善體貼。觀此，足以占子之所養矣。

同考試官教諭丁批：《論語》義要莊重渾厚。場中作者，不腐則鑿，讀之殊為可厭。雅徤切實，無如此篇，宜錄之以式來學。
translation_en:
…the ultimate standard: one does not merely know it, but also faithfully puts it into practice. Ah! From knowing where to rest to being able to attain it, the progression is thus: that its sequence cannot be disordered and that no part of its effort can be omitted become apparent through one another. Can those pursuing the learning of the great person fail to know where to direct their efforts? Moreover, consider the Documents: its expressions “rest in your proper stopping place” and “reverently attend to that stopping place” refer precisely to resting in the highest good. The Changes says, “Know what is to be reached and reach it; know what is to be completed and complete it.” This refers precisely to knowing where to rest and being able to attain it. During the Three Dynasties and earlier, the Way was clear and virtue unified; hence the counsel that sages and worthies offered their rulers never departed from this. From this we can understand their teaching. After the Three Dynasties, government declined and instruction grew lax; hence the sages and worthies explained these matters in numerous ways. From this we can understand their concern for the world. By pondering the words of the Documents, learners will better understand that the highest good is where they ought to rest; by pondering the words of the Changes, they will better understand the effort required to rest in the highest good.

“A scholar must be broad-minded and resolute: his burden is heavy and his road is long.”
By Zhang Xun 張勛.

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: Broad-mindedness and resolve reveal what a scholar has cultivated within himself. This essay’s exposition is entirely sound, and its treatment of the heavy burden and long road shows especially perceptive understanding. Reading it is sufficient to discern what you have cultivated within yourself.

Comment by Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor: An exposition of the meaning of the Analects should be dignified, substantial, and generous in spirit. Writers in the examination hall are either stale or forced in their interpretations, making their work particularly tiresome to read. For elegance, vigor, and sound substance, none equals this essay. It should be recorded as a model for future learners.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正孫　批〔說理之文自是難作此篇備得〕
考試官學正顏　批〔理不悖而詞足以發之可取〕
論士之所養者有不苟以其所責者自不易蓋
士之係於養也尚矣況夫責於已者重且遠焉
豈可以苟為哉昔曾子之意蓋謂凡民之秀
者莫如士而士之貴者莫如養養之不弘無以
為容善之地士以謀道為志者也豈可以不弘
乎養之不毅無以為造善之基士以希賢為志
者也豈可以不毅乎故必寬以居之而廓然襟
===
度之含弘初無淺陋狹隘之私否則一庸人耳
謂為士也奚可哉勇以強之而卓然志力之堅
毅初無逡巡委靡之失否則一鄙夫耳名為士
也奚宜哉士之弘毅如此夫豈徒然而已誠以
任之不重猶可以易為也士則思夫天之賦於
我者匪輕而我奉持之蓋有此身所不能載者
其重也孰加焉道之未遠猶可以易致也士則
念夫天之畀於已者甚大而我蹈履之蓋有終
身所不可窮者其遠也孰過焉以衆善而見於
punctuated:
考試官學正孫，批〔說理之文，自是難作，此篇備得。〕
考試官學正顏，批〔理不悖，而詞足以發之，可取。〕
論士之所養者有不苟，以其所責者自不易。蓋士之係於養也尚矣，況夫責於已者重且遠焉，豈可以苟為哉？昔曾子之意，蓋謂凡民之秀者莫如士，而士之貴者莫如養。養之不弘，無以為容善之地。士以謀道為志者也，豈可以不弘乎？養之不毅，無以為造善之基。士以希賢為志者也，豈可以不毅乎？故必寬以居之，而廓然襟度之含弘，初無淺陋狹隘之私，否則一庸人耳，謂為士也奚可哉？勇以強之，而卓然志力之堅毅，初無逡巡委靡之失，否則一鄙夫耳，名為士也奚宜哉？士之弘毅如此，夫豈徒然而已？誠以任之不重，猶可以易為也。士則思夫天之賦於我者匪輕，而我奉持之，蓋有此身所不能載者，其重也孰加焉？道之未遠，猶可以易致也。士則念夫天之畀於已者甚大，而我蹈履之，蓋有終身所不可窮者，其遠也孰過焉？以衆善而見於
translation_en:
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔Writing that expounds principles is inherently difficult to compose. This essay fully achieves its purpose.〕
Examiner Yan, Instructor, comments: 〔Its reasoning does not contravene principle, and its language adequately expresses it. It merits selection.〕
In considering what a scholar cultivates in himself, we find that he must not be careless, because the responsibilities incumbent upon him are inherently difficult. Indeed, the scholar’s dependence upon self-cultivation has long been recognized. Moreover, the responsibilities he bears are weighty and far-reaching: how could he discharge them carelessly? What Zengzi meant in former times was presumably this: among the common people, none excels the scholar; and among the scholar’s qualities, none is more precious than his self-cultivation. If his cultivation lacks breadth, there is no ground in which to accommodate goodness. The scholar sets his heart on pursuing the Way: how could he lack breadth? If his cultivation lacks resolve, there is no foundation for attaining goodness. The scholar sets his heart on emulating the worthy: how could he lack resolve?
Thus he must dwell in broad-mindedness, his capacious heart embracing all with breadth, wholly free of shallow and narrow selfishness. Otherwise he is merely an ordinary man: how could he be called a scholar? He must strengthen himself through courage, his will and strength standing firm and resolute, wholly free of hesitation and languor. Otherwise he is merely a base fellow: how could the name of scholar befit him? Such are the scholar’s breadth and resolve. Surely they are not without purpose!
Indeed, if a burden were not heavy, one might still undertake it easily. But the scholar reflects: what Heaven has bestowed upon me is no light matter; in upholding it, there is something that this body cannot bear. What could exceed its weight? If the Way did not extend far, one might still reach its end easily. But the scholar considers: what Heaven has granted me is exceedingly great; in treading its course, there is something that an entire lifetime cannot exhaust. What could surpass its distance?
