title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
美也春秋紀入郕城邢之師而予奪齊衛之義
見矣在昔衛懷郕怨爰舉三軍以入之似若兵
出有名者春秋以為暴何耶蓋衛自州吁倡亂
之後呻吟塗炭之民誠可憫也宜以新君繼世
苟增修德政深固本根君國子民之道得矣執
意大衆悉出而有事于郕耶傷痍未洗於前時
荼毒轉加於今日環甲荷戈使其飢者弗食勞
者弗息也不亦暴乎噫萬姓仇予予將疇依此
書所以載太康之困民也今乃不鑒其覆轍如
===
此吾知邦本一搖民將作慝豈不動反側之危
哉苟不罪之則窮兵黷武者無所懲故特稱師
所以著其暴也至若齊因邢遷大合三國以城
之似若輕舉妄動者春秋以為盛何耶蓋邢遭
狄人迫逐之後奔亡溝壑之勢甚可危也桓以
首霸創業苟仍遣孤軍遠亦薄救方伯連帥之
職隳矣孰幸舍次聶北而有夷儀之城耶施大
功於不報存小國於將亡壅衆合謀殆見築之
登登往哉生生也一何盛乎噫豈不懷歸畏此
punctuated:
美也。春秋紀入郕、城邢之師，而予奪齊衛之義見矣。在昔衛懷郕怨，爰舉三軍以入之，似若兵出有名者，春秋以為暴，何耶？蓋衛自州吁倡亂之後，呻吟塗炭之民，誠可憫也。宜以新君繼世，苟增修德政，深固本根，君國子民之道得矣。執意大衆悉出，而有事于郕耶？傷痍未洗於前時，荼毒轉加於今日，環甲荷戈，使其飢者弗食，勞者弗息也，不亦暴乎？噫！「萬姓仇予，予將疇依？」此《書》所以載太康之困民也。今乃不鑒其覆轍如此，吾知邦本一搖，民將作慝，豈不動反側之危哉？苟不罪之，則窮兵黷武者無所懲，故特稱師，所以著其暴也。
至若齊因邢遷，大合三國以城之，似若輕舉妄動者，春秋以為盛，何耶？蓋邢遭狄人迫逐之後，奔亡溝壑之勢，甚可危也。桓以首霸創業，苟仍遣孤軍，遠亦薄救，方伯連帥之職隳矣。孰幸舍次聶北，而有夷儀之城耶？施大功於不報，存小國於將亡，壅衆合謀，殆見築之登登，往哉生生也，一何盛乎！噫！豈不懷歸，畏此
translation_en:
…is what makes it praiseworthy. By recording the armies that entered Cheng and walled Xing, the Spring and Autumn Annals reveals the principles governing its approval and disapproval of Qi and Wei. Formerly, Wei harbored resentment against Cheng and accordingly mobilized its three armies to invade it. This might appear to have been a military expedition with a legitimate cause. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals deem it cruel? After Zhou Xu instigated disorder in Wei, the people, groaning in misery, were indeed pitiable. With a new ruler succeeding to the throne, they should have been governed accordingly: if he had further cultivated virtuous government and firmly secured the foundations, he would have fulfilled the way of ruling a state and cherishing its people as his children. Why insist on sending out the entire host to undertake a campaign against Cheng? The wounds of earlier days had not yet healed, yet further suffering was inflicted upon them now. Clad in armor and bearing spears, the hungry were denied food and the weary denied rest. Was this not cruel? Alas! “If the myriad people regard me as their enemy, on whom shall I rely?” This is why the Book of Documents records how Tai Kang distressed his people. Now, to this extent, Wei failed to take warning from his disastrous precedent. I know that once the foundations of the state were shaken, the people would rise in wrongdoing. Would this not provoke the danger of unrest? If such conduct were not condemned, those who exhausted their resources in warfare and recklessly employed military force would have no deterrent. Thus the Annals specifically calls the force an “army,” thereby exposing its cruelty.
As for Qi, when Xing relocated, it assembled the forces of three states on a grand scale to build walls for it. This might appear to have been rash and reckless action. Why, then, does the Spring and Autumn Annals deem it magnificent? After Xing had been harried and driven out by the Di, its people faced the grave danger of flight and death in ditches and ravines. Duke Huan was establishing his achievement as the foremost hegemon. Had he merely sent a solitary force again, providing scant aid from afar [?], he would have failed in his duties as regional overlord and leader of the allied lords. How fortunate that the troops encamped at Niebei and that walls were built at Yiyi! He performed a great service without recompense and preserved a small state on the verge of destruction. Gathering the multitude and combining their plans [?], one could almost see the wall-building proceed with resounding blows, and the people going forth to renewed life [?]. How magnificent! Alas! “Do we not long to return home? We stand in awe of this…”

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
簡書此詩所以美南仲之城國也今乃克踵其
芳躅如此吾見中國以安夷狄以攘寧不為霸
業之光哉苟不矜之則使義立功者何以勸故
持稱師所以美其盛也吁惡衛宣則人皆知視
民如子而牛羊用人者無有也予齊桓則人皆
知憂人之憂而秦越相視者無有也以此垂法
則民無不安國無不存經世之治成矣嘗考之
宣桓美惡有自也得位由於國人之手其始事
已出於專險阻嘗于出亡之時其蚤年志復向
===
鋭況當時石碏之請老已久管仲之攝政方新
仁賢存否之殊效驗至於如此有國者其鑒之
哉
宋師伐陳衛人救陳〔宣公十二年〕
王文
同考試官訓導蘇 批〔宋衛俱失作者每泥於傳意文斯晦矣此作於錯綜檃括殆盡錄之〕
考試官學正孫 批〔以義信立說最是〕
考試官學正顏 批〔明暢〕
punctuated:
簡書。」此詩所以美南仲之城國也。今乃克踵其芳躅如此，吾見中國以安，夷狄以攘，寧不為霸業之光哉？苟不矜之，則使義立功者何以勸？故持稱師，所以美其盛也。吁！惡衛宣，則人皆知視民如子，而牛羊用人者無有也；予齊桓，則人皆知憂人之憂，而秦越相視者無有也。以此垂法，則民無不安，國無不存，經世之治成矣。嘗考之，宣、桓美惡有自也。得位由於國人之手，其始事已出於專；險阻嘗于出亡之時，其蚤年志復向鋭。況當時石碏之請老已久，管仲之攝政方新，仁賢存否之殊，效驗至於如此。有國者其鑒之哉！
宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔宣公十二年〕
王文
同考試官訓導蘇批〔宋衛俱失，作者每泥於傳意，文斯晦矣。此作於錯綜檃括殆盡，錄之。〕
考試官學正孫批〔以義信立說，最是。〕
考試官學正顏批〔明暢。〕
translation_en:
…the written orders.” This poem praises Nan Zhong for fortifying the country. Now, in thus following his illustrious footsteps, I see the central states secured and the foreign peoples driven back. Is this not a glory of the hegemon’s achievement? If this were not commended, how could those who act righteously and accomplish worthy deeds be encouraged? Thus the designation “army” is retained [?] to praise the grandeur of this undertaking. Ah! By condemning Duke Xuan of Wei, everyone is taught to regard the people as their children, and none will treat human beings like cattle and sheep. By approving Duke Huan of Qi, everyone is taught to share others’ anxieties, and none will regard one another with the indifference of Qin and Yue. With these principles handed down as standards, all people will be secure and all states preserved: orderly government of the world will be achieved.
I have examined this: the evil of Duke Xuan and the goodness of Duke Huan had their respective origins. The former obtained his position through the hands of the people of his state, and his initial acts already sprang from arbitrary self-assertion; the latter experienced hardship while in exile, and his youthful resolve became still keener. Moreover, at that time Shi Que had long since requested retirement, while Guan Zhong had only recently assumed direction of government. The difference made by the presence or absence of humane and worthy men produced effects as great as these. Let those who rule states take warning!
“The army of Song attacked Chen; men of Wei came to Chen’s rescue.” 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕
Wang Wen
Associate Examiner Su, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Song and Wei were both at fault. Writers are often constrained by the meaning of the commentary, and their writing consequently becomes obscure. This composition interweaves and distills the material almost exhaustively. Include it.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔Basing the argument on righteousness and trustworthiness is entirely correct.〕
Examiner Yan, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
春秋於二國之兵有托詞以著其罪者有直詞
以見其失者于以見陳德于楚宋不當伐而衛
不當救也春秋明義惇信得不致嚴於書法間
哉慨自辰陵之會既還陳人之從楚已久清丘
之盟聿講諸侯之謀貳方新乃今魯宣中葉宋
帥大衆以伐陳衛乃提一旅以救之焉故自常
情觀之陳以中國而服於楚冠裳之辱罪不容
恕也宋以大邦致討未為不可君子以為罪者
君曰有義存焉彼陳有西氏之逆宋則縱之楚
===
能討之縣陳之舉固肆其强復封之恩亦不可
泯其罪未足責也宋能内自省德吾見養威蓄
銳之餘寧無陰奪其外附之志乎柰何舍已不
修惟人是責鳴鍾擊鼓彼何罪之可聲命將出
車我無詞之可執是殆挑目前之釁以召終身
之憂卒之宗社被圍兆諸此行也語曰君子義
以為質宋何足以語此若夫陳以無罪而困於
宋門庭之寇患所當禦也衛以友邦往救不為
不善君子以為失者則曰有信寓焉彼晉為清
punctuated: 春秋於二國之兵，有托詞以著其罪者，有直詞以見其失者，于以見陳德于楚，宋不當伐，而衛不當救也。春秋明義惇信，得不致嚴於書法間哉！慨自辰陵之會既還，陳人之從楚已久；清丘之盟聿講，諸侯之謀貳方新。乃今魯宣中葉，宋帥大衆以伐陳，衛乃提一旅以救之焉。故自常情觀之，陳以中國而服於楚，冠裳之辱，罪不容恕也。宋以大邦致討，未為不可。君子以為罪者，君曰有義存焉。彼陳有西氏之逆，宋則縱之，楚能討之。縣陳之舉，固肆其强；復封之恩，亦不可泯。其罪未足責也。宋能内自省德，吾見養威蓄銳之餘，寧無陰奪其外附之志乎？柰何舍已不修，惟人是責？鳴鍾擊鼓，彼何罪之可聲？命將出車，我無詞之可執。是殆挑目前之釁，以召終身之憂。卒之宗社被圍，兆諸此行也。語曰：「君子義以為質。」宋何足以語此？若夫陳以無罪而困於宋，門庭之寇，患所當禦也。衛以友邦往救，不為不善。君子以為失者，則曰有信寓焉。彼晉為清
translation_en:
In its accounts of the military actions of these two states, the Spring and Autumn Annals sometimes employs indirect wording to expose an offense and sometimes direct wording to reveal a failing. Here it shows that Chen was indebted to Chu: Song ought not to have attacked, and Wei ought not to have come to the rescue. In clarifying righteousness and fostering good faith, could the Annals fail to exercise rigor in its manner of recording events?

Alas, since the return from the meeting at Chenling, the people of Chen had long followed Chu; with the covenant at Qingqiu newly concluded, the other lords’ plans to draw Chen away from that allegiance were still fresh. Now, in the middle years of Duke Xuan of Lu’s reign, Song led a great host against Chen, while Wei brought a single brigade to its rescue. Viewed in ordinary terms, Chen, a state of the central realm, had submitted to Chu. This disgraced the ceremonial caps and robes of civilized rule and was an unforgivable offense. For Song, a great state, to punish it was not necessarily wrong. Yet the gentleman regards Song as culpable, saying [?] that righteousness was at stake. When the Xi clan [?] committed treason in Chen, Song let it pass, whereas Chu was able to punish it. Though Chu’s conversion of Chen into a county certainly displayed its brute strength, the favor it bestowed by restoring Chen as a fief cannot be effaced either. Chen’s offense was insufficient grounds for reproach.

Had Song been able to examine its own virtue inwardly, I believe that, after nurturing its power and conserving its strength, it surely could have quietly overcome Chen’s inclination to attach itself to an outside power. Why neglect its own cultivation and reproach others alone? When sounding bells and beating drums, what offense of Chen’s could it proclaim? When appointing commanders and sending out chariots, it had no justification to invoke. This was surely to provoke an immediate quarrel and thereby invite a lifetime of trouble. That Song’s ancestral temples and altars of state were eventually besieged was foreshadowed in this expedition. The Analects says: “The gentleman takes righteousness as his substance.” How could Song deserve to be spoken of in these terms?

As for Chen, suffering at Song’s hands despite being innocent, the invaders at its gates were a danger it ought to resist. For Wei to go to its rescue as a friendly state was hardly without merit. Yet the gentleman regards this as a failing, saying that good faith was at stake. Jin had established the covenant at Qing…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
立之盟宋實成之衛則助之牲歃之口血未乾
詔神之約言猶在其好不可棄也衛能弗貳其
志吾見偕謀恊筭之下能不益崇夫中國之體
乎柰何變詐是圖訂盟輙渝悉索車賦拯彼即
異之邦爰及干戈撓我尚同之國是徒矯能救
之名而適以激人之怒卒之追咎于臣竟何所
補也傳曰君子以信易生衛曷足以知此春秋
於宋伐之下而書衛救所以責宋而衛人之失
亦見矣雖然亦慨當時之無霸也晉景紹文襄
之後為中國霸主乃坐視陳亂遺義于夷而使
之獲以藉口及陳鄭交貳又復任用非人喪師
黷信一切可耻無或乎小弱者弗以自存強詐
者轉相師效也故先正曰有霸非美名無霸非
細故其所以待衰世之語者至是益驗
禮記
清廟之瑟朱絃而疏越壹倡而三歎有遺
音者矣
葉棒
punctuated:
立之盟，宋實成之，衛則助之。牲歃之口血未乾，詔神之約言猶在，其好不可棄也。衛能弗貳其志，吾見偕謀恊筭之下，能不益崇夫中國之體乎？柰何變詐是圖，訂盟輙渝，悉索車賦，拯彼即異之邦，爰及干戈，撓我尚同之國？是徒矯能救之名，而適以激人之怒，卒之追咎于臣，竟何所補也？傳曰：「君子以信易生。」衛曷足以知此？春秋於宋伐之下而書衛救，所以責宋，而衛人之失亦見矣。雖然，亦慨當時之無霸也。晉景紹文襄之後，為中國霸主，乃坐視陳亂，遺義于夷，而使之獲以藉口。及陳鄭交貳，又復任用非人，喪師黷信，一切可耻。無或乎小弱者弗以自存，強詐者轉相師效也。故先正曰：「有霸非美名，無霸非細故。」其所以待衰世之語者，至是益驗。

禮記

清廟之瑟，朱絃而疏越，壹倡而三歎，有遺音者矣。

葉棒
translation_en:
…the covenant at Qingli [?]: Song indeed brought it about, and Wei assisted. The blood from the sacrificial oath had not yet dried upon their lips, and the sworn words proclaimed to the spirits still stood; their amity could not be abandoned. Had Wei remained undivided in its purpose, I believe that their joint deliberations and coordinated plans would surely have further enhanced the standing of the central states. Why, then, did it pursue deceit and treachery, repeatedly breaking the covenant it had concluded, levying all its chariot forces to rescue a state that had sided with outsiders, and resorting to arms to harass a state that upheld their common allegiance? This merely claimed the reputation of being able to bring rescue, while serving only to provoke others’ anger. In the end, what good did it do to lay the blame retrospectively upon a minister? The Commentary says: “The gentleman gives up his life to preserve good faith.” How could Wei have understood this? By recording Wei’s rescue immediately after Song’s attack, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures Song while also revealing the fault of the men of Wei.

Yet one must also lament the absence of a hegemon at that time. Duke Jing of Jin succeeded Dukes Wen and Xiang as hegemon of the central states, yet he sat by and watched the disorder in Chen, leaving the performance of righteousness to the outsiders and allowing them to use it as a justification for their actions. When Chen and Zheng both became disloyal, he again appointed unsuitable men, lost his army, and dishonored good faith: all of this was shameful. It is no wonder that the small and weak could not preserve themselves, while the strong and deceitful took turns emulating one another. Thus a former worthy said: “Having a hegemon brings no glorious name; having none is no small matter.” These words concerning an age of decline [?] are all the more clearly borne out here.

Record of Rites

“The se zithers in the Pure Temple have red silk strings and widely spaced sound holes. One voice leads, and three respond: there is a lingering resonance.”

Ye Bang 葉棒

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正孫　批〔詞旨淡而不厭宛然古樂當〕
〔自得於知音者〕
考試官學正顏　批〔古樂質素而有遺音極難模寫〕
〔此作只平平寫去而趣味之妙溢於言表讀之當亦有遺音〕
〔也〕
記者論古樂雖不著其妙自不盡其妙蓋古樂
之妙固有出於聲音之外者也於是語樂可以
知先王制作之本矣且君子之德固備於知樂
而言樂之隆不在於極音彼清廟之詩德音之
===
致者也以是詩而被諸瑟謂非樂之隆者乎是
故文之以瑟將清越以長之是工也清廟之瑟
則練朱絲以爲絃而使其聲之濁渾厚和平一
冲以澹焉瑟以和之將徑出而直之是求也清
廟之瑟則疏其底以爲越而使其聲之遲從容
和緩不輕以疾焉秘至文於大朴蘊極美於優
柔是特質素之聲焉耳是聲也初發之際倡和
宜有應也然一人倡之三人和之寥寥僅見其
相從何有於迭和之盛登歌之頃比合宜有人
punctuated:
考試官學正孫批〔詞旨淡而不厭，宛然古樂，當自得於知音者。〕

考試官學正顏批〔古樂質素而有遺音，極難模寫。此作只平平寫去，而趣味之妙溢於言表，讀之當亦有遺音也。〕

記者論古樂，雖不著其妙，自不盡其妙。蓋古樂之妙，固有出於聲音之外者也。於是語樂，可以知先王制作之本矣。且君子之德固備於知樂，而言樂之隆，不在於極音。彼清廟之詩，德音之致者也。以是詩而被諸瑟，謂非樂之隆者乎？是故文之以瑟，將清越以長之，是工也。清廟之瑟，則練朱絲以爲絃，而使其聲之濁，渾厚和平，一冲以澹焉。瑟以和之，將徑出而直之，是求也。清廟之瑟，則疏其底以爲越，而使其聲之遲，從容和緩，不輕以疾焉。秘至文於大朴，蘊極美於優柔，是特質素之聲焉耳。是聲也，初發之際，倡和宜有應也。然一人倡之，三人和之，寥寥僅見其相從，何有於迭和之盛？登歌之頃，比合宜有人
translation_en:
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and purport are restrained yet never wearying, just like ancient music. Those who understand its tones will surely appreciate it for themselves.〕

Examiner Yan, Instructor, comments: 〔Ancient music is plain and unadorned, yet possesses lingering resonance: this is exceedingly difficult to portray. This composition proceeds in an entirely plain manner, yet its exquisite flavor overflows beyond the words. Reading it, one should likewise find a lingering resonance.〕

The compiler of the Record discusses ancient music: although he does not explicitly reveal its subtle excellence, neither does he exhaust it. For the subtle excellence of ancient music assuredly includes something beyond sound itself. From this discussion of music, one can understand the foundation of the former kings’ institutions. Moreover, the gentleman’s virtue is indeed brought to completeness through understanding music; yet musical excellence does not consist in taking sound to its utmost limits. The ode “Pure Temple” (Qing miao) represents the consummation of virtuous sound. When this ode is accompanied on the se zither, could one say that it is not the height of music?

Thus, when embellishing it with the se, to make the sound clear and far-reaching and thereby prolong it would be considered skillful. But the se of the Pure Temple uses prepared red silk for its strings, making its sound deep, full, harmonious, and peaceful, wholly serene and restrained. When using the se to harmonize with the singing, to make the sound issue directly and proceed straight forth [?] would be the aim. But the se of the Pure Temple has widely spaced sound holes in its underside, making its sound slow, unhurried, harmonious, and gentle, without frivolity or haste. It conceals the highest refinement within great simplicity and holds supreme beauty within gentleness. This is merely a plain, unadorned sound.

When this sound first arises, one would expect a response between the leading voice and those joining it. Yet one person leads and three join in: so sparse are they that one barely perceives their following one another. Where is the abundance of successive responses? During the singing in the hall, there should be people joining in harmony …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也然作之者一而歎之者三落落無聞其相應
何有於雜比之隆要妙無取乎世俗鏗鏘不愜
于衆庶謂非貭素之聲可乎若然宜若不足於
古樂者殊不知英華雖未發也而和順之中積
者自洋溢於器數之外傾聽之自有餘音者存
探之而不窮也味之而不厭也其感通之幾真
可以平天下之情而移其風者矣詎可得而盡
之耶文釆雖不省也而神明之内藴者自充盎
於節奏之表細玩之自有遺響者在若抑而實
===
揚也若晦而實光也其絪緼之妙真可以復人
道之正而易其俗者矣又可得而盡之耶蓋至
樂無聲而天下以和大樂雖易而百物以化樂
之隆固有所主而可事於聲音求哉抑此非獨
見之言也孔子曰樂云樂云鍾皷云乎哉至周
子之論古樂則一以淡爲主蓋樂有道有器有
本有文後世不揣其本惟從事于奸聲淫樂之
末以飾治具至於古聖王所以養性情和上下
而宣化焉者畧不加之意以魏文侯之賢聽古
punctuated:
也。然作之者一，而歎之者三，落落無聞其相應，何有於雜比之隆？要妙無取乎世俗，鏗鏘不愜于衆庶，謂非貭素之聲可乎？若然，宜若不足於古樂者。殊不知英華雖未發也，而和順之中積者，自洋溢於器數之外。傾聽之，自有餘音者存，探之而不窮也，味之而不厭也。其感通之幾，真可以平天下之情而移其風者矣，詎可得而盡之耶？文釆雖不省也，而神明之内藴者，自充盎於節奏之表。細玩之，自有遺響者在，若抑而實揚也，若晦而實光也。其絪緼之妙，真可以復人道之正而易其俗者矣，又可得而盡之耶？
蓋至樂無聲，而天下以和；大樂雖易，而百物以化。樂之隆固有所主，而可事於聲音求哉？抑此非獨見之言也。孔子曰：「樂云樂云，鍾皷云乎哉？」至周子之論古樂，則一以淡爲主。蓋樂有道有器，有本有文。後世不揣其本，惟從事于奸聲淫樂之末，以飾治具。至於古聖王所以養性情、和上下而宣化焉者，畧不加之意。以魏文侯之賢，聽古
translation_en:
…Yet one person begins the song and three respond; so sparse are they that their mutual responses are scarcely heard. Where is the fullness of voices joining in varied combinations? Its subtle refinement offers nothing to popular taste, and its ringing tones do not please the multitude. Can one deny that these are sounds of unadorned simplicity? If so, ancient music might seem deficient. What is not understood is that, although its brilliance has not yet unfolded, the harmony and accord accumulated within overflow beyond its instruments and prescribed forms. Listen intently, and lingering tones remain: explore them and they are inexhaustible; savor them and they never cloy. The subtle impulse by which they move people and elicit a response can truly bring the feelings of all under Heaven into equilibrium and transform their prevailing ways. How could its effects ever be exhausted? Although its ornamentation is not apparent [?], the spiritual illumination stored within brims over beyond its rhythms. Attend to it closely, and echoes remain: seemingly restrained, it actually rises; seemingly obscure, it actually shines. The subtle wonder of its intermingling influences can truly restore human relationships to their proper order and transform customary practices. How, again, could its effects ever be exhausted?
For the highest music is soundless, yet through it all under Heaven attain harmony; great music is simple, yet through it the myriad things are transformed. The excellence of music assuredly has its essential foundation: can it be sought merely through attention to sounds? Nor is this merely an opinion peculiar to me. Confucius said: “Music, music—is it merely bells and drums?” When Master Zhou discussed ancient music, he likewise took mildness as its sole guiding principle. Music has its Way and its instruments, its root and its embellishment. Later generations failed to consider its root, attending only to such superficial things as corrupt sounds and licentious music to adorn the apparatus of government. They gave no thought at all to how the sage kings of antiquity nurtured human nature and feelings, harmonized those above and below, and spread their transforming influence. Even one as worthy as Marquis Wen of Wei, when listening to ancient…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
樂而猶恐卧則夫溺於刹欲如齊宣者無怪乎
好俗樂而不知倦也噫齊宣不足道也而文侯
亦為之愚以是益知鄭聲之惑人也甚矣
君子也者人之成名也百姓歸之名謂之
君子之子是使其親為君子也是為成
其親之名也已
賀梧
考試官學正孫　批〔君子成親之義當如此講〕
考試官學正顏　批〔題本正大冠冕而畧無傳註可〕
===
〔據場中作者不失之拘則涉於泛不滯於晦則雜於冗此〕
〔篇理既明白而詞又足以暢之盖深潜而有得者録之可〕
〔以式後學矣〕
人君成已之譽因以隆親之譽焉夫顯親莫大
於揚名也人君成已譽而致親譽之隆可謂能
成其親矣孔子告哀公之意如此謂夫人之有
身皆本於其親而親之成名每繫於其子彼名
之所重莫過於君子也君子之名豈易成哉必
善有諸已而後君子之名始全一有闕焉則名
punctuated:
樂而猶恐卧，則夫溺於刹欲如齊宣者，無怪乎好俗樂而不知倦也。噫！齊宣不足道也，而文侯亦為之愚，以是益知鄭聲之惑人也甚矣。
君子也者，人之成名也。百姓歸之名，謂之君子之子，是使其親為君子也，是為成其親之名也已。
賀梧
考試官學正孫　批〔君子成親之義，當如此講。〕
考試官學正顏　批〔題本正大冠冕，而畧無傳註可〕〔據。場中作者，不失之拘則涉於泛，不滯於晦則雜於冗。此〕〔篇理既明白，而詞又足以暢之，盖深潜而有得者。録之，可〕〔以式後學矣。〕
人君成已之譽，因以隆親之譽焉。夫顯親莫大於揚名也，人君成已譽而致親譽之隆，可謂能成其親矣。孔子告哀公之意如此，謂夫人之有身，皆本於其親，而親之成名，每繫於其子。彼名之所重，莫過於君子也。君子之名，豈易成哉？必善有諸已，而後君子之名始全；一有闕焉，則名
translation_en:
…yet even he feared falling asleep when listening to this music. Thus, when someone like King Xuan of Qi is immersed in desires [?], it is no wonder that he delights in popular music and never tires of it. Alas! King Xuan of Qi is scarcely worth discussing, yet even Marquis Wen was beguiled by it. This makes all the clearer how profoundly the music of Zheng deludes people.
“‘Gentleman’ is a designation marking a person's full moral achievement. When the common people accord him this designation and call him ‘the son of a gentleman,’ this makes his parent a gentleman: it is thereby that he completes his parent's good name.”
He Wu
Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: 〔This is how the meaning of a gentleman's completing his parent's good name should be expounded.〕
Examiner Yan, School Instructor, comments: 〔The topic is inherently upright, grand, and dignified, yet there is scarcely any commentary on which to rely. Candidates writing in the examination hall either err through constraint or stray into generalities; either become mired in obscurity or encumber their writing with verbosity. In this essay, the reasoning is clear, and the language fully conveys it. Its author has evidently reflected deeply and gained understanding. Recording it can provide a model for later students.〕
The ruler establishes his own good reputation and thereby enhances that of his parents. Nothing brings greater distinction to one's parents than making one's name renowned. A ruler who establishes his own good reputation and thus elevates his parents' reputation may be said to have fulfilled his duty of bringing them to distinction. Such is the meaning of Confucius's words to Duke Ai: everyone's existence originates in their parents, while the establishment of the parents' good name often depends upon their child. Among esteemed designations, none surpasses “gentleman.” Can the name of gentleman be easily attained? Only when one possesses goodness within oneself does one's claim to the name of gentleman become complete. Once there is any deficiency, then that name…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
隨以隳矣敬以成身而後君子之實始副少有
失焉則人得而議矣君子非人之成名乎誠能
言不過辭足以為斯人之表率動不過則有以
聳百姓之觀瞻將見雜閭閻而居有所謂市井
之臣也感君之德化者莫不曰吾君之賢若是
殆君子之徧祚歟涵養於儲貳之既深而繼承
乎今日之至善不命而民敬恭無遠近焉環提
封而治有所謂草莽之臣也樂君之治安者莫
不曰幸哉有子如此其世德之流衍歟訓迪於
===
義方之有素而嗣續乎厥後之休美弗命而民
聽上無衆寡焉夫身者親之枝也子既為君子
之子則親為君子之父蓋不獨身享其名而稱
揚之顧固及其所自矣不但已專其善而歆慕
之誠且本其所生矣不使其親為君子耶由是
聞望騰播於四方貽謀燕翼自此其不朽乎聲
名洋溢於中國父作子述至是其有徵乎君子
成親之名如此人君敬身之功孰有大於是哉
嘗因是而考之此即武王周公之達孝也纘先
punctuated:
隨以隳矣。敬以成身，而後君子之實始副；少有失焉，則人得而議矣。君子非人之成名乎？誠能言不過辭，足以為斯人之表率；動不過則，有以聳百姓之觀瞻。將見雜閭閻而居，有所謂市井之臣也，感君之德化者莫不曰：「吾君之賢若是，殆君子之徧祚歟！」涵養於儲貳之既深，而繼承乎今日之至善，不命而民敬，恭無遠近焉。環提封而治，有所謂草莽之臣也，樂君之治安者莫不曰：「幸哉，有子如此，其世德之流衍歟！」訓迪於義方之有素，而嗣續乎厥後之休美，弗命而民聽，上無衆寡焉。夫身者，親之枝也。子既為君子之子，則親為君子之父。蓋不獨身享其名，而稱揚之顧固及其所自矣；不但已專其善，而歆慕之誠且本其所生矣。不使其親為君子耶？由是聞望騰播於四方，貽謀燕翼，自此其不朽乎？聲名洋溢於中國，父作子述，至是其有徵乎？君子成親之名如此，人君敬身之功，孰有大於是哉？
嘗因是而考之，此即武王、周公之達孝也。纘先
translation_en:
…his reputation consequently falls into ruin. Only after reverently perfecting himself does he begin to live up to the substance of a gentleman; should he fall short even slightly, others will have grounds to criticize him. Is not “gentleman” the consummate designation a person can attain? If indeed his speech never exceeds what is fitting, he can serve as an example to the people; if his actions never transgress the rules, he can inspire awe among the watching populace. Then one will see those who dwell amid the lanes and neighborhoods—the so-called subjects of the marketplaces—all moved by their ruler’s transforming virtue and saying: “Our ruler is so worthy! Surely this is the widespread blessing of a gentleman [?]!” Having been deeply nurtured while heir apparent, he succeeds today to the highest goodness. Without being commanded, the people show reverence; near and far alike, they are respectful. Throughout the territory under his governance, those called subjects of the countryside, delighting in their ruler’s peaceful government, will all say: “How fortunate to have such a son! Surely this is the continuing flow of his family’s virtue!” Long instructed in the ways of righteousness, he carries forward their excellence in succeeding generations. Without being commanded, the people obey; whether many or few, they honor their superior.
A person is a branch of his parents. Once the son is a son who is a gentleman, his parent becomes the father of a gentleman. Thus he does not enjoy this reputation alone: the regard expressed in praise necessarily extends to those from whom he came. Nor does he possess this goodness exclusively: the sincere admiration it inspires also traces back to those who gave him life. Does this not cause his parent to be regarded as a gentleman? Thereupon his renown spreads throughout the four quarters. Through plans bequeathed to bring peace and support to his descendants, will his parent not henceforth be immortal? His fame overflows throughout the Central Kingdom. The father initiates and the son carries on: is this not now borne out? Such is the way a gentleman completes his parent’s good name. What achievement of a ruler’s reverent cultivation of himself could be greater than this?
Reflecting on this, I have found it to be precisely the universally acknowledged filial piety of King Wu and the Duke of Zhou. Carrying forward their forebears’ …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
世之緒成文武之德宗周之祀至於八百餘年
而人猶思慕之所謂能敬其身以成其親者非
耶抑此特為君人者發耳傳曰立身行道揚名
於後世以顯父母蓋自天子以至於庶人莫不
有親而達道之在天下不以貴賤而或殊使哀
公能因是而致力焉雖舉而措之天下無難矣
惜乎簡切之言不足以悟寘煩之心也
第貳場
論
===
君志定而天下之治成
張勛
同考試官教諭費 批 論題甚冠冕場中作者
援筆類能滿紙然與題意率無關涉披閱甚
厭人意晚得此卷立意奇特而用詞雅徤疊
疊千餘言神采煥發無一字蹈襲陳語蓋學古
而有得者貢之
天府倘備
乙夜之覽必大有啓心之助者予豈但為江右文士而已耶
punctuated:
世之緒，成文武之德，宗周之祀至於八百餘年，而人猶思慕之。所謂能敬其身以成其親者，非耶？抑此特為君人者發耳。傳曰：「立身行道，揚名於後世，以顯父母。」蓋自天子以至於庶人，莫不有親，而達道之在天下，不以貴賤而或殊。使哀公能因是而致力焉，雖舉而措之天下，無難矣。惜乎！簡切之言，不足以悟寘煩之心也。
第貳場
論
君志定而天下之治成
張勛
同考試官教諭費批：論題甚冠冕，場中作者援筆類能滿紙，然與題意率無關涉，披閱甚厭人意。晚得此卷，立意奇特，而用詞雅徤，疊疊千餘言，神采煥發，無一字蹈襲陳語，蓋學古而有得者。貢之天府，倘備乙夜之覽，必大有啓心之助者。予豈但為江右文士而已耶？
translation_en:
…the legacy of preceding generations, bringing to completion the virtue of Kings Wen and Wu. The ancestral sacrifices of the Zhou royal house continued for more than eight hundred years, and people still thought of them with longing. Is this not what is meant by reverently attending to one's own conduct so as to bring fulfillment to one's parents? Yet these remarks were addressed specifically to rulers. The transmitted text says: “Establish oneself, practice the Way, and make one's name known to later generations, thereby bringing glory to one's parents.” From the Son of Heaven down to the common people, everyone has parents; the universal Way throughout the world does not differ according to high or low status. Had Duke Ai devoted himself to this teaching, he would have had no difficulty extending it to all under Heaven. Alas! Such concise and pointed words could not awaken a mind encumbered with vexations [?].
Second Session
Discourse
“When the Ruler's Purpose Is Settled, Order throughout the Realm Is Achieved”
Zhang Xun
Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: The topic of this discourse is most dignified. Most candidates in the examination could take up their brushes and fill their papers, yet their writing generally had no bearing on the meaning of the topic. Reading through them was exceedingly tiresome. Late in the process I came upon this paper. Its conception is distinctive, and its language elegant and vigorous. Through its successive passages, amounting to more than a thousand words, its spirit shines forth; not a single word falls back upon stale expressions. Its author has evidently learned from antiquity and gained real understanding. I submit it to the imperial court. Should it be included in His Majesty's nighttime reading, it will surely contribute greatly to enlightening the imperial mind. Could I be acting merely for the men of letters of Jiangyou?

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭丁　批　〔議論縱橫皆自胷中流出未復以神宗用安石爲據學識兩到殆非拘拘於〕
〔數舉者取之不但以其文也〕
考試官學正孫　批　〔此題不難於敷衍而難於切實場中作者泛濫無序殊失本旨歛華就〕
〔實而辭氣莊栗僅見此篇觀者寧不爲之起敬〕
考試官學正顏　批　〔立意正大用語精深論場〕
〔孰能出其右〕
===
人主一念之天其萬化之所從出者乎夫
君天下之主也而其心則萬化之原也心
之所之謂之志定其志則所謂一念之天
也天下萬化豈復有外此者乎是蓋至約
也而能施博至簡也而能御煩至寡也而
能服衆人主於此果何道以得之亦惟稽
古正學以明此心之天使善惡之歸忠邪
之分曉然不昧於所趨則本然之天以復
萬化之原以正天下之治固猶影響之於
形聲有不期而自至者矣否則志慮□□
punctuated:
同考試官教諭丁，批：〔議論縱橫，皆自胷中流出，未復以神宗用安石爲據。學識兩到，殆非拘拘於〕〔數舉者。取之不但以其文也。〕

考試官學正孫，批：〔此題不難於敷衍，而難於切實。場中作者泛濫無序，殊失本旨。歛華就〕〔實，而辭氣莊栗，僅見此篇。觀者寧不爲之起敬？〕

考試官學正顏，批：〔立意正大，用語精深，論場〕〔孰能出其右？〕

人主一念之天，其萬化之所從出者乎？夫君，天下之主也，而其心則萬化之原也。心之所之謂之志，定其志，則所謂一念之天也。天下萬化，豈復有外此者乎？是蓋至約也，而能施博；至簡也，而能御煩；至寡也，而能服衆。人主於此，果何道以得之？亦惟稽古正學，以明此心之天，使善惡之歸、忠邪之分，曉然不昧於所趨，則本然之天以復，萬化之原以正。天下之治，固猶影響之於形聲，有不期而自至者矣。否則志慮□□
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor, comments: “The argument ranges freely, flowing entirely from the writer’s own breast, without again invoking Shenzong’s employment of Wang Anshi as evidence. Both learning and discernment are fully realized; this is hardly someone narrowly confined to a few instances [?]. We select him for more than his writing alone.”

Examiner Sun, Director of Studies, comments: “The difficulty of this topic lies not in elaborating it, but in treating it concretely. Writers in the examination hall ranged broadly without order, departing far from its fundamental purport. Only this essay restrains ornament in favor of substance while maintaining a solemn and dignified tone. Could any reader fail to feel respect?”

Examiner Yan, Director of Studies, comments: “Its conception is upright and elevated, its language precise and profound. Among those writing discourses in the examination hall, who could surpass it?”

Is not the Heaven present in a single thought of the ruler the source from which all transformations proceed? The sovereign is the master of all under Heaven, and his mind is the source of all transformations. That toward which the mind moves is called the will. When he fixes his will, this is what is meant by Heaven within a single thought. Could any transformation in the world lie outside this? It is supremely concentrated, yet its application can be broad; supremely simple, yet it can govern complexity; supremely few, yet it can bring the multitude into submission. By what means, then, can the ruler attain this? Only by examining antiquity and rectifying his learning, thereby illuminating the Heaven within this mind. He must clearly understand where good and evil lead and the distinction between loyalty and perversity, remaining undeluded about the course to follow. Then his original Heaven is restored, and the source of all transformations is rectified. Order throughout the realm will follow of itself, without being sought, just as a shadow follows a form and an echo follows a sound. Otherwise, his aims and deliberations [two illegible characters] …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
事愈廢神愈勞而事愈隳欲治化之成其
可得哉程子曰君志定而天下之治成可
謂善告君者矣且天下若彼其大也人君
以一身而主之三綱欲其正九疇欲其叙
百度欲其貞萬目欲其舉鰥寡孤獨者之
欲有養剛柔善惡者之欲易其惡至其中
飛潜動植之欲得其所九夷八蠻之欲賓
貢山嶽河海之欲奠安三光寒暑之欲順
其序而不愆若此者皆所謂治也然而人
===
主之志欲於一掬之間而發於一念之微
即之無端也體之無象也顧欲成其治於
天下不亦難乎自其難而求其易是必有
道矣蓋人主一念之發雖甚微而本然之
天則甚大况天下之事萬有不同而皆根
於一特患人主志之不一耳能一其志則
動皆以天所謂復德之本恒德之固矣豈
不足以萃萬於一而成其治也哉譬之水
焉千流萬派而皆沛然東注者源之一也
punctuated: 事愈廢，神愈勞，而事愈隳，欲治化之成，其可得哉？程子曰：「君志定而天下之治成。」可謂善告君者矣。且天下若彼其大也，人君以一身而主之，三綱欲其正，九疇欲其叙，百度欲其貞，萬目欲其舉，鰥寡孤獨者之欲有養，剛柔善惡者之欲易其惡，至其中飛潜動植之欲得其所，九夷八蠻之欲賓貢，山嶽河海之欲奠安，三光寒暑之欲順其序而不愆。若此者，皆所謂治也。然而人主之志欲於一掬之間，而發於一念之微，即之無端也，體之無象也，顧欲成其治於天下，不亦難乎？自其難而求其易，是必有道矣。蓋人主一念之發雖甚微，而本然之天則甚大。况天下之事萬有不同，而皆根於一，特患人主志之不一耳。能一其志，則動皆以天，所謂「復，德之本；恒，德之固」矣。豈不足以萃萬於一，而成其治也哉？譬之水焉，千流萬派，而皆沛然東注者，源之一也。
translation_en:
…affairs become ever more neglected, the spirit ever more wearied, and affairs fall ever further into ruin. Could successful government and moral transformation possibly be achieved? Master Cheng said: “When the ruler’s resolve is settled, order throughout the realm is achieved.” He may indeed be called one who knew how to counsel a ruler well.

Moreover, vast as the realm is, its ruler presides over it in his single person. He wishes the Three Bonds to be set right, the Nine Categories to be duly ordered, the hundred institutions to be correct, and the myriad particulars of administration to be carried out. He wishes widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless elderly to receive support, and people of firm or yielding disposition, good or evil, to reform whatever evil they possess. He wishes even the creatures that fly or swim, animals and plants, to find their proper places; the Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples to come as guests bearing tribute; the mountains, rivers, and seas to be settled and secure; and the three luminaries—the sun, moon, and stars—and the cold and heat to follow their proper sequence without deviation. All these things constitute what is called good government.

Yet the ruler’s resolve and desires reside within a mere handful of space [?], issuing in the subtlety of a single thought. Seek them, and they have no discernible beginning; try to give them bodily form, and they have no visible shape. To wish nevertheless to bring order to the realm through them—is this not difficult? There must surely be a way to seek ease within this difficulty. For although the arising of a single thought in the ruler is exceedingly subtle, the Heaven inherent in his nature is exceedingly vast. Moreover, although the affairs of the realm differ in myriad ways, they are all rooted in unity. The sole concern is that the ruler’s resolve may lack unity. If he can unify his resolve, all his actions will accord with Heaven. This is what is meant by “Return is the root of virtue; Constancy is the firmness of virtue.” Would this not suffice to gather the myriad into the one and bring about good government? Take water as an analogy: its thousand streams and myriad branches all flow abundantly eastward because their source is one.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
譬之木焉千柯萬葉而皆森然聳秀者本
之一也人主之志其水之源而木之本乎
然所謂定者抑豈强制之哉又豈寘然無
所為哉蓋必有以精密博大之見而後謂之
定有貞確果毅之守而後謂之定有純粹
悠久之道而後謂之定見不定則耳目之
好皆得以奪之守不定則讒諂之徒皆得
以眩之道不定則駁雜之政因循之論皆
得以間之而吾一念之天幾為人欲之所
===
汩矣人主於此盡亦慮之審而養之豫乎
是故非學無以明理非稽古無以正學理
不明則析義未真而無的然之見學不正
則信善未篤而無卓然之守由是貿貿焉
莫知所之而道非其道矣故必誠意正心
以立其本擇善固執以踐其實五帝之所
以帝三王之所以王吾皆稽其德以為進
脩之資五霸之所以霸後世之所以雜吾
皆考其跡以為勸戒之助善惡之歸不明
punctuated: 譬之木焉，千柯萬葉而皆森然聳秀者，本之一也。人主之志，其水之源而木之本乎？然所謂定者，抑豈强制之哉？又豈寘然無所為哉？蓋必有以精密博大之見而後謂之定，有貞確果毅之守而後謂之定，有純粹悠久之道而後謂之定。見不定，則耳目之好皆得以奪之；守不定，則讒諂之徒皆得以眩之；道不定，則駁雜之政、因循之論皆得以間之，而吾一念之天幾為人欲之所汩矣。人主於此，盡亦慮之審而養之豫乎？是故非學無以明理，非稽古無以正學。理不明，則析義未真而無的然之見；學不正，則信善未篤而無卓然之守。由是貿貿焉，莫知所之，而道非其道矣。故必誠意正心以立其本，擇善固執以踐其實。五帝之所以帝，三王之所以王，吾皆稽其德以為進脩之資；五霸之所以霸，後世之所以雜，吾皆考其跡以為勸戒之助。善惡之歸不明
translation_en:
Compare this to a tree: its thousand branches and myriad leaves all rise in luxuriant splendor because its root is one. Is the ruler’s resolve not like the source of water and the root of a tree? Yet does what we call being settled mean forcibly constraining it? Or does it mean leaving it alone and doing nothing? Only with understanding that is precise and comprehensive may it be called settled; only with adherence that is steadfast, resolute, and firm may it be called settled; only with a Way that is pure and enduring may it be called settled. If understanding is unsettled, everything that pleases the ears and eyes can divert it. If adherence is unsettled, slanderers and flatterers can bewilder it. If the Way is unsettled, inconsistent policies and arguments for merely following precedent can intrude upon it, until the heavenly principle within one’s single thought is all but submerged by human desires. Should the ruler not [?] deliberate carefully upon this and nurture his resolve beforehand?

Thus, without learning there is no means of illuminating principle; without examining antiquity there is no means of rectifying learning. If principle is not clear, one’s analysis of what is right will lack accuracy, and one will have no definite understanding. If learning is not correct, one’s faith in goodness will lack conviction, and one will have no firm adherence. Consequently, one proceeds in bewilderment, not knowing where to go, and one’s Way ceases to be the proper Way. One must therefore make one’s intentions sincere and rectify one’s mind to establish the foundation, choosing what is good and holding firmly to it to put it into practice. As for what enabled the Five Emperors to be emperors and the Three Kings to be kings, I examine all their virtues as resources for advancing my self-cultivation. As for what enabled the Five Hegemons to become hegemons and caused later ages to mix disparate approaches, I examine all their deeds as aids to encouragement and admonition. If the outcomes of good and evil are not clear…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
則志容有所感吾從而審之天理人欲之
幾瞭然矣忠邪之分不辨則志容有所偏
吾從而察之君子小人之用判然矣老成
之士所以輔吾志者也吾惟尊禮之而不
勞之以細務宴安之事所以害吾志者也
吾惟儆戒之而不忽之於漸習若然則耳
目之好舉不足以奪其志而吾之所見以
定讒諂之徒舉不足以眩其志而吾之所
守以定後世駁雜之政流俗因循之論舉
===
不足以間其志而吾之所道者以定人主
於此蓋有以純乎天而不汨之以人其猶
水之止而木之靜矣乎將見念慮所加有
以妙夫過化存神之機政事所出可以致
夫綏來動和之盛三綱以正九疇以叙百
度以貞萬目以舉鰥寡孤獨者之皆有養
剛柔善惡者之皆易其惡至其中飛潛動
植者之皆遂其生適其性九夷八蠻無不
賓貢山嶽河海無不奠安三光寒暑無不
punctuated: 則志容有所感，吾從而審之，天理人欲之幾瞭然矣。忠邪之分不辨，則志容有所偏，吾從而察之，君子小人之用判然矣。老成之士，所以輔吾志者也，吾惟尊禮之，而不勞之以細務；宴安之事，所以害吾志者也，吾惟儆戒之，而不忽之於漸習。若然，則耳目之好舉不足以奪其志，而吾之所見以定；讒諂之徒舉不足以眩其志，而吾之所守以定；後世駁雜之政、流俗因循之論舉不足以間其志，而吾之所道者以定。人主於此，蓋有以純乎天而不汨之以人，其猶水之止而木之靜矣乎！將見念慮所加，有以妙夫過化存神之機；政事所出，可以致夫綏來動和之盛。三綱以正，九疇以叙，百度以貞，萬目以舉。鰥寡孤獨者之皆有養，剛柔善惡者之皆易其惡，至其中飛潛動植者之皆遂其生、適其性。九夷八蠻無不賓貢，山嶽河海無不奠安，三光寒暑無不
translation_en:
…then the will may be swayed. I accordingly scrutinize the matter, and the subtle beginnings of heavenly principle and human desires become clear. If the distinction between loyalty and wickedness is not discerned, the will may become biased. I accordingly examine the matter, and the difference between employing gentlemen and employing petty men becomes plain. Mature and experienced men are those who support my resolve: I accord them honor and courtesy and do not burden them with petty duties. Ease and indulgence are things that injure my resolve: I remain vigilant against them and do not overlook the gradual formation of habits. If this is so, nothing that pleases the ears and eyes will suffice to deflect the ruler’s resolve, and my understanding will thereby become settled. No slanderers or flatterers will suffice to bewilder his resolve, and the principles I uphold will thereby become settled. Neither the impure and mixed governance of later ages nor conventional arguments for simply following established practices will suffice to undermine his resolve, and the Way I follow will thereby become settled.

At this point, the ruler can surely attain purity in accord with Heaven, unclouded by human desires. Would he not be like still water and a tree at rest? We shall then see that, wherever his thoughts are directed, he can wondrously realize the workings of transformation wherever he passes and spiritual influence wherever he abides; and through the policies he issues, he can achieve the flourishing condition in which bringing peace draws people to him and his actions inspire harmony. The Three Bonds will be set right, the Nine Categories put in order, the hundred institutions made correct, and the myriad particulars carried into effect. Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless elderly will all receive support; the strong and the weak, the good and the bad, will all reform whatever is evil in them. Even the creatures that fly or swim, and all animals and plants within the realm, will fulfill their lives and find conditions suited to their natures. The Nine Yi and Eight Man peoples will all come as guests bearing tribute; the mountains, rivers, and seas will all be secured in tranquility; the three celestial lights—the sun, moon, and stars—and the cold and heat will all…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
順序而罔或愆天下之治已成矣謂之成
者造其極而無以加之詞也雖堯之時雍
舜之風動禹之四敷湯之允殖文武之咸
休亦不過此而區區五霸之功利後世之
雜霸雜夷者皆不足言矣向使人主之志
一有不定而徒瑣瑣於事為文具之末雖
欲致小康之治且難而況成天下之大治
乎蓋至是而真有以得夫守約而施博以
簡而御煩以寡而服衆之要矣雖然天下
之治固本於君志之定然其定亦有未易
===
言者蓋其居之以崇高養之以逸樂而便
辟左右之人又從臾於其前凡可欲之事
足以呈其巧而售其術者雜然日進以幸
其一中自非英明剛毅之資鮮有不為其
所移者而況能超然自力于學以致夫治
也哉程子上疏於神宗首以志定為言蓋
有以窺君之志矣觀其銳意圖治不事遊
畋若將大有所為率之任用非人力行新
punctuated:
順序而罔或愆，天下之治已成矣。謂之成者，造其極而無以加之詞也。雖堯之時雍、舜之風動、禹之四敷、湯之允殖、文武之咸休，亦不過此，而區區五霸之功利、後世之雜霸雜夷者，皆不足言矣。向使人主之志一有不定，而徒瑣瑣於事為文具之末，雖欲致小康之治且難，而況成天下之大治乎？蓋至是而真有以得夫守約而施博、以簡而御煩、以寡而服衆之要矣。
雖然，天下之治固本於君志之定，然其定亦有未易言者。蓋其居之以崇高，養之以逸樂，而便辟左右之人又從臾於其前，凡可欲之事足以呈其巧而售其術者，雜然日進，以幸其一中。自非英明剛毅之資，鮮有不為其所移者，而況能超然自力于學，以致夫治也哉？程子上疏於神宗，首以志定為言，蓋有以窺君之志矣。觀其銳意圖治，不事遊畋，若將大有所為，率之任用非人，力行新
translation_en:
…follow their proper sequence without any deviation, and order throughout the realm is fully achieved. To call it “fully achieved” means that it has reached its utmost point and nothing further can be added. Even the harmony of Yao’s age, the transforming influence of Shun, Yu’s virtue spreading to the four quarters, Tang’s firmly established virtue, and the universal blessings of Kings Wen and Wu went no further than this. The petty achievements and pursuit of advantage of the Five Hegemons, and the later admixtures of hegemonic methods and barbarian ways, are altogether unworthy of mention. If the ruler’s resolve were at all unsettled, and he merely busied himself with the minutiae of administrative activity and empty formalities, even attaining modest peace and order would be difficult. How much less could he bring about consummate order throughout the realm? Only upon reaching this point does he truly grasp the essentials of holding to what is fundamental while extending benefits widely, managing complexity through simplicity, and bringing the many into submission through the few.
Nevertheless, although order throughout the realm is indeed rooted in the firmness of the ruler’s resolve, securing that firmness is not so easily discussed. He occupies an exalted position and is nurtured in ease and pleasure, while flattering attendants around him further egg him on. Every desirable thing through which they can display their ingenuity and ply their devices is presented to him daily in a bewildering array, in the hope that one will hit its mark. Unless he possesses intelligence, discernment, firmness, and resolution, he will seldom escape being swayed by them. How much less can he rise above them and apply himself to learning, thereby bringing about good government? When Master Cheng submitted a memorial to Emperor Shenzong, he began by speaking of firmness of resolve, evidently having discerned the ruler’s intentions. Shenzong was keenly intent upon achieving good government and did not occupy himself with excursions and hunts, seemingly poised to accomplish great things. In the end, however, he employed the wrong men and vigorously implemented new…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
法海內翕然雖帝王之志定之學亦王安石
曲學偏見有以誤之也使神宗果能稽古
正學以任安石之志而任程子則必有聖
賢之學以為緝熙光明之地熙寧元豐之
治當必為唐虞三代之盛矣惜乎不足以
與此然則有天下之責者尚鑒茲哉
表
擬宋立崇文院群臣賀表〔太平興國三年〕
郭鵬
同考試官教諭張　批〔駢驪莊重可羨〕
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔考訂精確且與摭拾舊語者不〕
===
同宜錄以表多士
同考試官教諭楊　批〔語自胷中流出且得諷體錄之〕
考試官學正孫　批〔詞語清新得駢驪體佳士也〕
考試官學正顏　批〔語莊意到可嘉〕
太平興國三年某月日具官臣某等恭遇
宸命特立崇文院成者臣等誠歡誠忭稽首頓
首上言伏以
punctuated:
法，海內翕然。雖帝王之志定之學，亦王安石曲學偏見有以誤之也。使神宗果能稽古正學，以任安石之志而任程子，則必有聖賢之學，以為緝熙光明之地。熙寧元豐之治，當必為唐虞三代之盛矣。惜乎不足以與此！然則有天下之責者，尚鑒茲哉！

表
擬宋立崇文院群臣賀表〔太平興國三年〕
郭鵬
同考試官教諭張　批〔駢驪莊重，可羨。〕
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔考訂精確，且與摭拾舊語者不〕同，宜錄以表多士。
同考試官教諭楊　批〔語自胷中流出，且得諷體，錄之。〕
考試官學正孫　批〔詞語清新，得駢驪體，佳士也。〕
考試官學正顏　批〔語莊意到，可嘉。〕

太平興國三年某月日，具官臣某等，恭遇宸命特立崇文院成者。臣等誠歡誠忭，稽首頓首上言，伏以：
translation_en:
…laws, and all within the seas fell in line. Although he possessed an emperor’s resolve and the learning that steadies it [?], Wang Anshi’s distorted learning and biased views led him astray. Had Shenzong truly examined antiquity and pursued correct learning, employing Master Cheng with the same determination with which he employed Anshi, he would surely have had the learning of the sages and worthies as the foundation for ever-increasing enlightenment. The government of the Xining and Yuanfeng eras would surely have attained the flourishing condition of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and the Three Dynasties. Alas, he failed to attain this! Let those who bear responsibility for all under Heaven take warning from this!

Memorial
A Memorial of Congratulation by the Assembled Officials on the Establishment of the Chongwen Academy under the Song, Composed as an Examination Exercise 〔Third year of Taiping Xingguo [978]〕
Guo Peng

Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The parallel prose is dignified and worthy of admiration.”〕
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “The examination and verification of historical details are precise, and this differs from works that merely gather old phrases. It should be selected for inclusion as an example to the many candidates.”
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔“The words flow from his own breast, and he also achieves the manner of indirect admonition. Include it.”〕
Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: 〔“The diction is fresh and clear, and he has mastered the parallel-prose form. A fine scholar indeed.”〕
Examiner Yan, School Instructor, comments: 〔“The language is dignified and the meaning fully conveyed. Commendable.”〕

We, your servants, truly rejoice and exult; bowing our heads and knocking them upon the ground, we submit this memorial. We humbly submit that …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
棟宇巍峩韋竹萃群書之芳潤
丹青燦爛芸蓀霏至治之英華
六龍騰座右之輝萬水會源頭之大惟
聖人貴禮樂以淑家國斯治道不兵革而振華
夷一德孔良四方時憲虞韶偶奏喜食味
之忘齊周典俄陳章人文之寄魯宗孔教
綫存於顔逝慨秦焚緒墜於孟傳雖石渠
天祿僅收煨燼之餘而麟閣蘭臺尚乏治
平之鑑堂既高而廉斯遠臣日謟而君益
===
驕師章句者訓詁徒勤重詞華者支離彌
甚譬諸群飲詎測江河之深如彼墻窺未
見室家之好治不逺古事可規今恭惟
○○○○
識際道真
神凝聖域
金貞玉裕英姿天挺於穆清
雨施雲行至德日加於寰宇追
□□祖鳳崇儒術陋漢髙不事詩書以有獲非古
punctuated:
棟宇巍峩，韋竹萃群書之芳潤；丹青燦爛，芸蓀霏至治之英華。六龍騰座右之輝，萬水會源頭之大。惟聖人貴禮樂以淑家國，斯治道不兵革而振華夷。一德孔良，四方時憲。虞韶偶奏，喜食味之忘齊；周典俄陳，章人文之寄魯。宗孔教綫存於顔逝，慨秦焚緒墜於孟傳。雖石渠天祿僅收煨燼之餘，而麟閣蘭臺尚乏治平之鑑。堂既高而廉斯遠，臣日謟而君益驕。師章句者，訓詁徒勤；重詞華者，支離彌甚。譬諸群飲，詎測江河之深；如彼墻窺，未見室家之好。治不逺古，事可規今。
恭惟○○○○，識際道真，神凝聖域。金貞玉裕，英姿天挺於穆清；雨施雲行，至德日加於寰宇。追□□祖鳳崇儒術，陋漢髙不事詩書，以有獲非古
translation_en:
…The halls rise lofty and imposing; leather-bound bamboo texts gather the fragrance and richness of all books. Vermilion and blue shine brilliantly; fragrant rue and sweet flag diffuse the flowering excellence of consummate government. The six dragons send forth radiance beside the throne; myriad waters converge in the vastness of their source. The sage prizes rites and music to improve his household and realm; thus the way of government brings order to the Chinese lands and the outlying peoples without recourse to arms. His single virtue is most excellent, and the four quarters take it as their model. When the Shao music of Shun was played, delight made one forget the taste of food in Qi; when the institutions of Zhou were displayed, they revealed that civilized culture had found its home in Lu. Revering Confucius’s teaching, we see its thread barely surviving at Yan’s death [?]; lamenting the Qin burning of books, we see its continuity lost in the transmission from Meng [?]. Although the Shiqu and Tianlu libraries gathered only what remained of the ashes, the Qilin Pavilion and Orchid Terrace still lacked a mirror for orderly and peaceful government. As the hall grew higher, its edge became more remote: ministers grew daily more flattering, and rulers increasingly arrogant. Those who taught textual divisions and sentences labored vainly over glosses; those who valued literary ornament became ever more fragmented in their learning. Like people drinking together, how could they fathom the depths of rivers? Like someone peering through a wall, they had not seen the beauty of the rooms within. The government of antiquity is not far beyond reach; its precedents can guide the present.
We reverently consider Your Majesty [○○○○]: your understanding reaches the truth of the Way, and your spirit rests concentrated in the realm of sagehood. Firm as metal and generous as jade, your outstanding qualities rise by Heaven’s gift in the solemn purity of the court. Like falling rain and moving clouds, your supreme virtue daily extends throughout the world. You emulate □□祖鳳 [?] in honoring Confucian learning, and deem inferior Gaozu of Han’s neglect of the Odes and Documents, holding that attainment without ancient …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
訓不能而此心惟問學可養六庫之繙緗
既盛三館之輪奐復新西序雖宏稍妨披
閱便門載啓庶易
幸臨適吉壤之方虛正
帝心之簡在隣
昇龍以軒豁宜
駐蹕於頻繁爰命經營式新創作規模啓山
斗之基翬飛鳥革奎壁應圖書之府馬負
龜呈名冠
===
崇文實專稽古牙籤八萬卷珍藏移自于两
偏上下百千年掌故奚言乎東觀羅史子
集雄當紫電之標璀璨珠璣光動青藜之
照折衆言而俟聖開四府以法天宋規不
出於戶庭大道自登乎畔岸
堯謨帝訓燕貽克固本根孔思周情繩武罔
迷遠轍事關述作功倍表章臣等躬陽獻
曝幸一得之粗陳秋水望洋愧三冬之未
足心寔顒於賛頌辭莫罄於揄揚伏願
punctuated: 訓不能，而此心惟問學可養。六庫之繙緗既盛，三館之輪奐復新。西序雖宏，稍妨披閱；便門載啓，庶易幸臨。適吉壤之方虛，正帝心之簡在。隣昇龍以軒豁，宜駐蹕於頻繁。爰命經營，式新創作。規模啓山斗之基，翬飛鳥革；奎壁應圖書之府，馬負龜呈。名冠崇文，實專稽古。牙籤八萬卷，珍藏移自于两偏；上下百千年，掌故奚言乎東觀？羅史子集，雄當紫電之標；璀璨珠璣，光動青藜之照。折衆言而俟聖，開四府以法天。宋規不出於戶庭，大道自登乎畔岸。堯謨帝訓，燕貽克固本根；孔思周情，繩武罔迷遠轍。事關述作，功倍表章。臣等躬陽獻曝，幸一得之粗陳；秋水望洋，愧三冬之未足。心寔顒於賛頌，辭莫罄於揄揚。伏願
translation_en:
…teachings, one cannot accomplish it; and this mind can be nourished only through inquiry and learning. The opening of silk-bound books in the Six Repositories already flourishes, and the magnificence of the Three Institutes has been renewed. Though the western hall is spacious, it presents some inconvenience for reading; a side gate has therefore been opened, so that Your Majesty may visit more easily. An auspicious site happened to lie vacant, precisely the one selected in the imperial mind. Adjoining Shenglong, it is open and lofty, well suited to frequent imperial visits. Accordingly, orders were given to plan and build, creating something new. Its design establishes a foundation as eminent as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper; its eaves spread like a pheasant’s wings, its roof rises like a bird in flight. The celestial lodges Kui and Bi correspond to this repository of books and charts, where the horse bears its chart and the tortoise presents its writing.

It bears the name Chongwen—“Exalting Civil Culture”—and is devoted in practice to investigating antiquity. Eighty thousand scrolls with ivory labels: these treasures have been transferred from the two side repositories. Records spanning hundreds and thousands of years: why speak any longer of the Eastern Library? It assembles histories, philosophical works, and literary collections, standing grandly beneath a pinnacle of purple lightning [?]. Its glittering pearls and gems shine with the radiance of the burning green goosefoot staff. It adjudicates the many teachings and awaits a sage; it opens four repositories in imitation of Heaven. The Song pattern does not extend beyond the doors and courtyard [?]; the Great Way itself ascends to the shore [?]. The counsels of Yao and instructions of the emperors, bequeathed for the peace of later generations, firmly secure the roots. The thoughts of Confucius and sentiments of the Duke of Zhou enable successors to follow their footsteps without losing the tracks laid down long ago. This undertaking concerns transmission and creation alike; its achievement redoubles the work of honoring and elucidating the tradition.

We, your servants, offer our humble gift of sunshine [?], fortunate to have roughly set forth even a single insight. Like the river spirit gazing upon the ocean in “Autumn Floods,” we are ashamed that our three winters of study remain insufficient. Our hearts are truly earnest in praise, yet our words cannot exhaust its expression. We humbly wish that…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
始終典學惟得意以忘言
精一執中期自博而歸約紹百王之道統淵
乎行地之中啓一代之文明炳矣光天之
下〔臣〕等無任瞻
天仰
聖欣躍屏營之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
===
第叁場
策
第一問
郭鵬
同考試官教諭張　批〔我〕
朝宏綱大目子能鋪叙無餘篇末尤見忠愛允宜錄出
同考試官教諭蔡　批〔我〕
聖祖德業如天不可名狀禮與法特其大端也是篇能考究而敷陳之其亦通達
國體者矣况初二場及後四策理精詞暢尤見淹貫之學秋闈得士如此可以自
punctuated:
始終典學，惟得意以忘言；精一執中，期自博而歸約。紹百王之道統，淵乎行地之中；啓一代之文明，炳矣光天之下。〔臣〕等無任瞻天仰聖、欣躍屏營之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。
第叁場
策
第一問
郭鵬
同考試官教諭張批：〔我〕朝宏綱大目，子能鋪叙無餘，篇末尤見忠愛，允宜錄出。
同考試官教諭蔡批：〔我〕聖祖德業如天，不可名狀，禮與法特其大端也。是篇能考究而敷陳之，其亦通達國體者矣。况初二場及後四策，理精詞暢，尤見淹貫之學。秋闈得士如此，可以自
translation_en:
… may you devote yourself to learning from beginning to end, grasping the meaning and thus forgetting the words; remain discerning and single-minded in holding to the mean, seeking through broad learning to arrive at essential principles. Carry forward the succession of the Way transmitted by the hundred kings, profound as it courses through the earth; inaugurate the cultural brilliance of an age, resplendent beneath the shining heavens. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Majesty with boundless joy and reverent trepidation. We respectfully submit this memorial of congratulations for your hearing.
Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question
Guo Peng
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “You have fully expounded the grand framework and principal provisions of our dynasty, leaving nothing out. The conclusion especially reveals your loyalty and devotion. This certainly merits selection for inclusion.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The virtue and achievements of our sagely founder are like Heaven, beyond description; rites and laws are merely their principal aspects. This essay investigates and expounds them: its author surely understands the institutions of the state. Moreover, his work in the first two sessions and the following four policy essays displays precise reasoning and fluent expression, further revealing his extensive and thorough learning. To obtain a scholar like this through the autumn Provincial Examination gives us cause to congratulate ourselves …”

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
慶矣
同考試官教諭楊　批〔遠意出於該博之外錄之非專以其文也〕
考試官學正孫　批〔事核詞暢高薦何忝〕
考試官學正顏　批〔條荅中可占素蘊之厚矣〕
帝王有大經以嘉天下之會有大防以禁
天下之非嘉會以禮禮行而民志定是之
謂大經禁非以法法立而民行正是之謂
大防一於法而不裁之以禮無以通天下
===
之情一於理而不輔之以法無以祛天下
之弊用雖不同而維持道化一也嘗觀天
之於萬物矣匪生弗成至夏而生之功始
盛不止則過得秋而生之功始成帝王之
治蓋取諸此伯夷降典折民惟刑刑以禮
而得中臯陶明刑以弼五教禮資刑而無
斁自夏及商率由是道逮至成周制度益
詳凡其治道之所以雍熙泰和貽世之所
長治久安者有由然哉自是以降載於魯
punctuated:
慶矣。
同考試官教諭楊，批〔遠意出於該博之外，錄之非專以其文也。〕
考試官學正孫，批〔事核詞暢，高薦何忝？〕
考試官學正顏，批〔條荅中可占素蘊之厚矣。〕
帝王有大經，以嘉天下之會；有大防，以禁天下之非。嘉會以禮，禮行而民志定，是之謂大經；禁非以法，法立而民行正，是之謂大防。一於法而不裁之以禮，無以通天下之情；一於理而不輔之以法，無以祛天下之弊。用雖不同，而維持道化一也。嘗觀天之於萬物矣：匪生弗成，至夏而生之功始盛；不止則過，得秋而生之功始成。帝王之治，蓋取諸此。伯夷降典，折民惟刑，刑以禮而得中；臯陶明刑，以弼五教，禮資刑而無斁。自夏及商，率由是道。逮至成周，制度益詳，凡其治道之所以雍熙泰和，貽世之所長治久安者，有由然哉！自是以降，載於魯
translation_en:
…congratulate ourselves.
Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: 〔The far-reaching purport goes beyond even its breadth of learning. It is selected not solely for its literary merit.〕
Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: 〔The facts are sound and the language fluent. How could it be unworthy of a high recommendation?〕
Examiner Yan, School Instructor, comments: 〔From these itemized answers one can discern the depth of his accumulated learning.〕
Emperors and kings have great guiding principles with which to bring excellence to the gatherings of all under Heaven, and great safeguards with which to prohibit wrongdoing throughout the realm. They give excellence to gatherings through ritual: when ritual is practiced, the people's purposes become settled. This is what is meant by great guiding principles. They prohibit wrongdoing through law: when law is established, the people's conduct becomes upright. This is what is meant by great safeguards. Exclusive reliance on law, without regulating it through ritual, cannot accommodate the circumstances and feelings of all under Heaven. Exclusive reliance on principle [perhaps ritual is intended here; ?], without supporting it through law, cannot eliminate the realm's abuses. Though their functions differ, they are one in sustaining moral transformation through the Way.
I have considered Heaven's relation to the myriad things. Without generation, there can be no completion; only with summer does the work of generation reach its fullness. Without restraint, it goes too far; only with autumn does the work of generation reach completion. The government of emperors and kings surely takes its model from this. Bo Yi promulgated the statutes, and the people were restrained through punishments: punishment attained due measure through ritual. Gao Yao clarified the punishments to support the five teachings: ritual drew upon punishment and thus suffered no decay. From Xia through Shang, all followed this way. By the time of Zhou, institutions and regulations had become still more detailed. There were indeed reasons why their government achieved concord, prosperity, and supreme harmony, and why what they bequeathed to later generations secured lasting order and enduring peace! From that time onward, as recorded in Lu…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而有繫纓之惜廢於衛而有相鼠之刺先
王之禮日以隳矣法經造而煩苛已甚商
君用而改革無遺而先王之法日以壞矣
三代而下享國長久蔚然可稱者漢唐宋
也觀其除秦苛法而條約有章除隋苛政
而兵田有制亦庶乎所謂法矣然綿蕞之
禮仍秦舊習貞觀之禮多踵隋轍禮之大
經何有耶忠厚廉恥為立國之本非肅敦
睦為齊家之道亦幾於所謂禮矣然而思
===
威不立事每從乎苟簡號令不嚴政每成
于姑息法之大防何有耶此其治道之所
以龎雜而不純垂世之所以淺近而不柔
者豈非職此之故哉
太祖高皇帝挺生南服起定中原鼎新於革命
之始賁飾於蠱壞之餘雖草昧之秉寧而
宏規之已立設律局而舊官之練於憲章
者居之律令于是定矣設儀局而宿儒之
通於古制者居之禮儀於是完矣設誥局
punctuated:
而有繫纓之惜，廢於衛而有相鼠之刺，先王之禮日以隳矣。法經造而煩苛已甚，商君用而改革無遺，而先王之法日以壞矣。三代而下，享國長久、蔚然可稱者，漢、唐、宋也。觀其除秦苛法而條約有章，除隋苛政而兵田有制，亦庶乎所謂法矣。然綿蕞之禮仍秦舊習，貞觀之禮多踵隋轍，禮之大經何有耶？忠厚廉恥為立國之本，非肅敦睦為齊家之道，亦幾於所謂禮矣。然而思威不立，事每從乎苟簡；號令不嚴，政每成于姑息，法之大防何有耶？此其治道之所以龎雜而不純，垂世之所以淺近而不柔者，豈非職此之故哉？
太祖高皇帝挺生南服，起定中原，鼎新於革命之始，賁飾於蠱壞之餘。雖草昧之秉寧，而宏規之已立。設律局，而舊官之練於憲章者居之，律令于是定矣；設儀局，而宿儒之通於古制者居之，禮儀於是完矣；設誥局，
translation_en:
…yet there was the lament over tying the cap-strings; when ritual was abandoned in Wei, there was the satire of “Look at the Rat.” The ritual of the former kings deteriorated daily. When the Canon of Laws was compiled, its provisions were already excessively burdensome and harsh; when Lord Shang was employed, his reforms left nothing untouched. Thus the laws of the former kings were daily undermined. After the Three Dynasties, those dynasties whose long tenure of the realm most conspicuously deserves praise are the Han, Tang, and Song. Consider how the harsh laws of Qin were abolished and orderly statutes established, and how the oppressive government of Sui was abolished and systems instituted for military service and landholding: these came close to what may properly be called law. Yet the rites rehearsed with bundles of thatch retained the old practices of Qin, and the rites of the Zhenguan era largely followed Sui precedents. Where were the great guiding principles of ritual? Making loyalty, generosity, integrity, and a sense of shame the foundation of the state, and reverence [?] and familial harmony the means of ordering the household, likewise came close to what may properly be called ritual. Yet authority [?] was not established, and affairs were repeatedly handled with careless expediency; commands were not strict, and government repeatedly descended into indulgence. Where were the great safeguards of law? Was this not precisely why their methods of government were heterogeneous rather than pure, and why their legacy to later generations was shallow and lacked enduring effect [?]?
Emperor Taizu Gao arose outstandingly in the southern regions and rose to pacify the Central Plain. At the inception of the change of mandate, he established a new order, bringing refinement after an age of decay. Though order was only beginning to emerge from the unsettled founding period [?], the grand framework had already been established. He set up an office for compiling laws and staffed it with former officials versed in statutes and regulations; thus the statutes and ordinances were settled. He set up an office for ritual and staffed it with senior scholars thoroughly familiar with ancient institutions; thus the rites and ceremonies were brought to completion. He set up an office for drafting patents of appointment…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而才俊之優於文辭者屬之
誥命以撰而凡
封拜之命檄諭之文於是乎製矣當時創造
之務雖非一端而禮法所先無出於此是
誠畧而不遺詳而有體
聖智之高
神謨之妙不於是而可窺也哉其後復
命群臣率諸儒定擬三禮又集議禮樂徵在
野道德文章之士相與考訂之以至
洪武禮制等書頒行而禮之大經以次而立自
===
大誥三篇以戒飭臣民為
製
大明令為
祖訓以至
大明律等書頒行而法之大防以立
鴻規懿範周悉精詳識可以行之萬世而無
憾者也蓋上有以追唐虞而繼商周豈漢
唐宋之君可以彷彿者乎
punctuated: 而才俊之優於文辭者屬之，誥命以撰，而凡封拜之命、檄諭之文，於是乎製矣。當時創造之務，雖非一端，而禮法所先，無出於此。是誠畧而不遺，詳而有體，聖智之高、神謨之妙，不於是而可窺也哉？其後復命群臣率諸儒定擬三禮，又集議禮樂，徵在野道德文章之士，相與考訂之，以至《洪武禮制》等書頒行，而禮之大經以次而立。自《大誥》三篇以戒飭臣民，為製《大明令》，為《祖訓》，以至《大明律》等書頒行，而法之大防以立。鴻規懿範，周悉精詳，識可以行之萬世而無憾者也。蓋上有以追唐虞而繼商周，豈漢唐宋之君可以彷彿者乎？
translation_en:
…and assigned to it talented men who excelled in literary composition. Thus patents of appointment were drafted, and all commands conferring titles and offices, as well as proclamations and admonitions, were composed. Although the work of founding institutions at that time encompassed many undertakings, none took precedence over these in matters of ritual and law. This was truly concise without omission, detailed yet properly ordered. Can we not perceive herein the loftiness of his sagely wisdom and the subtlety of his divine planning?

Later, he again commanded his ministers to lead the Confucian scholars in deliberating upon and settling the Three Rites. He also convened discussions of ritual and music and summoned men outside official service distinguished for moral cultivation and literary accomplishment to examine and revise these matters together. Eventually, books including the Ritual Institutions of the Hongwu Reign were promulgated, and the great guiding principles of ritual were established in succession. Beginning with the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements, intended to admonish and discipline officials and commoners, he compiled [?] the Ordinances of the Great Ming and composed the Ancestral Instructions. Eventually, books including the Code of the Great Ming were promulgated, and the great restraints of law were established.

These magnificent plans and admirable models were comprehensive, meticulous, refined, and detailed—truly [?] fit to be put into practice for ten thousand generations without cause for regret. Indeed, he could reach back to the age of Tang and Yu and carry on the legacy of the Shang and Zhou. How could the rulers of the Han, Tang, or Song even approach him?

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承率由愼守重熈累治百有餘年
皇上臨御勤勵有加行已同倫而違越之禁尤
嚴刑已當罪而
欽恤之典屢下正箕子所謂平康正直孔子所
謂勝殘去殺之時也然奢靡之風稍興而
僭以敗度豪猾之徒間出而縱以犯法則
亦長治久安之世深仁厚澤之餘其勢然
耳玆欲復
聖祖創造之初舉
===
列聖繼守之盛以副
皇上圖治之心不必史張之大過也以姚崇所
謂法行自近者加之意而已不必懲究之
大重也以吳漢所謂愼無赦者加之意而
已矣寅淸明允之本轉移感應之機在吾
君吾相固自有道而草茅之士則不敢以妄議
也惟執事其終敎之
第二問
張鑑
punctuated:
列聖相承，率由愼守，重熈累治百有餘年。皇上臨御，勤勵有加，行已同倫，而違越之禁尤嚴；刑已當罪，而欽恤之典屢下。正箕子所謂平康正直、孔子所謂勝殘去殺之時也。然奢靡之風稍興，而僭以敗度；豪猾之徒間出，而縱以犯法，則亦長治久安之世、深仁厚澤之餘，其勢然耳。玆欲復聖祖創造之初，舉列聖繼守之盛，以副皇上圖治之心，不必史張之大過也，以姚崇所謂法行自近者加之意而已；不必懲究之大重也，以吳漢所謂愼無赦者加之意而已矣。寅淸明允之本，轉移感應之機，在吾君吾相，固自有道，而草茅之士則不敢以妄議也。惟執事其終敎之。

第二問
張鑑
translation_en:
Successive sage emperors inherited the throne, following and carefully preserving established precedents, accumulating prosperity and good government for more than a hundred years. Since ascending the throne, His Majesty has shown ever greater diligence. Conduct already conforms to common norms, yet prohibitions against transgression are especially strict; punishments already fit the crimes, yet edicts enjoining reverent care in administering punishment have repeatedly been issued. This is precisely an age of what Jizi called “peace and stability, with uprightness and rectitude,” and what Confucius called “overcoming cruelty and dispensing with killing.” Yet extravagance has gradually become fashionable, and overstepping prescribed distinctions undermines the established rules; powerful and cunning men occasionally emerge, and their unrestrained conduct violates the law. These are simply tendencies that arise in an age of enduring order and peace, after the enjoyment of profound benevolence and abundant favor.

If we now wish to restore the conditions of the founding days of the Sage Progenitor and revive the flourishing government maintained by his sage successors, thereby fulfilling His Majesty’s desire for good government, there is no need for excessively sweeping changes [?]. We need only give attention to what Yao Chong meant by “enforcement of the law begins with those close to the ruler.” There is no need for excessively severe punitive investigations; we need only give attention to what Wu Han meant by “take care not to grant pardons.” The foundation of reverence, purity, discernment, and fairness, and the means by which transformation is set in motion and responses are elicited, rest with our sovereign and our chief ministers, who assuredly have their own proper way of proceeding. A scholar from the countryside such as myself dares not offer presumptuous opinions. I ask only that you, honored examiners, complete my instruction.

Second Policy Question
Zhang Jian

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭黎　批〔通篇評擬精確末復歸重於預養人材非胷中素有進術者不能本旁之毬知無以易子矣〕
同考試官教諭樊　批〔選用人材皆人雖有成說然世變不同法制亦不能無異此策援古證今鑿鑿可行而整潔之〕
詞昌大之氣又足以發之行將進春官對
大廷可以脫穎而出矣得士如此良以自慶
同考試官教諭方　批〔選中今任將帥二者正今日急務場中士子或縱浮詞而畧事實或僅能掇拾一二餖飣而缺此策考據精詳〕
意見亶出他日或膺衡鑑之任低昂斟酌如今日所言者可
===
以紓
當宁側席之求矣
同考試官教諭李　批〔五策俱善荅而此策尤爲明暢可〕
以覩子之所養矣敬羨敬羨
考試官學正孫　批〔識見周而詞格整佳士也高薦無〕
忝
考試官學正顏　批〔條荅詳悉錄之〕
任人之法能求之廣而用之愼則可以致
治而安民矣夫國之治忽係於民民之安
punctuated:
同考試官教諭黎批〔通篇評擬精確，末復歸重於預養人材。非胷中素有進術者不能。本旁之毬，知無以易子矣。〕

同考試官教諭樊批〔選用人材皆人，雖有成說，然世變不同，法制亦不能無異。此策援古證今，鑿鑿可行，而整潔之〕詞、昌大之氣，又足以發之。行將進春官，對大廷，可以脫穎而出矣。得士如此，良以自慶。

同考試官教諭方批〔選中今任將帥二者，正今日急務。場中士子或縱浮詞而畧事實，或僅能掇拾一二餖飣而缺。此策考據精詳，〕意見亶出。他日或膺衡鑑之任，低昂斟酌如今日所言者，可以紓當宁側席之求矣。

同考試官教諭李批〔五策俱善荅，而此策尤爲明暢，可〕以覩子之所養矣。敬羨！敬羨！

考試官學正孫批〔識見周而詞格整，佳士也。高薦無〕忝。

考試官學正顏批〔條荅詳悉，錄之。〕

任人之法，能求之廣而用之愼，則可以致治而安民矣。夫國之治忽係於民，民之安
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The assessments throughout are precise, and the conclusion again places the emphasis on cultivating talent in advance. Only someone who has long possessed methods for advancement [?] could accomplish this. [The phrase 本旁之毬 is unclear.] I know there is no one who could replace you.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fan, Instructor: “Concerning the selection and employment of talent [皆人 unclear], although established views exist, circumstances change with the times, and institutions and regulations must also differ. This policy essay draws on antiquity to substantiate present practice; its proposals are demonstrably practicable. Its orderly diction and expansive spirit further give them expression. Soon you will proceed to the Ministry of Rites and answer before the imperial court, where you can distinguish yourself. To have found such a scholar is truly cause for self-congratulation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Fang, Instructor: “The two matters—selection [選中今 unclear] and the appointment of commanders—are precisely the urgent tasks of today. Candidates in the examination hall either indulge in empty language and neglect practical matters, or merely gather one or two scraps of borrowed material, leaving their treatment deficient. This policy essay is precise and thorough in its examination of evidence, and its views are truly outstanding [?]. If one day you are entrusted with judging talent, weighing and assessing it as you have proposed here, you can ease His Majesty’s anxious search for worthy men.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “All five policy questions are well answered, but this essay is especially lucid and fluent. It reveals what you have cultivated within yourself. My admiration and esteem! My admiration and esteem!”

Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: “Comprehensive in understanding and orderly in literary form: a fine scholar. He fully merits a high recommendation.”

Comment by Examiner Yan, School Instructor: “His answers to the individual points are detailed and thorough. Accept him.”

The method of appointing men is this: if one can search broadly and employ them cautiously, one can achieve good government and bring peace to the people. Whether the state is well governed or neglected depends upon the people; the people’s security …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
危繫於兵守令得人則親民者多循良而
民之生養有賴將帥得人則典兵者皆武
勇而民之扞衛有托然其任之之法則顧
吾之所以鼓舞作興者何如耳使能廣求
於始而慎用之於終才德不致於遺佚而
賢否不容於混淆法制立於上人才作於
下貪夫廉而懦夫有立志矣何患不足以
追配古人而成乂安於
今日也哉請因明問而條陳之三代以前分
===
地建國與天下共其利寓兵於農與百姓
均其勞法天而不自私盡制而不曲防萬
事萬物各得其理此所以久安長治非後
世之所能及也自夫封建之法廢而郡縣
始置井田之法廢而兵農始分付守令以
親民之職任將帥以領兵之權此固勢之
不得不然者守令寄一方之休戚其於清
慎勤之三事固當加之意將帥係三軍之
存亡其於知仁信勇嚴之五德又豈可不
punctuated:
危繫於兵。守令得人，則親民者多循良，而民之生養有賴；將帥得人，則典兵者皆武勇，而民之扞衛有托。然其任之之法，則顧吾之所以鼓舞作興者何如耳。使能廣求於始，而慎用之於終，才德不致於遺佚，而賢否不容於混淆，法制立於上，人才作於下，貪夫廉而懦夫有立志矣。何患不足以追配古人，而成乂安於今日也哉？請因明問而條陳之。
三代以前，分地建國，與天下共其利；寓兵於農，與百姓均其勞。法天而不自私，盡制而不曲防，萬事萬物各得其理，此所以久安長治，非後世之所能及也。自夫封建之法廢而郡縣始置，井田之法廢而兵農始分，付守令以親民之職，任將帥以領兵之權，此固勢之不得不然者。守令寄一方之休戚，其於清慎勤之三事，固當加之意；將帥係三軍之存亡，其於知仁信勇嚴之五德，又豈可不
translation_en:
…or peril depends on the military. When suitable men are appointed as prefects and magistrates, those who govern the people directly are mostly conscientious and upright, and the people have support for their livelihood and nurture. When suitable men are appointed as commanders, those in charge of the troops are all martial and courageous, and the people have someone to entrust with their protection. Yet the method of appointing them depends upon how we encourage and inspire them. If we seek men widely at the outset and employ them cautiously thereafter, men of talent and virtue will not be overlooked, nor will the worthy and unworthy be confused. Laws and institutions will be established above, and talented men will rise below; the greedy will become incorruptible, and the timid will gain the resolve to stand firm. Why fear that we cannot rival the ancients and achieve order and peace today? Allow me to set out the points in response to your discerning question.
In the Three Dynasties and earlier, territory was divided and states established, sharing their benefits with all under Heaven; soldiers were incorporated among the farmers, sharing the burdens with the common people. They took Heaven as their model without pursuing private interests, and fully established institutions without resorting to intricate safeguards. Every affair and every thing attained its proper order. This was how they achieved lasting peace and enduring good government, beyond what later ages could match. Once the system of enfeoffment was abolished, commanderies and counties were established; once the well-field system was abolished, soldiers and farmers became separate. Prefects and magistrates were entrusted with governing the people directly, and commanders were given authority to lead troops. Circumstances indeed made this unavoidable. Prefects and magistrates are entrusted with the well-being or distress of an entire locality, so they must give particular attention to the three qualities of integrity, caution, and diligence. Commanders determine the survival or destruction of the armies; how, then, could they fail to attend to the five virtues of wisdom, benevolence, trustworthiness, courage, and strictness…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
究厥心哉方今
聖
明勵精圖治守令之選簡拔於科目甄別於
銓曹其制非不嚴且重也然而惠澤未溥
於閭閻而貪饕之風猶存者茲蓋有說耳
黜陟不關於政理而毀譽是循考績不責
於久任而陞遷罔稱以逢迎爲悅而勵志
剛正者顧付之悠悠以催科爲能而撫字
心勞者乃考居下下以是求得清脩之士
殆猶欲好書而掣其肘不亦難乎誠欲使
===
列郡縣者必如孔奮令富邑而力行清潔
裴俠守河北而躬履節儉歷遷三郡謙恭
每形於色如崔元亮之賢爲宰數年教化
大洽於民如卓茂之最莫如廣求而慎用
之其始進也必察其履歷觀其年貌因才
器之高下爲地方之繁簡可任則任之不
必拘之以科目可拔則拔之不必限之以
資格而又俟其久任責以成效擯斥不避
其豪貪墨者必懲汲引無間於疎遠
punctuated: 究厥心哉？方今聖明勵精圖治，守令之選，簡拔於科目，甄別於銓曹，其制非不嚴且重也。然而惠澤未溥於閭閻，而貪饕之風猶存者，茲蓋有說耳。黜陟不關於政理，而毀譽是循；考績不責於久任，而陞遷罔稱。以逢迎爲悅，而勵志剛正者，顧付之悠悠；以催科爲能，而撫字心勞者，乃考居下下。以是求得清脩之士，殆猶欲好書而掣其肘，不亦難乎？誠欲使列郡縣者，必如孔奮令富邑而力行清潔，裴俠守河北而躬履節儉，歷遷三郡、謙恭每形於色如崔元亮之賢，爲宰數年、教化大洽於民如卓茂之最，莫如廣求而慎用之。其始進也，必察其履歷，觀其年貌，因才器之高下，爲地方之繁簡。可任則任之，不必拘之以科目；可拔則拔之，不必限之以資格。而又俟其久任，責以成效。擯斥不避其豪，貪墨者必懲；汲引無間於疎遠，
translation_en:
…give these their utmost consideration? At present, His Sagacious Majesty devotes himself earnestly to good government. Prefects and county magistrates are selected through the examinations and screened by the personnel authorities: the system is certainly strict and weighty. Yet its benefits have not spread throughout the common people's neighborhoods, and the habit of rapacity persists. There is surely an explanation for this. Demotion and promotion bear no relation to the quality of administration, but follow slander and praise; evaluations do not demand achievement over a long tenure, and advancement is not commensurate with merit. Flattery wins favor, while those resolved to be firm and upright are simply left neglected. Skill in pressing tax collections counts as ability, while those who expend their hearts and labor nurturing the people receive the lowest possible evaluation. To seek men of integrity and disciplined conduct in this way is rather like wanting fine calligraphy while tugging at the writer's elbow. Is it not difficult?

If we truly wish those serving in prefectures and counties to emulate Kong Fen, who governed a wealthy county yet diligently maintained his integrity; Pei Xia, who governed Hebei and personally practiced frugality; the worthy Cui Yuanliang, who served successively in three prefectures and always showed humility and respect in his expression; and the outstanding Zhuo Mao, who, after several years as magistrate, brought the people fully under his transforming instruction—nothing is better than searching widely and appointing carefully. When candidates first enter service, their previous experience must be examined and their age and appearance observed; their abilities and capacities, whether greater or lesser, should be matched to the complexity or simplicity of local administrative duties. Those fit for appointment should be appointed, without necessarily restricting selection to examination qualifications; those worthy of advancement should be advanced, without necessarily limiting them by formal eligibility. They should then be allowed a long tenure and held responsible for results. In dismissing men, do not shrink from their power: the corrupt must be punished. In drawing men into service, make no distinction against those distant from official connections…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而賢能者必錄將見爲守令者爭自磨濯
克脩三事可以追配古人於百世之上矣
將帥之求既遴選於武舉又擢用於軍功
其制非不慎且密也然而威望未嚴於敵
愾而糜費之弊滋甚者豈無其故哉分閫
邊陲者皆綺紈之子課功武部者皆請托
之徒手握重兵而弓矢之莫諳累坐敗衂
而襲蔭之如故以是欲求驍雄之將是猶
適燕薊而南其轅烏可得乎茲欲使授節
===
鉞者必如田單養兵用間以復齊七十餘
城謝玄移陣渡水以却秦八十萬衆師行
有紀如鄧禹佐漢光以中興使命交通如
羊祜致吳人之悅服亦莫若廣求而慎用
之其始進也或取之於世冑或拔之於行
伍投之以險而觀其氣試之以難而堅其
守而又明立賞罰分別功罪勇畧顯著者
畀以節鉞而不假於干求貪懦素聞者奪
其襲蔭而不事夫姑息將見爲將帥者皆
punctuated:
而賢能者必錄。將見爲守令者爭自磨濯，克脩三事，可以追配古人於百世之上矣。

將帥之求，既遴選於武舉，又擢用於軍功，其制非不慎且密也。然而威望未嚴於敵愾，而糜費之弊滋甚者，豈無其故哉？分閫邊陲者，皆綺紈之子；課功武部者，皆請托之徒。手握重兵，而弓矢之莫諳；累坐敗衂，而襲蔭之如故。以是欲求驍雄之將，是猶適燕薊而南其轅，烏可得乎？茲欲使授節鉞者，必如田單養兵用間，以復齊七十餘城；謝玄移陣渡水，以却秦八十萬衆；師行有紀，如鄧禹佐漢光以中興；使命交通，如羊祜致吳人之悅服；亦莫若廣求而慎用之。其始進也，或取之於世冑，或拔之於行伍，投之以險而觀其氣，試之以難而堅其守。而又明立賞罰，分別功罪，勇畧顯著者畀以節鉞，而不假於干求；貪懦素聞者奪其襲蔭，而不事夫姑息。將見爲將帥者皆
translation_en:
…and those who are worthy and capable must invariably be selected. We shall then see prefects and magistrates vying to refine and purify themselves, successfully fulfilling the three duties, and able to rival the ancients of a hundred generations past.

In seeking generals and commanders, men are selected through the military examinations and also promoted for military merit. The system is certainly careful and thorough. Yet their prestige and authority have failed to inspire awe in confronting the enemy, while the abuses of wasteful expenditure grow ever worse. Can this be without cause? Those entrusted with regional military command on the frontiers are all sons of luxury; those whose achievements are assessed by the Ministry of War are all men who solicit favors through intermediaries. They hold powerful armies in their hands yet know nothing of bows and arrows; repeatedly held culpable for defeats, they nevertheless retain their hereditary privileges as before. To seek valiant generals by these means is like setting out for Yan and Ji with one's carriage shafts pointing south. How could one succeed?

If we now wish those invested with the commander's tally and battle-axe to emulate Tian Dan, who nurtured his troops and employed spies to recover more than seventy cities of Qi; or Xie Xuan, who shifted battle formations and crossed the river to repel Qin's host of eight hundred thousand; if we wish their armies to march with discipline, as when Deng Yu assisted Emperor Guangwu of Han in restoring the dynasty, and their envoys to maintain communication, as when Yang Hu won the willing submission of the people of Wu—then here too nothing is better than searching widely and appointing cautiously. When men first enter service, some may be chosen from hereditary military families and others raised from the ranks. Place them in peril to observe their spirit; test them with difficulties to strengthen their resolve. Furthermore, clearly establish rewards and punishments, distinguishing merit from fault. Those whose courage and strategic ability are manifest should be granted the tally and battle-axe, without these being bestowed in response to solicitation. Those long known for greed and cowardice should be stripped of their hereditary privileges, without indulgence. We shall then see generals and commanders all…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
自相激昂克舉五德可以繼踵往躅於千
載之下矣夫文武並用國家長久之術然
欲才兼文武世亦鮮其人也有宋韓范奮
起儒流致位通顯在郡邑則著招徠之績
在廟堂則成弼亮之休而分帥陝右英謀
義烈又有以破西賊之膽以收平定之功
後之景仰二公而欲追其芳躅史冊班班
可考也雖然人才國家之利器必養之有
素而後用之不窮楩柟杞梓排風雨而振
===
雲霄豈一朝一夕之故哉欂櫨梁棟隨用
隨宜亦曰灌溉栽培之久耳事已倥偬變
生倉卒方且皇皇然跅弛之求激西江以
救涸轍吾見其無及矣詩曰豐水有芑武
王豈不仕貽厥孫謀以燕翼子愚切有望
於
今日
第三問
萬振聲
punctuated:
自相激昂，克舉五德，可以繼踵往躅於千載之下矣。夫文武並用，國家長久之術。然欲才兼文武，世亦鮮其人也。有宋韓范，奮起儒流，致位通顯；在郡邑則著招徠之績，在廟堂則成弼亮之休；而分帥陝右，英謀義烈，又有以破西賊之膽，以收平定之功。後之景仰二公而欲追其芳躅，史冊班班可考也。雖然，人才，國家之利器，必養之有素，而後用之不窮。楩柟杞梓，排風雨而振雲霄，豈一朝一夕之故哉？欂櫨梁棟，隨用隨宜，亦曰灌溉栽培之久耳。事已倥偬，變生倉卒，方且皇皇然跅弛之求，激西江以救涸轍，吾見其無及矣。《詩》曰：「豐水有芑，武王豈不仕？貽厥孫謀，以燕翼子。」愚切有望於今日。

第三問
萬振聲
translation_en:
…will spur one another onward and fully embody the five virtues, enabling them to follow in their predecessors’ footsteps a thousand years later. Employing both civil and military abilities is the means by which a state endures. Yet people whose talents encompass both are rare indeed. In the Song dynasty, Han and Fan rose from the ranks of Confucian scholars to attain eminent office. In local administration they distinguished themselves by attracting people to settle; at court they rendered distinguished service in assisting the ruler. When they held separate military commands in western Shaanxi, their brilliant strategies and deeds of righteousness and valor broke the courage of the western foes and secured the achievement of pacification. For later generations who admire these two gentlemen and wish to follow their illustrious footsteps, the historical records offer abundant evidence to consult.

Nevertheless, talented people are the state’s effective instruments: only when they have been cultivated beforehand can their service be drawn upon without exhaustion. Great trees—pian, nan, qi, and zi—weather wind and rain and tower into the clouds: could this be the work of a single day or night? That timber can serve appropriately as brackets, bearing blocks, beams, or ridgepoles is likewise simply the result of prolonged watering and cultivation. If one waits until affairs are already pressing and upheaval arises suddenly, and only then anxiously seeks men of unrestrained talent, it is like diverting the waters of the western river to rescue a creature stranded in a dried-up wheel rut: I see that it will be too late. The Book of Odes says: “By the Feng River grows the qi plant. Did King Wu not employ worthy men? He bequeathed plans to his descendants, thereby bringing peace to and protecting his children.” In my humble judgment, I earnestly hope for this in our own day.

Third Policy Question
Wan Zhensheng

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官訓導蘇　批〔左氏論人物一篥子業經予〕
〔弗責且疆記惟觀其裁斷以驗尚友之志何如耳子掌〕
〔品第之詳猶持舊衡而低昂不失竊期待之意自〕
〔溢言表予固知子非徒事涉獵者佳士佳士〕
考試官學正孫　批〔考衡人物如漢與老吏剖決〕
〔精當闡博之士也可敬可敬〕
考試官學正顔　批〔此卷五策俱嘉而吕論人物〕
〔策尤為精確録之〕
取人於微者得一時之隺論人以全者寳
===
萬世之經以隺非恕也一時之不獲已者
勢也以經非嚴也萬世之不可無者理也
惟其勢則一事之善亦可稱述惟其理則
全德之備必君子而後可故一事之善三
代以下或有之全德之稱非三代以上不
能也儒者生於千百世之下以品藻千百
世而上之人物可苟然而已哉理以主乎
勢背以濟乎經將無徃而不當矣孔子曰
聽言觀行者經也孟子曰彼善於比者權
punctuated:
同考試官訓導蘇批〔左氏論人物一篥，子業經予〕〔弗責且疆記，惟觀其裁斷，以驗尚友之志何如耳。子掌〕〔品第之詳，猶持舊衡而低昂不失，竊期待之意自〕〔溢言表。予固知子非徒事涉獵者，佳士！佳士！〕

考試官學正孫批〔考衡人物，如漢與老吏，剖決〕〔精當，闡博之士也，可敬！可敬！〕

考試官學正顔批〔此卷五策俱嘉，而吕論人物〕〔策尤為精確，録之。〕

取人於微者，得一時之隺；論人以全者，寳萬世之經。以隺非恕也，一時之不獲已者，勢也；以經非嚴也，萬世之不可無者，理也。惟其勢，則一事之善亦可稱述；惟其理，則全德之備必君子而後可。故一事之善，三代以下或有之；全德之稱，非三代以上不能也。儒者生於千百世之下，以品藻千百世而上之人物，可苟然而已哉？理以主乎勢，背以濟乎經，將無徃而不當矣。孔子曰：「聽言觀行」者，經也；孟子曰：「彼善於比」者，權
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Su, Assistant Instructor, comments: “On Master Zuo’s discussion of historical figures [the opening wording is garbled: ?]. I do not demand extensive memorization [?]; I look only at your judgments, to ascertain the nature of your aspiration to befriend the worthy of antiquity. You command the details of their ranking, as though holding an established balance whose rise and fall never errs. My private hopes for you overflow beyond words. I certainly know that you are no mere casual reader. An excellent scholar! An excellent scholar!”

Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “In assessing and weighing historical figures, you are like Han [?] and a seasoned administrative clerk: your analyses and judgments are precise and fitting. You are a scholar of broad learning [?]. Admirable! Admirable!”

Examiner Yan, Instructor, comments: “All five policy essays in this script are excellent, but the policy essay discussing historical figures [?] is especially precise. Include it in the record.”

Those who recognize a person’s worth on the strength of a minor merit grasp what is expedient for a particular time [?]; those who judge a person in his entirety treasure the constant standard for all ages. Employing expediency [?] is not indulgence: what circumstances make unavoidable at a particular time is a matter of the situation. Employing the constant standard is not severity: what no age can do without is a matter of principle. In view of the situation, even excellence in a single deed may deserve praise; in view of principle, only a gentleman can possess virtue in its completeness. Thus, excellence in a single deed may sometimes be found after the Three Dynasties; the designation of complete virtue can apply only to those of the Three Dynasties and earlier.
