Can a Confucian scholar, born hundreds or thousands of generations later, presume to appraise the figures of hundreds or thousands of generations before him casually? Let principle govern the situation, and expediency [?] supplement the constant standard: then one’s judgments will be fitting in every case. Confucius’s saying, “Listen to their words and observe their conduct,” expresses the constant standard; Mencius’s saying, “That one is better than this one,” expresses expediency…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
也舍此將無以為法矣唐虞三代君臣與
稷契伊傅周召之流其將何以譬之過此
則時非其時人非其人也嗚呼責人以先
舜千古無盛治求人以孔孟天下無真儒
而蘿豈可少哉要之不失乎經而已宋儒
真西山讀書記於歷代輔臣必以正己格
君用人謀國律之此則孔氏之法也請以
今日論及春秋人物而律以西山四事為
對如臧孫以兵諫傳稱其愛此格君之謂
===
也異缺以饁敬傳紀其德此正己之謂也
祁奚釋讐嫌以薦賢非善於用人者乎相
三君而無私積見文子之忠受彤弓而弗
辭成士句之禮以至叔弓大館之却豫讓
國士之報荀息股肱之竭又皆其謀國之
一節者蓋春秋之世利詐日趍道義罔有
數子能裒然特出乎其間胥不可少左氏
國語因事書之亦彼善於此之微意耳惜
夫光嶽之氣分裂於吾道頹墜之餘學問
punctuated: 也。舍此，將無以為法矣。唐虞三代君臣，與稷契伊傅周召之流，其將何以譬之？過此，則時非其時，人非其人也。嗚呼！責人以先舜，千古無盛治；求人以孔孟，天下無真儒。而蘿豈可少哉？要之，不失乎經而已。宋儒真西山《讀書記》，於歷代輔臣，必以正己、格君、用人、謀國律之，此則孔氏之法也。請以今日論及春秋人物，而律以西山四事為對。如臧孫以兵諫，傳稱其愛，此格君之謂也。異缺以饁敬，傳紀其德，此正己之謂也。祁奚釋讐嫌以薦賢，非善於用人者乎？相三君而無私積，見文子之忠；受彤弓而弗辭，成士句之禮。以至叔弓大館之却，豫讓國士之報，荀息股肱之竭，又皆其謀國之一節者。蓋春秋之世，利詐日趍，道義罔有，數子能裒然特出乎其間，胥不可少。《左氏》《國語》因事書之，亦彼善於此之微意耳。惜夫光嶽之氣，分裂於吾道頹墜之餘，學問
translation_en:
…is discretionary judgment. Abandon this, and there will be no standard to follow. With what could one compare the rulers and ministers of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, and such men as Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and the Duke of Shao? Beyond that age, the times were no longer those times, nor the men those men. Alas! If we judge men by the standard of Xian and Shun [?], no age has enjoyed flourishing government; if we seek men equal to Confucius and Mencius, there are no true Confucians in the world. Yet how could luo [?] be dispensed with? The essential point is simply not to depart from constant principles. In his Notes on Reading, the Song Confucian Zhen Xishan invariably judged the chief ministers of successive dynasties by four criteria: rectifying oneself, correcting the ruler, employing men, and planning for the state. This is Confucius’s method. Permit me, in answering today’s discussion of figures of the Spring and Autumn period, to assess them by Xishan’s four criteria.

For example, Zangsun remonstrated by force of arms, and the Commentary praised his love for his ruler: this is what is meant by correcting the ruler. Yi Que [probably Xi Que; ?] showed reverence when food was brought to him in the fields, and the Commentary recorded his virtue: this is what is meant by rectifying oneself. Qi Xi set aside concerns about enmity to recommend a worthy man: was he not skilled in employing men? Serving as chief minister to three rulers without accumulating private wealth revealed Wenzi’s loyalty; accepting the red bow without declining it fulfilled the ritual propriety of Shi Ju [probably Shi Gai; ?]. Sh ugong’s refusal of the grand guest residence, Yu Rang’s repayment of treatment as an outstanding man of the state, and Xun Xi’s utmost exertion as a trusted minister were likewise particular instances of their planning for the state.

In the Spring and Autumn age, men pursued profit and deception more each day, while the Way and righteousness were absent. These few men stood conspicuously above their contemporaries, and none could be dispensed with. The Zuo Commentary and Discourses of the States recorded them in connection with particular events, conveying only the subtle judgment that one man was better than another. Alas, the vital force of the great mountains became fragmented in the aftermath of our Way’s decline, and their scholarly learning…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
之功素乏乎師友淵源之講雖天資偶合
似若可觀而君立身大節終不可為法然□
於此寔有說焉拳諫似愛矣嘗稽之古□□
逢比干之諫何嘗以兵為名哉若以拳之
法吾恐恫疑恐喝恣行陵暴致後世有以
誅君側為名稱兵向闕而實欲脅君取國
者非拳啓之乎至於郤缺則不止此觀其
他日為政以德禮訓趙盾以才智復士會
而不負胥臣之舉較之拳優劣從可知矣
===
祁奚在晉將中軍而無失德國語稱其果
敢不淫宜乎克保厥終也若乃文子納賂
使齊俛首宗楚一節之小廉曲謹烏足為
世輕重哉宣子誠知禮矣他日中軍之遜
懦衰之迈又皆可録惜乎為刑書以貽後
不能不為終身之累叔弓誠近德矣觀其
累使晉楚不辱君命足驗其賢柰何彊鄆
圖費得失相半若夫豫讓之節固人所難
然其自處亦過矣向使智伯弗遇以國士
punctuated:
之功素乏乎師友淵源之講，雖天資偶合，似若可觀，而君立身大節終不可為法。然□於此寔有說焉。拳諫似愛矣，嘗稽之古□□逢、比干之諫，何嘗以兵為名哉？若以拳之法，吾恐恫疑恐喝，恣行陵暴，致後世有以誅君側為名，稱兵向闕，而實欲脅君取國者，非拳啓之乎？至於郤缺，則不止此。觀其他日為政，以德禮訓趙盾，以才智復士會，而不負胥臣之舉，較之拳，優劣從可知矣。

祁奚在晉，將中軍而無失德，《國語》稱其果敢不淫，宜乎克保厥終也。若乃文子納賂，使齊俛首宗楚，一節之小廉曲謹，烏足為世輕重哉？宣子誠知禮矣，他日中軍之遜，懦衰之迈，又皆可録。惜乎為刑書以貽後，不能不為終身之累。叔弓誠近德矣，觀其累使晉楚，不辱君命，足驗其賢。柰何彊鄆圖費，得失相半。若夫豫讓之節，固人所難，然其自處亦過矣。向使智伯弗遇以國士
translation_en:
…their efforts at learning had always lacked instruction rooted in a lineage of teachers and friends. Although their natural endowments happened to accord with the Way and seemed worthy of regard, their conduct in the great matters of personal integrity [?] could ultimately not serve as a model. Yet [illegible] there is indeed something to be said about this. Quan’s remonstrance seemed to express love for his ruler. But when we examine the remonstrances of the ancient … Feng [?] and Bi Gan, when did they ever invoke armed force? Were Quan’s method adopted, I fear that intimidation, threats, and unrestrained violence would lead later generations to raise troops against the palace under the pretext of punishing those around the ruler, while actually seeking to coerce him and seize his state. Would Quan not have opened the way for them? As for Xi Que, his merits went further. Consider his later conduct in government: he instructed Zhao Dun in virtue and ritual propriety, and used his abilities and intelligence to bring Shi Hui back, thus vindicating Xu Chen’s recommendation of him. Compared with Quan, their relative merits are readily apparent.

Qi Xi commanded the central army in Jin without any lapse in virtue. The Discourses of the States praises him as resolute and courageous without excess; it was fitting that he should preserve his integrity to the end. Wenzi, however, accepted bribes and made Qi bow its head and acknowledge Chu’s supremacy. How could his petty incorruptibility and punctilious caution in a single matter carry weight in the world? Xuanzi certainly understood ritual propriety. His later yielding of command of the central army and his withdrawal in infirm old age [?] also deserve to be recorded. Regrettably, his production of a penal code for posterity could not but blemish his life’s record. Shu Gong certainly approached virtue. His repeated missions to Jin and Chu, in which he brought no disgrace upon his ruler’s commands, sufficiently demonstrate his worth. Yet why did he strengthen Yun and scheme against Fei, leaving his faults to offset his merits? As for Yu Rang’s integrity, it was certainly something others would find difficult to match; yet he too went too far in the obligations he set himself. Had Zhi Bo not treated him as an outstanding man of the state…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
則將奚報之昔崔杼弑齊君晏平仲曰人
有君而人弑之吾焉得死之而焉得亡之
君子不以是罪晏子者見齊君不為社稷
死而晏子非其私暱之臣也智伯之死與
齊君一耳讓為晏子可也否則為博浪之
椎亦可也而乃愚以自投陷阱與匹夫匹
婦自經溝瀆者類焉豈但擊衣之狂而已
哉求其可矜惟荀息其庶幾耳竭其力而
加之以忠貞至今讀之凜凜生氣其於碧
===
子以信易生之說允蹈厥躬惜乎事之不
濟者天也非人也善乎先正有曰學問之
所得有限量故功業之所就有分數蟬然
又豈可以成敗論英雄哉孔子曰吾之於
人也誰毀誰譽如有所譽者必有所試矣
而司馬溫公又曰蓋棺事始定此又取人
論人之至要也而可弗之思乎然西山之
意猶有存者其曰留侯之為韓輔漢諸公
之撫周為唐武侯之志存恢復文正之憂
punctuated: 則將奚報之？昔崔杼弑齊君，晏平仲曰：「人有君而人弑之，吾焉得死之，而焉得亡之？」君子不以是罪晏子者，見齊君不為社稷死，而晏子非其私暱之臣也。智伯之死與齊君一耳，讓為晏子可也；否則，為博浪之椎亦可也。而乃愚以自投陷阱，與匹夫匹婦自經溝瀆者類焉，豈但擊衣之狂而已哉？求其可矜，惟荀息其庶幾耳。竭其力，而加之以忠貞，至今讀之，凜凜生氣。其於碧子以信易生之說，允蹈厥躬。惜乎事之不濟者，天也，非人也。善乎先正有曰：「學問之所得有限量，故功業之所就有分數。」蟬然，又豈可以成敗論英雄哉？孔子曰：「吾之於人也，誰毀誰譽？如有所譽者，必有所試矣。」而司馬溫公又曰：「蓋棺事始定。」此又取人論人之至要也，而可弗之思乎？然西山之意猶有存者，其曰留侯之為韓輔漢，諸公之撫周為唐，武侯之志存恢復，文正之憂
translation_en:
…then how would he have repaid him? Formerly, when Cui Zhu murdered the ruler of Qi, Yan Pingzhong said: “Someone has a ruler, and someone murders him: why should I die for him, and why should I go into exile for him?” The reason gentlemen do not condemn Master Yan for this is that they recognize that the ruler of Qi did not die for the state, and that Master Yan was not his personal favorite. Zhi Bo’s death was no different from that of the ruler of Qi. Yu Rang could have acted as Master Yan did; alternatively, he could have resorted to a blow like that at Bolang. Instead, he foolishly threw himself into a trap, resembling ordinary men and women who hang themselves in ditches. Was this merely the folly of striking a garment?

If we seek someone deserving sympathy, Xun Xi alone comes close. He exhausted his strength and added to it loyalty and steadfastness. Even now, reading his story, one feels an awe-inspiring vitality. As for Master Bi’s [?] teaching about exchanging one’s life for fidelity, he truly embodied it in his own conduct. Alas, that his undertaking failed was due to Heaven, not to human effort. Well did a worthy predecessor say: “What one gains through learning has its limits; thus what one achieves in meritorious service has its allotted measure.” Yet [?], how can heroes be judged by success or failure? Confucius said: “In my dealings with others, whom do I disparage, and whom do I praise? If there is someone I praise, he must have been put to the test.” And Sima Guang, Duke of Wen, also said: “Only when the coffin is closed are a person’s deeds finally settled.” These, too, are essential principles for selecting and judging people. Can we fail to reflect on them?

Yet Xishan’s meaning still has something further in it, when he speaks of the Marquis of Liu’s acting for Han 韓 while assisting Han 漢; the various lords’ tending to Zhou for the sake of Tang [?]; the Marquis of Wu’s resolve to achieve restoration; and Wenzheng’s concern…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
濟斯民論其事則皆青天白日論其功業
又皆百代殊絕人物其於正已格君用人
謀國無往而不盡者視彼區區為愛為德
為忠為禮者可能彷彿其萬一哉此則執
事謂其獨得之見裁論之正洵乎惟舉其
全而匪以權為也嗚呼比方人物較量短
長君子豈為是與詩曰高山仰止景行行
止實所以自期待也人安可苟於自棄自
暴哉聖人可學而至顧其立志何如耳志
===
聖弗獲則不失為賢志賢弗獲則不失為
一介之士若志士而弗能焉是置其身於
汚下將無一可為矣故曰經權者取論人
物之法也立志者希賢希聖之本也不識
執事以為何如
第四問
張勛
同考試官教諭費 批〔近世士子惟記誦舊文 不理會道學詩文一以策正欲觀其平日所養何〕
到源頭處使不理會道學詩文一以策正欲觀其平日所養何
punctuated:
濟斯民。論其事，則皆青天白日；論其功業，又皆百代殊絕人物。其於正已格君、用人謀國，無往而不盡者，視彼區區為愛、為德、為忠、為禮者，可能彷彿其萬一哉？此則執事謂其獨得之見、裁論之正，洵乎惟舉其全，而匪以權為也。嗚呼！比方人物，較量短長，君子豈為是與？《詩》曰：「高山仰止，景行行止。」實所以自期待也。人安可苟於自棄自暴哉？聖人可學而至，顧其立志何如耳。志聖弗獲，則不失為賢；志賢弗獲，則不失為一介之士。若志士而弗能焉，是置其身於汚下，將無一可為矣。故曰：經權者，取論人物之法也；立志者，希賢希聖之本也。不識執事以為何如？

第四問
張勛
同考試官教諭費，批〔近世士子惟記誦舊文，不理會道學詩文，一以策，正欲觀其平日所養何〕
到源頭處，使不理會道學詩文，一以策，正欲觀其平日所養何
translation_en:
…to bring relief to the people. Judged by their deeds, all were as clear as the blue sky and the bright sun; judged by their achievements, all were figures outstanding across a hundred generations. In rectifying themselves and correcting their rulers, employing men and planning for the state, they exerted themselves fully in every respect. Could those whose limited efforts amounted merely to affection, virtue, loyalty, or ritual propriety resemble them even to the slightest degree? This, then, is what you describe as their distinctive insight and the soundness of their judgments. Indeed, it considers their conduct in its entirety, rather than treating it as an exercise of expediency.

Alas! Would a gentleman compare historical figures and weigh their strengths and weaknesses merely for the sake of doing so? The Book of Odes says: “I look up to the lofty mountain; I travel along the great road.” This is truly a means of setting expectations for oneself. How can anyone lightly abandon or debase himself? Sagehood can be attained through learning; it depends only on the aspirations one establishes. If one aspires to sagehood but fails to attain it, one can still be a worthy. If one aspires to be a worthy but fails, one can still be a man of principle. But if one aspires to be a man of principle and cannot achieve even that, one consigns oneself to baseness and will be capable of nothing. Thus I say: constant principles and expedient adaptation provide the method for assessing historical figures; establishing one's aspirations is the foundation for emulating worthies and sages. I wonder what you think of this.

Fourth Question
Zhang Xun

Comment by Associate Examiner Fei, Instructor: 〔Students these days merely memorize and recite old writings, without understanding the Learning of the Way or poetry and prose. By testing them with a policy question [?], the intention is precisely to see how their habitual cultivation…〕

Reaching the very source, causing them not to understand the Learning of the Way or poetry and prose [?]; by testing them with a policy question [?], the intention is precisely to see how their habitual cultivation…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
如不意經生中乃有究心如此者得之為賢科重矣
同考試官教諭丁　批　塲中作者多為此策所窘
子能條荅如是豈亦欲合理學詩文為一者歟
考試官學正孫　批　此策如倒囊出物不煩心力
而自中尺度飽學之士也高薦允宜
考試官學正顏　批　考亭全集盡在此子腹中方
能隨叩隨鳴其積學待問之士歟
詩文一也前脩擅作者之名大儒有折衷
之論甚哉作者之難固矣自非前輩沉潛
===
六籍經緯一心仰師隆古俯視當世何以
信今而傳後逮夫大儒一出然後詩文理
學一以貫之所謂折衷之論其不在是乎
執事生當理學大明之時秋闈試士而以
吾鄉前輩詩文為問且以子朱子終之子
朱子遊宦吾鄉而遠紹濂溪之傳者也嗚
呼此執事策諸生以道學也非策諸生以
詩文也借詩文以明道學也愚雖不佞敢
不悉心以對自古詩既亡之後盖數百年
punctuated:
如，不意經生中乃有究心如此者，得之為賢科重矣。
同考試官教諭丁，批：塲中作者多為此策所窘，子能條荅如是，豈亦欲合理學詩文為一者歟？
考試官學正孫，批：此策如倒囊出物，不煩心力而自中尺度，飽學之士也，高薦允宜。
考試官學正顏，批：考亭全集盡在此子腹中，方能隨叩隨鳴，其積學待問之士歟？
詩文一也，前脩擅作者之名，大儒有折衷之論，甚哉作者之難固矣！自非前輩沉潛六籍，經緯一心，仰師隆古，俯視當世，何以信今而傳後？逮夫大儒一出，然後詩文理學一以貫之，所謂折衷之論，其不在是乎？執事生當理學大明之時，秋闈試士，而以吾鄉前輩詩文為問，且以子朱子終之。子朱子遊宦吾鄉，而遠紹濂溪之傳者也。嗚呼！此執事策諸生以道學也，非策諸生以詩文也，借詩文以明道學也。愚雖不佞，敢不悉心以對？自古詩既亡之後，盖數百年
translation_en:
…what it was like. I had not expected to find among students of the Classics someone who had devoted such attention to these matters. Finding him lends distinction to this examination for worthy men.

Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor, comments: Many writers in the examination hall were stymied by this policy question. You have answered its points so well: might you too seek to unite the Learning of Principle with poetry and prose?

Examiner Sun, School Director, comments: This policy essay is like tipping objects out of a bag: without taxing his mind, he naturally meets the standards. He is a man of extensive learning, fully deserving a high recommendation.

Examiner Yan, School Director, comments: Only someone with the complete collected works of Kaoting [Zhu Xi] stored in his belly could respond to every inquiry as a bell responds to each stroke. Surely he is a man who has accumulated learning and awaits questions!

Poetry and prose are one. Our learned predecessors enjoyed renown as writers, while the great Confucian master offered a definitive assessment. How very difficult it is indeed to be a writer! Had those predecessors not immersed themselves in the Six Classics, woven their teachings together within a single mind, looked upward to high antiquity for their models, and surveyed their own age from that vantage, how could they have won the trust of their contemporaries and transmitted their works to posterity? Only when the great Confucian master appeared were poetry, prose, and the Learning of Principle united by a single thread. Is this not where the definitive assessment lies?

You, sir, live in an age when the Learning of Principle has been made brilliantly clear. In examining scholars at the autumn Provincial Examination, you ask about the poetry and prose of our region’s predecessors and conclude with Master Zhu. Master Zhu served as an official in our region and carried forward the tradition handed down from Lianxi [Zhou Dunyi]. Ah! In this policy question you are testing the students on the Learning of the Way, rather than on poetry and prose: you use poetry and prose to illuminate the Learning of the Way. Though I lack ability, how could I fail to devote my whole mind to answering?

After the poetry of antiquity had disappeared, some several hundred years…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
而淵明出焉五柳先生自謂羲皇上人其
詩何詩也賦歸去而出處之義明朱子書
為晉徵士盖取之不獨以其詩矣保全忠
孝一世偉人竄不為廬阜增光乎自古文
不作之後亦數百年而永叔生焉六一居
士自實昌黎舊物其文何文也作本論而
闢邪之功大朱子録為宋名臣盖取之不
獨以其文矣砥礪名節一世僅見顧不為
廬陵出色乎若夫黄山谷之詩實吾鄉宗
===
派愬雖未敢許其窺靖節之戶牖然而獨
師杜子美則亦不專於詩若况春陵一贊
得吾儒之氣象乎王介甫書山石之辭雖
嘗編之續騷矣柰何創為新法以誤神宗
其事業可知矣能追陶黄二賢之逸駕哉
曾子固之文為吾鄉山斗遇雖未敢擬其
入歐陽之閫奧然而自負劉更生則亦不
專於文者况南豐一集有與諸之家風乎
李泰伯記袁州之學雖嘗列之文鑑矣柰
punctuated:
而淵明出焉。五柳先生自謂羲皇上人，其詩何詩也？賦歸去，而出處之義明。朱子書為晉徵士，盖取之不獨以其詩矣。保全忠孝，一世偉人，竄不為廬阜增光乎？
自古文不作之後，亦數百年而永叔生焉。六一居士自實昌黎舊物，其文何文也？作本論，而闢邪之功大。朱子録為宋名臣，盖取之不獨以其文矣。砥礪名節，一世僅見，顧不為廬陵出色乎？
若夫黄山谷之詩，實吾鄉宗派。愬雖未敢許其窺靖節之戶牖，然而獨師杜子美，則亦不專於詩。若况春陵一贊，得吾儒之氣象乎？
王介甫書山石之辭，雖嘗編之續騷矣，柰何創為新法以誤神宗？其事業可知矣，能追陶黄二賢之逸駕哉？
曾子固之文，為吾鄉山斗。遇雖未敢擬其入歐陽之閫奧，然而自負劉更生，則亦不專於文者。况南豐一集，有與諸之家風乎？
李泰伯記袁州之學，雖嘗列之文鑑矣，柰
translation_en:
…and then Yuanming appeared. The Master of Five Willows called himself a man of the age before Emperor Fuxi. What manner of poetry was his? In composing “Returning Home,” he clarified the right principles of entering office and withdrawing from it. Master Zhu recorded him as a summoned scholar of the Jin dynasty; surely his esteem was not based on poetry alone. Preserving both loyalty and filial devotion, he was a great man of his age. Did he not [?] bring glory to Lufu?
Likewise, several hundred years after ancient-style prose had ceased to flourish, Yongshu was born. The Retired Scholar of the Six Ones claimed [?] to be an heir to Changli. What manner of prose was his? By composing “On Fundamentals,” he made a great contribution to refuting heterodoxy. Master Zhu recorded him among the eminent ministers of the Song; surely his esteem was not based on prose alone. In cultivating an honorable reputation and moral integrity, he had few equals in his age. Did he not bring distinction to Luling?
As for Huang Shangu’s poetry, it indeed founded a school in our region. Though [the transcription is unclear here] I would not presume to grant that he had peered through Jingjie’s doors and windows, he took Du Zimei alone as his master, and thus his concerns extended beyond poetry. How much more so in his “Eulogy on Chunling,” which captured the bearing of our Confucian scholars!
Although Wang Jiefu’s verses inscribed on mountain rocks were once included in the Continuation of the Songs of Chu, why did he institute the New Policies and thereby mislead Emperor Shenzong? From this one can judge his achievements in public life. Could he catch up with the swift carriage of those two worthies, Tao and Huang?
Zeng Zigu’s prose stands as Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper for our region. Though [the transcription is unclear here] I would not presume to say that he had entered the innermost chambers of Ouyang’s art, he prided himself on matching Liu Gengsheng, and thus his concerns, too, extended beyond prose. How much more so when the collected writings of Nanfeng possess the scholarly family tradition of “Yuzhu” [?]!
Although Li Taibo’s account of the school at Yuanzhou was once included in the Mirror of Literature, how could …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
何敢為大言以詆孟子其學識可知安能
踵歐曾二公之芳躅哉執事所舉吾鄉詩
文之名家者如此愚也誦其詩讀其書亦
既陳其槩矣至於所謂吾儒之理學則不
容以不熟講者盖為學而不談理道斷非
執事策諸生之意而亦豈吾儒尚論之達
觀耶盖自濂溪周子分司吾鄉而道學一
倡考亭朱子假守吾鄉而道學再倡濂溪
不由師傳默契道體孔顔之樂親以發二
===
程太極之圖藏以俟百世其高固不可及
矣考亭朱子嗣濂溪之嫡統集諸儒之大
成故學以主敬為實地以窮理為入門其
為說甚長而為教甚明也何者作詩須從
陶靖節門庭來朱子嘗以是教人為詩矣蘇
州非吾鄉也執事之意盖欲推尊靖節而
借朱子以為重耳李性學有云朱子之詩
自陶靖來而理趣過之此其學所以無不
過也文章至歐蘇始是暢朱子嘗以是敎
punctuated:
何敢為大言以詆孟子？其學識可知，安能踵歐、曾二公之芳躅哉！執事所舉吾鄉詩文之名家者如此，愚也誦其詩，讀其書，亦既陳其槩矣。
至於所謂吾儒之理學，則不容以不熟講者。盖為學而不談理道，斷非執事策諸生之意，而亦豈吾儒尚論之達觀耶？盖自濂溪周子分司吾鄉，而道學一倡；考亭朱子假守吾鄉，而道學再倡。濂溪不由師傳，默契道體；孔顔之樂，親以發二程；太極之圖，藏以俟百世。其高固不可及矣！考亭朱子嗣濂溪之嫡統，集諸儒之大成，故學以主敬為實地，以窮理為入門。其為說甚長，而為教甚明也。
何者？「作詩須從陶靖節門庭來」，朱子嘗以是教人為詩矣。蘇州非吾鄉也，執事之意盖欲推尊靖節，而借朱子以為重耳。李性學有云：「朱子之詩自陶靖來，而理趣過之。」此其學所以無不過也。「文章至歐、蘇始是暢」，朱子嘗以是敎
translation_en:
…how could he dare to make grand pronouncements disparaging Mengzi? His learning and discernment are evident from this. How could he follow in the illustrious footsteps of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong? Such are the celebrated poets and prose writers of our province whom you have cited. I, in my humble capacity, have recited their poems and read their writings, and have now presented their broad outlines.
As for what is called our Confucian learning of principle, this must be discussed thoroughly. To pursue learning without discussing principle and the Way certainly cannot be your intention in setting policy questions for us students. Nor could this constitute the comprehensive understanding with which we Confucians assess the worthies of the past. When Master Zhou of Lianxi held a regional appointment in our province, learning of the Way was first promoted here; when Master Zhu of Kaoting provisionally served as prefect in our province, it was promoted anew. Without receiving instruction from a teacher, Lianxi silently apprehended the substance of the Way. He personally awakened the two Cheng brothers to the joy of Kongzi and Yan Hui, and preserved his Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate to await a hundred generations. His lofty attainment was indeed beyond reach! Master Zhu of Kaoting succeeded to Lianxi’s direct line of transmission and brought the learning of the various Confucian masters to its fullest achievement. Thus, in learning, he took maintaining reverent attentiveness as the firm foundation and investigating principle as the point of entry. His exposition was extensive, and his teaching exceedingly clear.
How was this so? “In composing poetry, one must enter through the gateway of Tao Jingjie.” Master Zhu once taught people to compose poetry in these terms. Suzhou was not of our province; your intention, presumably, was to exalt Jingjie and invoke Master Zhu to lend weight to this judgment. Li Xingxue said: “Master Zhu’s poetry derives from Tao Jing[?], yet surpasses it in its savor of principle.” This is why his learning surpassed others in every respect. “Only with Ouyang Xiu and Su Shi did prose attain full fluency.” Master Zhu once used these words to teach…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
人為文矣眉山非吾鄉也執事之意蓋欲
表章歐陽而引朱子以為據耳程端禮有
云朱子大學或問及集中他文皆是用歐
曾體此其學所以無不兼也今自其詩觀
之擬古八首直追漢魏而感春諸賦在屈
宋中吾不知其孰先而孰後也今自其文
言之雲谷一記出脫河東而造辟陳謨在
董賈中吾不知其孰伯而孰仲也他如感
興數篇發盡天人之蘊極於至大而無外
===
入於至小而無内豈可以詩論之哉庸學
二序發明心性之理尼子思之未備補曾
子之未完豈可以文求之哉是以論其詩
文者則曰律之呂之規之矩之不陶不韋
不李不杜不韓不柳不歐不曾也論其道
學者則曰邵至大也周至精也程至正也
朱子極其大盡其精而貫之以正者也嗚
呼此其所以為命世大儒而為古今詩人
文人之折衷也哉仰惟
punctuated: 人為文矣。眉山非吾鄉也，執事之意蓋欲表章歐陽，而引朱子以為據耳。程端禮有云：「朱子《大學或問》及集中他文，皆是用歐曾體。」此其學所以無不兼也。今自其詩觀之，《擬古》八首直追漢魏，而《感春》諸賦在屈宋中，吾不知其孰先而孰後也。今自其文言之，《雲谷》一記出脫河東，而造辟陳謨在董賈中，吾不知其孰伯而孰仲也。他如《感興》數篇，發盡天人之蘊，極於至大而無外，入於至小而無内，豈可以詩論之哉？庸學二序，發明心性之理，尼子思之未備，補曾子之未完，豈可以文求之哉？是以論其詩文者則曰：「律之呂之，規之矩之，不陶不韋，不李不杜，不韓不柳，不歐不曾也。」論其道學者則曰：「邵至大也，周至精也，程至正也。朱子極其大，盡其精，而貫之以正者也。」嗚呼！此其所以為命世大儒，而為古今詩人文人之折衷也哉！仰惟
translation_en:
…to teach people how to write prose. Meishan is not our native place. Your intention, sir, is presumably to honor Ouyang Xiu by invoking Master Zhu as your authority. Cheng Duanli once said: “Master Zhu’s Questions and Answers on the Great Learning, and the other prose pieces in his collected works, all employ the style of Ouyang Xiu and Zeng Gong.” This is why his learning embraces everything. Considering his poetry, his eight poems in Imitation of the Ancients reach directly back to the Han and Wei, while his rhapsodies such as Stirred by Spring stand alongside those of Qu Yuan and Song Yu: I cannot tell which should rank ahead of the other. Considering his prose, his Record of Cloud Valley transcends the manner of Liu Zongyuan of Hedong, while his counsels presented before the sovereign stand alongside those of Dong Zhongshu and Jia Yi: I cannot tell which should rank first and which second. Other works, such as the several poems entitled Reflections, fully disclose the mysteries of Heaven and humanity, extending to the utmost vastness, beyond which nothing lies, and penetrating to the utmost minuteness, within which nothing remains. How could they be judged merely as poetry?

His two prefaces to the Doctrine of the Mean and the Great Learning elucidate the principles of the mind and human nature, [supply?] what Zisi had left insufficiently developed [?], and complete what Zengzi had left unfinished. How could their meaning be sought merely as prose? Thus, those who discuss his poetry and prose say: “He tunes them to the pitch pipes and shapes them with compass and square; he is neither Tao Yuanming nor Wei Yingwu, neither Li Bai nor Du Fu, neither Han Yu nor Liu Zongyuan, neither Ouyang Xiu nor Zeng Gong.” Those who discuss his Learning of the Way say: “Shao Yong attained the utmost breadth; Zhou Dunyi attained the utmost subtlety; the Cheng masters attained the utmost correctness. Master Zhu carried that breadth to its limit, exhausted that subtlety, and united them through correctness.” Ah! Is this not why he is a great Confucian master born to guide his age, and the standard of judgment for poets and prose writers of past and present? Reverently considering…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖朝崇尚理學貢舉以朱子之言取士學校以
朱子之意建官
經筵以朱子之書進講百餘年來教不易道
業不改習人文化成之機寔不外是故凡
秉筆而為締思而作者若能以明義理切
世務為主則今文即古文古文即理學駸
駸乎進諸六經矣尚何有異同之可言哉
讀書錄曰不宗朱氏元非學脹膺有日矣
迂踈之見或可進焉願依末光以卒餘教
===
葉倖
考試官學正孫　批〔以儒生而談天下事歷歷中其肯綮蓋充養之有素者高薦何忝〕
考試官學正顏　批〔宇宙內事吾分內事也士於靜觀之餘強學待問端必有見況兵荒之策又吾人之所隱憂而願聞者子能敷對之詳處分之當是蓋于學識而有之者顧可以凡士目之哉〕
第五問
道出於萬全者得之可以成禦戎之功事
punctuated:
聖朝崇尚理學，貢舉以朱子之言取士，學校以朱子之意建官，經筵以朱子之書進講。百餘年來，教不易道，業不改習，人文化成之機，寔不外是。故凡秉筆而為、締思而作者，若能以明義理、切世務為主，則今文即古文，古文即理學，駸駸乎進諸六經矣。尚何有異同之可言哉？《讀書錄》曰：「不宗朱氏元非學。」脹膺有日矣。迂踈之見，或可進焉。願依末光，以卒餘教。
葉倖
考試官學正孫　批〔以儒生而談天下事，歷歷中其肯綮，蓋充養之有素者，高薦何忝？〕
考試官學正顏　批〔宇宙內事，吾分內事也。士於靜觀之餘，強學待問，端必有見。況兵荒之策，又吾人之所隱憂而願聞者。子能敷對之詳，處分之當，是蓋于學識而有之者，顧可以凡士目之哉？〕
第五問
道出於萬全者，得之可以成禦戎之功；事
translation_en:
…Our sagely dynasty honors the Learning of Principle. In recruitment through the examinations, it selects men according to Master Zhu’s words; in the schools, it establishes offices according to Master Zhu’s intentions; and at the Classics Colloquium, it presents lectures on Master Zhu’s books. For more than a hundred years, teaching has not departed from this Way, nor have studies altered their practices. The means by which literary culture transforms the people truly lie nowhere else. Thus, whenever those who take up the brush and compose through careful thought make clarifying moral principles and addressing worldly affairs their chief concern, contemporary writing becomes ancient writing, and ancient writing becomes the Learning of Principle. They will advance steadily toward the Six Classics. What differences or similarities would then remain to be discussed? The Record of Reading (Dushu lu) says: “Learning that does not take Master Zhu as its authority is no learning at all.” The day of ‘swelling the breast’ will come [?]. Perhaps these unworldly and inadequate views may be offered. I wish to draw upon the last rays of your illumination and thereby complete the instruction still remaining to me.
Ye Xing 葉倖.
Examiner Sun, an Instructor, comments: “Though a Confucian student, he discusses the affairs of the realm and strikes precisely at each crucial point. He is evidently someone who has long cultivated and nourished himself. How could a high recommendation be undeserved?”
Examiner Yan, an Instructor, comments: “The affairs within the universe are affairs within my own responsibility. A scholar who, beyond quiet contemplation, studies diligently and awaits questions must surely have insights. Moreover, policy proposals concerning warfare and famine address matters that secretly trouble us and about which we wish to hear. You have set out your answers in detail and proposed appropriate measures. This surely shows that you possess learning and discernment. How could you be regarded as an ordinary scholar?”
Fifth Question
A course grounded in complete assurance, once grasped, can achieve success in repelling hostile forces; undertakings…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
出於有備者行之可以定禦災之計夫國
衛於兵而用之以禦戎其為功也不易民
資於食而仰之以禦災其為計也不輕苟
徒事遠畧而非萬全之道急近功而無有
備之謀則亦何以圖其功之難以取勝而
定其計之重以無患也哉執事發策以兵
食為問是則政務之要而非藿食者之所
宜慮也然言及之而不言隱也固敢無辭
而對乎傳曰天生五才民並用之誰能去
===
兵兵之設也尚矣易稱弧矢之利以威天
下春秋曰三時務農一時講武詩曰公劉
入耕出戰干戈戚揚四方莫當國之政未
有要於兵者矣我
朝奄有天下文教四敷雖蕞尒蠻陬皆在撫
綏之下然猶謹華夷之辨而以不治治之
迺於沿邊諸鎮也以重兵主以大將而什
伍簡練之法寵異優養之恩至精且備以
戰可克以守可圖真無敵于天下而不戰
punctuated:
出於有備者，行之可以定禦災之計。夫國衛於兵，而用之以禦戎，其為功也不易；民資於食，而仰之以禦災，其為計也不輕。苟徒事遠畧，而非萬全之道；急近功，而無有備之謀，則亦何以圖其功之難以取勝，而定其計之重以無患也哉？執事發策，以兵食為問，是則政務之要，而非藿食者之所宜慮也。然言及之而不言，隱也，固敢無辭而對乎？
傳曰：「天生五才，民並用之，誰能去兵？」兵之設也尚矣。《易》稱：「弧矢之利，以威天下。」《春秋》曰：「三時務農，一時講武。」《詩》曰：「公劉入耕出戰，干戈戚揚，四方莫當。」國之政，未有要於兵者矣。我朝奄有天下，文教四敷，雖蕞尒蠻陬，皆在撫綏之下。然猶謹華夷之辨，而以不治治之。迺於沿邊諸鎮也以重兵，主以大將，而什伍簡練之法、寵異優養之恩，至精且備。以戰可克，以守可圖，真無敵于天下，而不戰
translation_en:
…arising from preparedness, when put into practice, can establish plans for warding off calamity. The state is protected by its troops and uses them to repel foreign foes; achieving this success is no easy matter. The people depend upon food and rely on it to withstand calamity; planning for this is no slight responsibility. If one merely pursues far-reaching strategies without a completely secure approach, or presses for immediate achievements without plans founded on preparedness, how can one accomplish the difficult task of securing victory and settle the weighty matter of planning so as to avert trouble? You, honored examiners, have issued a policy question concerning troops and provisions. These are essentials of government, hardly matters that a humble eater of bean leaves should presume to consider. Yet to remain silent when the subject has been raised would be to conceal what one knows. How, then, could I dare offer no words in reply?
The Commentary says: “Heaven produces the five materials, and the people use them all. Who can dispense with weapons?” The institution of armed forces is ancient indeed. The Book of Changes speaks of “the usefulness of bows and arrows in overawing all under Heaven.” The Spring and Autumn Annals says: “In three seasons, attend to farming; in one season, practice military affairs.” The Book of Odes says: “Gong Liu farmed at home and fought abroad; with shields, spears, and battle-axes, none in the four quarters could withstand him.” [?] Among the affairs of state, none is more essential than military preparedness. Our dynasty possesses all under Heaven, and its civilizing teachings spread in every direction. Even the tiniest remote settlements of the southern peoples come under its pacification and care. Yet it remains scrupulous about the distinction between the Chinese and the non-Chinese, governing the latter through nonintervention. Thus, at the various frontier garrisons, it has stationed substantial forces [?] under the command of senior generals. Its methods for selecting and training men in units of tens and fives, and its gracious provision of special favor and generous support, are most refined and complete. In battle they can prevail; in defense they can devise effective plans. Truly they are without equal under Heaven and, without fighting…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
以屈人者矣夫何須者獨石永寧等處醜
虜輒肆封豕之毒長驅內寇若蹈無人之
境而張猖獗之勢矣至厪
當宁宵旰之憂命將出師警牒紛至則亦何取
于邊之將與兵哉古之人李牧之守鴈門
趙充國之屯九郡楊業之知代州李元諒
之節度隴右固有匈奴不敢近者矣固有
單于輒自引去者矣固有却契丹而拒西
戎者矣然吏考其績李牧輩固以專制之
===
將而統素練之兵者曰饗士卒以率其必
勝之氣各習長技以厲其不可敗之勇以
逸制動其取勝宜也非幸也為今之計誠
使邊將皆就其如古人者務愛兵以同其
甘苦推心以係其安危尺籍之士不困於
私役而有持戟之實月入之糧不費於侵
漁而有挾纊之愛明其功罪之差均其勞
逸之節過于搯尅者必懲勤于捍衛者必
賞則感之有仁結之有義人樂為用而致
punctuated:
以屈人者矣。夫何須者，獨石、永寧等處，醜虜輒肆封豕之毒，長驅內寇，若蹈無人之境，而張猖獗之勢矣。至厪當宁宵旰之憂，命將出師，警牒紛至，則亦何取于邊之將與兵哉？古之人，李牧之守鴈門，趙充國之屯九郡，楊業之知代州，李元諒之節度隴右，固有匈奴不敢近者矣，固有單于輒自引去者矣，固有却契丹而拒西戎者矣。然吏考其績，李牧輩固以專制之將，而統素練之兵者。曰：饗士卒以率其必勝之氣，各習長技以厲其不可敗之勇，以逸制動，其取勝宜也，非幸也。

為今之計，誠使邊將皆就其如古人者，務愛兵以同其甘苦，推心以係其安危，尺籍之士不困於私役而有持戟之實，月入之糧不費於侵漁而有挾纊之愛，明其功罪之差，均其勞逸之節，過于搯尅者必懲，勤于捍衛者必賞，則感之有仁，結之有義，人樂為用而致
translation_en:
…thereby subduing others. Why, then, recently [?], have the vile raiders at Dushi, Yongning, and other places repeatedly unleashed their ferocity like monstrous boars, driving deep into our territory as though entering an unpeopled land and flaunting their rampant power? They have even burdened His Majesty with anxiety from before dawn until late at night. Generals have been appointed and troops dispatched, while urgent reports arrive in profusion. What use, then, are the generals and soldiers on the frontier?

Among men of old were Li Mu, who defended Yanmen; Zhao Chongguo, who stationed troops in the nine commanderies [?]; Yang Ye, who served as Prefect of Daizhou; and Li Yuanliang, who served as Military Commissioner of Longyou. There were indeed those whom the Xiongnu dared not approach, those before whom the chanyu would withdraw of his own accord, and those who repelled the Khitan and resisted the western Rong. Yet, examining their achievements [?], Li Mu and his peers were generals vested with independent authority who commanded thoroughly trained troops. It is said: they feasted their soldiers to inspire a spirit certain of victory, and had each practice his particular skills to sharpen his indomitable courage. Meeting the enemy’s movements with rested forces, they deserved their victories; these were no mere strokes of luck.

For our present policy, if we truly ensured that all frontier generals followed the example of the ancients, devoted themselves to caring for their soldiers and sharing their hardships and comforts, and gave them their wholehearted concern, binding themselves to their safety and peril; if soldiers on the military rolls were not burdened with private service but actually performed their duties under arms, and their monthly grain provisions were not squandered through embezzlement, so that they felt the warmth of care as though clothed in silk floss; if distinctions between merit and guilt were made clear, and periods of toil and rest fairly apportioned; and if those guilty of excessive exactions were invariably punished and those diligent in defense invariably rewarded—then benevolence would move the soldiers and righteousness bind them. Men would gladly serve and offer…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
效死之誠矣由是取之於見伍則必有以
引弩箭鏃自厲者矣不必募市井之無賴
用之於土兵則必有以心膽膂力自奮者
矣不必召他郡之白籍尚何邊警之足慮
乎萬全之道恐無以過此傳曰人情一日
不得食則飢食之當先也尚矣史曰王者
以民為天民以食為天知天之天者王事
有成管子曰倉廩實而知禮節衣食足而
知榮辱賈誼曰貯蓄天下之大命國之政
===
又未有大於食者我
朝統馭中外利用厚生凡我蒸民已享粒食
之休然猶經世之長慮而先事圖之郡縣
設勸農之職官府有儲備之倉貴則糶之
賤則糴之誠制治于未危而獲聚人之本
矣夫何頃者沴氣侵加飢饉荐至民不聊
生將有菜色而懷土以待于來者矣至厪
當宁軫念之勞遣官分賑使牒相望則亦何取
於郡縣之儲畜哉古之人知張詠之知益
punctuated:
效死之誠矣。由是取之於見伍，則必有以引弩箭鏃自厲者矣，不必募市井之無賴；用之於土兵，則必有以心膽膂力自奮者矣，不必召他郡之白籍。尚何邊警之足慮乎？萬全之道，恐無以過此。
傳曰：「人情一日不得食則飢，食之當先也尚矣。」史曰：「王者以民為天，民以食為天，知天之天者，王事有成。」管子曰：「倉廩實而知禮節，衣食足而知榮辱。」賈誼曰：「貯蓄，天下之大命。」國之政，又未有大於食者。我朝統馭中外，利用厚生，凡我蒸民已享粒食之休。然猶經世之長慮，而先事圖之：郡縣設勸農之職，官府有儲備之倉，貴則糶之，賤則糴之，誠制治于未危而獲聚人之本矣。夫何頃者沴氣侵加，飢饉荐至，民不聊生，將有菜色而懷土以待于來者矣。至厪當宁軫念之勞，遣官分賑，使牒相望，則亦何取於郡縣之儲畜哉？古之人知張詠之知益
translation_en:
…the sincerity of their resolve to serve unto death. If men are then selected from the existing ranks, there will surely be those who steel themselves by drawing crossbows and wielding arrowheads [?]; there will be no need to recruit the wastrels of the marketplaces. If local troops are employed, there will surely be those who exert themselves with courage and bodily strength; there will be no need to summon men without regular military registration from other prefectures. What frontier alarms would then warrant concern? For a wholly secure course, I fear nothing could surpass this.
A transmitted text says: “Human beings grow hungry if they go a single day without food. That food should take precedence has long been recognized.” A historical work says: “The ruler regards the people as Heaven, and the people regard food as Heaven. One who understands the Heaven of his Heaven will succeed in the affairs of kingship.” The Guanzi says: “When granaries are full, people understand ritual and propriety; when clothing and food are sufficient, they understand honor and disgrace.” Jia Yi says: “Stored reserves are the great lifeline of the realm.” In governing a state, moreover, nothing is more important than food. Our dynasty governs both the inner and outer domains, promoting useful resources and enriching the people's livelihood. All our people have already enjoyed the blessing of grain to eat. Yet, with the long view required to govern the world, the dynasty has planned ahead: prefectures and counties have posts charged with encouraging agriculture, and government offices have granaries for reserves. When prices are high, they sell grain; when prices are low, they buy it. This truly establishes order before danger arises and secures the foundation for keeping the people together. Why, then, have baleful influences recently assailed us and famines repeatedly occurred, leaving the people unable to sustain themselves? They are on the verge of taking on the pallor of hunger, clinging to their native soil as they await what is to come [?]. Matters have reached the point of burdening His Majesty with anxious concern: officials are dispatched to distribute relief, and the documents borne by envoys follow one another in an unbroken stream. What use, then, have the reserves of the prefectures and counties served? Among men of former times, we know of Zhang Yong's administration of Yi…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
州范純仁之知襄邑富弼之知青州蔡齊
之帥京東固有按田稅以計口收息者矣
固有籍賈舟以全糴者矣固有出公廩而
弛鹽禁者矣然夷考其政乃蘿一時之宜
而為通變之法者藏富于民以免流離之
苦佚道使衆以取活全之頋因利而利其
成功宜也非幸也誠使郡縣皆去其不如
古人者貴五穀而賤金玉勸劭有官而謹
其歛散之法奇羸有時而嚴其出納之禁
===
財不匱於侵年力不竭於征索取之無窮
九年耕必有三年之蓄用之必節一人織
乃無十人之衣則制節謹度量入為出國
有大計而無捐瘠之憂矣由是用之於禮
義則仰足事俯足育而順治矣用之於戰
勝則居積倉行褁糧而無敵矣尚何荒歉
之足患哉有備之法恐無以過此然此皆
特愚生補偏救弊之說焉至其要固未之
及也孔子曰為政在人朱子曰其本不在
punctuated: 州、范純仁之知襄邑、富弼之知青州、蔡齊之帥京東，固有按田稅以計口收息者矣，固有籍賈舟以全糴者矣，固有出公廩而弛鹽禁者矣。然夷考其政，乃蘿一時之宜而為通變之法者。藏富于民，以免流離之苦；佚道使衆，以取活全之頋；因利而利，其成功宜也，非幸也。誠使郡縣皆去其不如古人者，貴五穀而賤金玉，勸劭有官而謹其歛散之法，奇羸有時而嚴其出納之禁，財不匱於侵年，力不竭於征索，取之無窮，九年耕必有三年之蓄；用之必節，一人織乃無十人之衣。則制節謹度，量入為出，國有大計而無捐瘠之憂矣。由是用之於禮義，則仰足事、俯足育而順治矣；用之於戰勝，則居積倉、行褁糧而無敵矣。尚何荒歉之足患哉？有備之法，恐無以過此。然此皆特愚生補偏救弊之說焉，至其要，固未之及也。孔子曰：「為政在人。」朱子曰：「其本不在
translation_en:
…zhou, Fan Chunren’s service as magistrate of Xiangyi, Fu Bi’s service as prefect of Qingzhou, and Cai Qi’s command of Jingdong. Among them were those who assessed interest payments according to land taxes and household population [?], those who registered merchant vessels to secure grain purchases, and those who opened public granaries and relaxed restrictions on salt. Yet, upon an evenhanded examination of their administration, these were methods adapted to changing circumstances in accordance with the needs of the time [?]. They stored wealth among the people to spare them the suffering of displacement; they employed the populace in ways conducive to their well-being, seeking to preserve their lives [?]; and they benefited the people through the advantages already available to them. Their success was deserved, not a matter of luck.

If prefectures and counties truly eliminated everything in which they fell short of the ancients, valued the five grains above gold and jade, appointed officials to encourage agriculture and carefully regulated the collection and distribution of grain, accumulated surpluses at the appropriate times [?] and strictly enforced rules governing receipts and disbursements, then resources would not run short in years of poor harvest [?], nor would the people’s strength be exhausted by levies and exactions. Resources could be drawn upon without exhaustion: nine years of cultivation would assuredly provide three years of reserves. Expenditure must be restrained: what one person weaves cannot clothe ten. Thus, by regulating expenditure, carefully observing limits, and making outlays commensurate with revenues, the state would have a comprehensive fiscal plan and no anxiety over people abandoned to starvation.

If these resources were then devoted to ritual and righteousness, the people would have enough to serve their parents above and nurture their children below, and there would be orderly government. If devoted to victory in war, grain would be stored in granaries when troops were at rest and carried as provisions when they marched, and they would be invincible. What further cause would there be to fear crop failures and famine? I doubt that any method of preparedness could surpass this.

Yet these are merely this foolish student’s proposals for correcting imbalances and remedying abuses; I have not yet reached the essential point. Confucius said, “The practice of government depends on people.” Master Zhu said, “Its foundation does not lie in…”

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎威强而在乎德業其備不在乎邊境而
在乎
朝廷其具不在乎兵食而在乎紀綱此則司
國計者所當加之意也
punctuated: 乎威强，而在乎德業；其備不在乎邊境，而在乎朝廷；其具不在乎兵食，而在乎紀綱。」此則司國計者所當加之意也。
translation_en: …in coercive strength, but in virtue and accomplishment; its defenses lie not at the frontiers, but at the imperial court; its means lie not in troops and provisions, but in institutional order and discipline.” This, then, is what those responsible for planning the affairs of state ought to give particular attention to.

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
正德丙子秋八月式維鄉試取
士之期江西巡按監察御史大
潤率藩臬諸臣循故事舉行惟
慎事既訖合中式士與文之可
式暨諸執事者氏名貫址之異
裒刻成録將以上之
===
天府而昭示四方𦍒濫竽文柄僭
序諸末曰天生賢才為世道計
國家培植養育以致重焉者實惟
玆賴而士之所以種學績文以
自見於世者亦匪為身計也然
或生非其時培之淺而涵養者
歉焉其發之必索然萎薾矣子
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

正德丙子秋八月，式維鄉試取士之期。江西巡按監察御史大潤率藩臬諸臣，循故事舉行，惟慎。事既訖，合中式士與文之可式，暨諸執事者氏名貫址之異，裒刻成録，將以上之天府，而昭示四方。𦍒濫竽文柄，僭序諸末曰：「天生賢才，為世道計。國家培植養育，以致重焉者，實惟玆賴。而士之所以種學績文，以自見於世者，亦匪為身計也。然或生非其時，培之淺而涵養者歉焉，其發之必索然萎薾矣。子
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the eighth month of autumn in the bingzi year of Zhengde [1516], the appointed time arrived for selecting scholars through the Provincial Examination. Darun, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor for Jiangxi, led the officials of the Provincial Administration and Surveillance Commissions in conducting it according to established precedent, exercising utmost care. When the work was finished, the successful candidates, writings worthy to serve as models, and the respective names, native places, and residences of the officials who had performed the various duties were compiled and block-printed as a record. This was to be submitted to the imperial repository and made known throughout the realm. Having unworthily held responsibility for judging the writing [?], I presume to append this postface:

“Heaven brings forth worthy and talented men for the sake of the moral order of the world. The state cultivates and nurtures them, attaching great importance to them, because it truly depends upon them. Scholars likewise cultivate learning and develop their literary accomplishments to make themselves known in the world, not merely for their own advantage. Yet if they are born at an inopportune time, receive only shallow cultivation, and lack adequate nurture, their development will inevitably be feeble and withered. You …

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸士躬逢
文明之運居之有所肄之有業□
漸被于道化已非一日譬諸材
之產於沃壤也飽之以雨露禁
之以樵牧而又積之以歲月宜
其升也凌霄聳壑昂藏而峭挺
也歟即今日見於場屋者觀之
===
其藻思秀發傑然者形其特煇
然者吐其和淵然者露其英令
人心悸目眩而嘆曰懿哉其善
鳴乎茲雖秀禀自天而寔關於
熙朝之培育取而錄之不有裨於
世用矣乎雖然言華也行實也
資世用者不于其華于其實乎
punctuated: 諸士躬逢文明之運，居之有所，肄之有業，□漸被于道化，已非一日。譬諸材之產於沃壤也，飽之以雨露，禁之以樵牧，而又積之以歲月，宜其升也凌霄聳壑，昂藏而峭挺也歟！即今日見於場屋者觀之，其藻思秀發，傑然者形其特，煇然者吐其和，淵然者露其英，令人心悸目眩而嘆曰：「懿哉，其善鳴乎！」茲雖秀禀自天，而寔關於熙朝之培育。取而錄之，不有裨於世用矣乎？雖然，言華也，行實也，資世用者，不于其華，于其實乎？
translation_en: …You scholars have personally encountered an age of flourishing civilization. You have places in which to reside and studies to pursue; □ [?] you have long been gradually imbued with the transforming influence of the Way. You are like timber trees growing in fertile soil, nourished abundantly by rain and dew, protected from woodcutting and grazing, and given years to mature. Surely they should rise into the clouds and tower above the ravines, imposing, lofty, and upright! Judging by what you have displayed in the examination halls today, your literary imagination blossoms in elegance: the outstanding reveal their distinction, the radiant express their harmony, and the profound disclose their excellence. They set the heart trembling and dazzle the eyes, prompting the exclamation: “How admirable! How beautifully they give voice!” Although this exceptional endowment comes from Heaven, it is indeed bound up with the nurturing care of our flourishing dynasty. Would selecting and recording these writings not contribute to practical service in the world? Nevertheless, words are the blossom, while conduct is the fruit. Does what serves the world lie not in the blossom, but in the fruit?

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
諸士其知之乎矧江西為東南
大藩名卿偉士盛自前代固無
暇遠舉入我
朝来其著於紀錄有曰秉節堅貞
媲美文忠者有曰慥慥君子儒
林之特者有曰危言峻行名儒
風致者有曰不在温飽汲汲行
===
道者斯皆瑰瑋不群無負於
邦家而有裨於世道子諸士既知
之矣自今將歷華陟要毋庸嚮
慕於他方而借則於前代惟鄉
先進而求上之俾〔哇〕然者如層
巖絶巘邪徑無〔由〕〔進〕煇然者如
青天白日陰霾無容掩淵然者
punctuated: 諸士其知之乎？矧江西為東南大藩，名卿偉士盛自前代，固無暇遠舉。入我朝来，其著於紀錄，有曰「秉節堅貞，媲美文忠」者，有曰「慥慥君子，儒林之特」者，有曰「危言峻行，名儒風致」者，有曰「不在温飽，汲汲行道」者。斯皆瑰瑋不群，無負於邦家，而有裨於世道。子諸士既知之矣，自今將歷華陟要，毋庸嚮慕於他方，而借則於前代，惟鄉先進而求上之。俾〔哇〕然者如層巖絶巘，邪徑無〔由〕〔進〕；煇然者如青天白日，陰霾無容掩；淵然者
translation_en: Do you gentlemen understand this? Moreover, Jiangxi is a great province of the southeast, where eminent ministers and outstanding scholars have flourished since earlier dynasties; there is certainly no time to enumerate examples from the distant past. Since the beginning of our dynasty, among those celebrated in the records are men described as “steadfast and resolute in maintaining their integrity, rivalling Wenzhong”; as “earnest gentlemen, outstanding among the community of scholars”; as “upright in speech and lofty in conduct, possessing the bearing of renowned Confucian scholars”; and as “unconcerned with warmth and a full stomach, intent upon putting the Way into practice.” All these were extraordinary men, surpassing the common run, who did not fail their country and contributed to the moral order of the world. You gentlemen already know this. Henceforth, as you advance through illustrious posts and rise to important offices, you need not look admiringly toward other regions or borrow models from earlier dynasties. Look only to your own region’s predecessors and seek to surpass them. Let those who are [‘croaking’ [?], in the small annotation] resemble tiered cliffs and towering peaks, offering no crooked path by which to advance; let those who shine brilliantly resemble the blue sky and bright sun, which no gloomy haze can obscure; and let those who are profound…

title: 正德十一年江西鄉試錄
text:
如澄潭巨澤泥滓無能濁不亦
有裨於我
朝休明之治而荅累世培育之恩
也哉〔芝〕與子諸士有一日之雅
喜斯録之有成也於是乎書以
曷之
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正
孫□謹序
punctuated:
如澄潭巨澤，泥滓無能濁，不亦有裨於我朝休明之治，而荅累世培育之恩也哉？〔芝〕與子諸士有一日之雅，喜斯録之有成也，於是乎書以曷之。
山東東昌府高唐州儒學學正孫□謹序。
translation_en:
…like clear pools and great lakes that no mud or sediment can sully. Would this not contribute to the splendid governance of our dynasty and repay its gracious nurturing over successive generations? I, Zhi [?], have had the pleasure of a brief acquaintance with you gentlemen. Delighted that this record has been completed, I therefore write to commemorate it [?].
Preface respectfully composed by Sun □, Instructor of the Confucian School of Gaotang Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong.
